general_translation: Or something,  Any... (with question words), No matter (who)
formation: Noun  + でも + Suggestionだれでも - Anyoneなんでも - Anythingどこでも - Anywhereいつでも - Anytime
casual_structure: Noun  + でも + Suggestionだれでも - Anyoneなんでも - Anythingどこでも - Anywhereいつでも - Anytime
explanation: A word used for expressing undetermined possibilities or choices.

example_sentences.japanese: どこでもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Anywhere is good.

example_sentences.japanese: お茶でも飲みましょうか。
example_sentences.english: Shall we drink some tea, or something?

example_sentences.japanese: 大丈夫だよ、お前でも出来るよ。
example_sentences.english: It's okay, even someone like you can do it.

example_sentences.japanese: この簡単な漢字はだれでも分かるよ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone knows this easy kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 「明日はどこに行きたい？」「どこでもいいよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Where do you want to go tomorrow?' 'Anywhere is fine.'

example_sentences.japanese: お前は本当に何でも食べるね。
example_sentences.english: You really do eat anything.

example_sentences.japanese: いつでも電話してね。
example_sentences.english: Please, call me anytime.

example_sentences.japanese: いつでも家に来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please come to my house anytime.

example_sentences.japanese: いつでも電話に出るから。
example_sentences.english: I will answer the phone anytime, so... (please don't hesitate to call me)

example_sentences.japanese: いつでも洗濯できますよ。
example_sentences.english: I can do laundry anytime.

example_sentences.japanese: お茶でもどう？
example_sentences.english: How about tea or something?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日のパーティーでは、いつでもダンスをしていいんだよ。
example_sentences.english: At today's party, you can dance anytime you like.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝、一緒に散歩でもしませんか。
example_sentences.english: Won't you go on a walk with me or something tomorrow morning?

example_sentences.japanese: どこでもいいんです。
example_sentences.english: Anywhere is fine.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末は映画でも見に行きませんか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't we go watch a movie or something this weekend?

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、お茶がなかった。水でも大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: Sorry, I didn't have any tea. Is water or something alright?

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーに砂糖でも、入れませんか。
example_sentences.english: Won't you put sugar or something in your coffee?

example_sentences.japanese: 誰でも彼の名前を知っています。
example_sentences.english: Everyone knows his name.

example_sentences.japanese: スプーンでも缶詰が開く。
example_sentences.english: A can will open, even with a spoon.

formation: Verb［stem］+ やすい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ やすい
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ やすい + です
explanation: A word that is often used to highlight the simplicity of actions.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキはつくりやすい。
example_sentences.english: Cake is easy to make.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は食べやすいサイズにステーキを切る。
example_sentences.english: I will cut the steak into a size that's easy to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画にはフリガナがついているから読みやすいです。
example_sentences.english: Since this manga has furigana included, it's easy to read.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先輩は怒りやすいからめんどくさい。
example_sentences.english: That senpai is prone to getting angry, so he's annoying.

example_sentences.japanese: カスミちゃんは泣きやすいから優しくしてね。
example_sentences.english: Kasumi is likely to cry, so please be nice to her. (Kasumi cries easily)

example_sentences.japanese: この魚はたべやすいです。
example_sentences.english: This fish is easy to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の練習はしやすかった。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday's practice was easy to do.

example_sentences.japanese: この白い服は、よごれやすいです。
example_sentences.english: These white clothes are easy to get dirty.

example_sentences.japanese: この音楽が好きだから、おどりやすい。
example_sentences.english: Because I like this music, it is easy to dance.

example_sentences.japanese: この箸はつかいやすい。
example_sentences.english: These chopsticks are easy to use.

example_sentences.japanese: その動物園は近いからいきやすい。
example_sentences.english: That zoo is easy to go to, because it is close.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店員さんとははなしやすかった。
example_sentences.english: That clerk over there was easy to talk to.

example_sentences.japanese: この薬はのみやすい。
example_sentences.english: This medicine is easy to take.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪が降ったので、すべりやすくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Since it snowed, it has become easy to slip.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京から大阪へは電車がいきやすいですよ。
example_sentences.english: It is easy to go from Tokyo to Osaka by train!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の宿題は少なかったので、しやすかった。
example_sentences.english: Since there was only a little homework today, it was easy to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日やすいゲームを買った。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I bought a cheap game. (安（やす）い meaning cheap, not 易（やす）い meaning easy)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は簡単なゲームが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I enjoy easy games. (易（やす）い would not work here, as it is not usually used without a verb)

formation: Verb［stem］+ にくい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ にくい
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ にくい + です
explanation: An expression that focuses on the difficulty created by the speaker's lack of skill, or personal feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 甘くないケーキは、たべにくいです。
example_sentences.english: Cakes that aren't sweet are hard to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: この駐車場は狭いから止めにくい。
example_sentences.english: This parking lot is very cramped, so it is difficult to park.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は具合が悪いから呼吸がしにくい。
example_sentences.english: Because I am not feeling well today, it is hard to breathe.

example_sentences.japanese: 私には英語の「Literally」という単語がとても言いにくい。
example_sentences.english: For me, the English word 'literally' is very hard to say. (Hard due to the individual's skill level)

example_sentences.japanese: お前には本当に言いづらいけど、お前のギターを壊した。ごめん。
example_sentences.english: This is very difficult for me to say to you, but I broke your guitar. I'm sorry. (Hard because the speaker knows that telling the listener will cause a negative response)

example_sentences.japanese: アフリカにはいきにくいです。
example_sentences.english: It is hard to go to Africa.

example_sentences.japanese: 怖いことはしにくいです。
example_sentences.english: It is difficult to do scary things.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人とははなしにくいです。
example_sentences.english: That person is hard to talk to. (Unapproachable)

example_sentences.japanese: このコップ、形が変だからのみにくい。
example_sentences.english: Because this cup has a strange shape, it is hard to drink out of.

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい漢字はおぼえにくい。
example_sentences.english: Tricky Kanji are difficult to memorize.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社ははたらきにくいけど、働かなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: It is difficult to work at this company, but I have to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語ははなしにくいですが、頑張ります。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is difficult to speak, but I will try my best.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ慣れていないからやりにくい。
example_sentences.english: Because I am still not used to it, it is hard to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 緊張して声がでにくい。
example_sentences.english: I'm nervous, making it hard to talk. (Difficult to produce my voice)

example_sentences.japanese: 性格が元彼女に似ているから、はなしにくい。
example_sentences.english: Her personality is like my ex's, so it is hard to talk with her. (Unapproachable)

example_sentences.japanese: 遠いから日本にはいきにくいけど、行くつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Because it is far Japan is difficult to get to, but I intend to go.

general_translation: Hard to, Tough to, Painful to, Difficult to
formation: Verb［stem］+ づらい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ づらい
explanation: A suffix used to indicate that something is difficult or tough to do due to psychological, emotional, or physical reasons.

example_sentences.japanese: 道が狭くてはしりづらい。
example_sentences.english: The road is narrow and tough to run on.

example_sentences.japanese: こたえづらい事を聞かれた。
example_sentences.english: I was asked something that was tough to answer.

example_sentences.japanese: 後ろの席からはみえづらい。
example_sentences.english: It's tough to see from the back seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯が痛くてしゃべりづらいです。
example_sentences.english: My tooth hurts so it's tough to talk.

example_sentences.japanese: タピオカが大きすぎてすいづらい。
example_sentences.english: The tapioca is too big so it's tough to suck.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は、単語が多くておぼえづらい。
example_sentences.english: Japanese has a lot of words so it's tough to memorize.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏：「ちょっとききづらいんだけど・・・。」彼女：「うん。なに？」
example_sentences.english: Boyfriend: 'It's a little tough to ask, but...'Girlfriend: 'Yeah? What is it?'

example_sentences.japanese: その結果になるとはかんがえづらいな。
example_sentences.english: It's tough to think that would be the result.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日学校を休んだから、いきづらい。
example_sentences.english: I was absent from school yesterday, so it's tough to go (today).

example_sentences.japanese: カップが小さいので、のみづらいです。
example_sentences.english: The cup is small, so it's tough to drink from.

example_sentences.japanese: 母：「ケーキが可愛すぎて、ろうそくをさしづらいわ。」娘：「ほんとに！」
example_sentences.english: Mom: 'The cake is too cute, so it's tough to stick the candles in.'Daughter: 'I know!'

example_sentences.japanese: いいづらいことも、何でも話せる関係です。
example_sentences.english: We have a relationship where we can talk about anything, even things that are tough to say.

example_sentences.japanese: この服はきづらい。
example_sentences.english: These clothes are tough to wear.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹：「あのスニーカーまだ乾いてないの？」姉：「そう。かわきづらいのよね。」
example_sentences.english: Younger sister: 'That sneaker isn't dry yet?'Older sister: 'Yeah. It's tough to dry.'

example_sentences.japanese: ユリ：「シンヤと付き合ったよ！」アキ：「私も好きだったから、よろこびづらいよ。」
example_sentences.english: Yuri: I'm going out with Shinya!'Aki: 'I liked him too, so it's tough to be happy for you.'

example_sentences.japanese: まだ完全に治ってないから、歩きづらい。
example_sentences.english: I haven't fully recovered yet, so it is hard to walk.

example_sentences.japanese: この車のハンドルは重いから、運転しづらい。
example_sentences.english: The steering wheel of this car is heavy, so it is hard to drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 職場の人たちと仲が悪いから、ちょっと辛い。
example_sentences.english: I don't get along with the people at work, so it is a little tough.

general_translation: Gradually, Little by little, Step by step
formation: だんだん + （と） + Phrase
casual_structure: だんだん + （と） + Phrase
explanation: A phrase showing that (A) is gradually increasing, step by step.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が後輩に話している：「大丈夫、だんだん上手になるよ。」
example_sentences.english: A senpai speaking to their kouhai: 'Don't worry, you will become better gradually.'

example_sentences.japanese: １２月になってからだんだん寒くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: Since December, it has gotten colder steadily.

example_sentences.japanese: だんだん仕事の環境に慣れてきた。
example_sentences.english: I have steadily gotten used to work's environment.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はだんだんと暑くなってきたね。
example_sentences.english: Recently it has progressively gotten hotter, right? (Slow progression)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が話している：「秋になったからこれからだんだん寒くなるよね。」
example_sentences.english: Friends talking: 'Autumn is here, so it will gradually become cooler, don't you think?'

example_sentences.japanese: 英語の教師が生徒の親と話している、教師：「娘さんはだんだん英語がうまくなってきました。」
example_sentences.english: An English teacher talking with a student's parents, teacher: 'Your daughter has been gradually improving in speaking English.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が話している：「だんだんとあのやつの事が嫌いになってきていて、今は避けるようにしている。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I gradually came to dislike that guy, and now I do my best to avoid him.'

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが子供と話している：「あなたはだんだんおかしを食べたくなくなる。」
example_sentences.english: A mother speaking with a child: 'You will gradually lose interest in sweets.'

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル：「夜になったら、雨がだんだん強くなる。」
example_sentences.english: Light novel: 'With the fall of night, the rain will gradually get strong.'

example_sentences.japanese: 近所の人が話している：「来週からだんだん暖かくなるってニュースで言っていましたよ。」
example_sentences.english: Neighbors talking: 'The news said that it will gradually get warmer from next week.'

example_sentences.japanese: 近所の人が話している：「ともちゃんは最近、だんだん大きくなっているでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Neighbors talking: 'Recently, Tomo-chan is gradually getting bigger, right?'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が話している：「このアニメはだんだんつまらなくなるって友達が言ってた。」
example_sentences.english: Friends talking: 'My friend was saying that this anime gets boring gradually.'

example_sentences.japanese: 近所の人が話している：「もう４月だね、これからだんだん暖かくなるね。」
example_sentences.english: Neighbors talking: 'It's already April isn't it, from now it will gradually get warmer.'

example_sentences.japanese: 近所の人が話している：「これからだんだん寒くなるから、ジャケットを買う。」
example_sentences.english: Neighbors talking: 'Because it is going to get colder gradually from now, I will buy a jacket.'

example_sentences.japanese: インタビューした学生：「高校生になってから、だんだんと授業が難しくなったので毎日勉強をしています。」
example_sentences.english: Interviewed student: 'Ever since becoming a high school student, classes are gradually getting harder, so I study everyday.'

example_sentences.japanese: だんだん雨が降ってきた。
example_sentences.english: It is starting to rain. (Slow progression, does not imply great speed or severity)

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん雨が降ってきた。
example_sentences.english: It is starting to rain. (Rapid progression, may imply great speed and/or severity)

general_translation: Progressively, Rapidly increasing, More and more
formation: どんどん + （と） + Phrase
casual_structure: どんどん + （と） + Phrase
explanation: A word which stems from loud repetitive noises, to show that (A) is rapidly progressing.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん暑くなる。
example_sentences.english: It will rapidly get warmer and warmer.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が出来てからどんどんお金が減っていく。
example_sentences.english: Since I got a girlfriend, my cash has been rapidly decreasing.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん頼んでね！
example_sentences.english: Quickly order! (Literally means 'more and more' in a sentence like this, with the nuance of 'don't hold back, order in rapid succession')

example_sentences.japanese: バスの運転手がどんどんと減っている。
example_sentences.english: The number of bus drivers is rapidly decreasing.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん日本語が上手になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to get better and better at Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の人口がどんどん減る。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese population will rapidly decrease.

example_sentences.japanese: 音がどんどん大きくなる。
example_sentences.english: The sound will get louder and louder.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がどんどん綺麗になる。
example_sentences.english: She will become prettier and prettier (quickly).

example_sentences.japanese: 川がどんどん広くなる。
example_sentences.english: The river will rapidly get wider. (steadily)

example_sentences.japanese: 車の運転免許を取ったので、どんどん車に乗って出かけましょう。
example_sentences.english: Since I got my license, let's go out by car more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週から、彼の意見がどんどん増えた。
example_sentences.english: (The number of) his opinions have rapidly increased starting from last week.

example_sentences.japanese: これから、どんどん寒くなるから、温かい服を買わなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: From now on, it will get rapidly colder, so I have to buy warm clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品はこれからどんどん安くなるから、買うのを待ちましょう。
example_sentences.english: These goods will rapidly get cheaper from here on, so let's wait to buy them.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん料理を頼みましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's rapidly order food.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日筋トレをしたり、プロテインを飲んだりして、どんどんマッチョになる。
example_sentences.english: Every day I have been doing things like working out and drinking protein, so I will progressively become more macho.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日ピアノを練習しているから、だんだんピアノが上手になってきた。
example_sentences.english: Because I practice the piano everyday, I have steadily gotten better at playing. (Slow progression)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日ピアノを練習しているから、どんどんピアノが上手になってきた。
example_sentences.english: Because I practice the piano everyday, I have rapidly gotten better at playing. (Rapid progression)

formation: Pronoun + ら
casual_structure: Pronoun + ら
explanation: A casual suffix which is used to identify groups of (A), by stating (A) and etc.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは十分に勉強をしたから、試験が簡単だった。
example_sentences.english: They studied sufficiently, so the test was easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは日本語を勉強しにきた。
example_sentences.english: They came in order to study Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: お前ら、アニメを見ないの？
example_sentences.english: You guys don't watch anime?

example_sentences.japanese: これらを捨ててください。
example_sentences.english: Could you please toss these?

example_sentences.japanese: それらの畳はいい匂いがしている。
example_sentences.english: Those tatami mats smell good.

example_sentences.japanese: 君ら池に入るつもり？
example_sentences.english: Do you all intend to go swimming in the pond?

example_sentences.japanese: 奴らはプロだ。
example_sentences.english: They are pros.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕らは全員日本に留学したことがあります。
example_sentences.english: We have all studied abroad in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がこれらは絶対にテストに出ると言っていた。
example_sentences.english: The teacher said that these will absolutely show up on the test.

example_sentences.japanese: それらは後でします。
example_sentences.english: I will do those later.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは来週日本へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: They will go to Japan next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺ら？やりたくないよ。
example_sentences.english: Us? We don't want to do that.

example_sentences.japanese: そいつらが犯人です。
example_sentences.english: They are the culprits.

example_sentences.japanese: お前らが喧嘩をしていた間に、俺らは逃げたぞ。
example_sentences.english: We fled, while you guys were fighting.

general_translation: To ~ and go, To go on, To start
formation: Verb［て］+ いく
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ いく
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ いきます
explanation: A phrase used when a specific event will go on to occur, or continue to intensify.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい音で、鳥がとんでいく。
example_sentences.english: With a loud noise, the birds will fly away. (fly and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はうちで食べていく？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to go and eat at my place today? (Literally 'will you', but comes across more as an invitation in casual Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 今晩は雨が降ると聞いたから、傘を持っていった。
example_sentences.english: Because I heard that it was going to rain tonight, I took an umbrella.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日ゴルフの練習をしたらだんだんと上手くなっていく。
example_sentences.english: When you practice golf everyday, you will gradually get better.

example_sentences.japanese: これを先生にもっていってください。
example_sentences.english: Please take this to the teacher. (hold and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達にプレゼントをかっていく。
example_sentences.english: I am going to buy a present and take it to my friend. (buy and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 大丈夫！お弁当をもっていくから。
example_sentences.english: It's okay! Because I will take a lunch (bento) with me. (hold and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はテストを受けるから鉛筆をもっていく。
example_sentences.english: Because I am going to take a test today, I will take a pencil. (hold and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 何かたべていってください。
example_sentences.english: Please eat something before you go. (eat and go)

example_sentences.japanese: お医者さんに行って、薬をもらっていくね。
example_sentences.english: I am going to go to the doctor and get some medicine. (receive and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 車で行くのは危険なので、電車にのっていってください。
example_sentences.english: It is dangerous to go by car, so please take a train. (ride and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 服を買って、お祖母さんにもっていく。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to buy clothes and take them to grandma. (hold and go)

example_sentences.japanese: 車に乗る前に、朝ごはんを必ずたべていく。
example_sentences.english: Before getting in the car, I make sure to eat breakfast and then go.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から日本語の勉強をし始めたら、だんだん上手になっていくよ。
example_sentences.english: If you start studying Japanese now, you will go on to become more proficient.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどんお金がたまっていくのを見るのが好き。
example_sentences.english: I like to see my money go on to accumulate steadily.

general_translation: To come to, To become, To continue, To be starting to, Has been ~ing
formation: Verb［て］+ くる
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ くる
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ きます
explanation: A phrase used when a specific event is coming, or has come to be a certain way.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐかえってくるね？
example_sentences.english: You will come back home soon, right? (Literally - Return and come)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も宿題を持ってくるのを忘れた。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to bring my homework today too. (To 'come with' homework was forgotten)

example_sentences.japanese: パパ〜、じゃが芋を買ってきたよ！
example_sentences.english: Dad, I bought the potatoes. (Bought and 'came with')

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、日本語が上手くなってきた感じがする。
example_sentences.english: Recently I feel like I have come to be better at Japanese. (Very similar to 'gotten' in English)

example_sentences.japanese: お金がなくなってきた。
example_sentences.english: I have started to lose money. (has become)

example_sentences.japanese: トイレにいってきます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to the bathroom and come back.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんににてきたね。
example_sentences.english: You have come to look like your mother.

example_sentences.japanese: お弁当をもってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring a bento with you. (hold and come)

example_sentences.japanese: やっと日本語が上手になってきた。
example_sentences.english: I finally came to be better at Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はアメリカに戻ってから、どんどんふとってきた。
example_sentences.english: Since coming back to America, I have rapidly come to be fatter.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が出来ることがわかってきただろう。
example_sentences.english: You have come to understand what you are capable of, haven't you?

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースではずっと雨が降ると言っていたけど、はれてきた。
example_sentences.english: The news said that it was going to keep on raining, but the weather has come to be clear.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスがちかづいてきたから、子供たちが色々なものを欲しいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: Christmas has drawn near(er), so the children are saying that they want various things. (Literally - Has come to be near)

example_sentences.japanese: 朝から家の掃除をしているので、家が綺麗になってきています。
example_sentences.english: Since I've been cleaning the house from this morning, the house is becoming cleaner.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品がだんだん安くなってきたから、また今度買うつもりです。
example_sentences.english: This product has gradually started to get cheaper, so I intend to buy it next time. (has come to be)

general_translation: Way of ~ing, How to ~, Manner of ~ing
formation: Verb［stem］+ 方（かた）［する］Verb + の + 仕方（しかた）Noun + の + Verb［stem］+ 方（かた）Examples:飲（の）みます + 方（かた）勉強（べんきょう）+ の + 仕方（しかた）
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 方（かた）［する］Verb + の + 仕方（しかた）Noun + の + Verb［stem］+ 方（かた）Examples:飲（の）みます + 方（かた）勉強（べんきょう）+ の + 仕方（しかた）
explanation: A common structure highlighting the way in which (A) is done.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のおよぎかたは変だ。
example_sentences.english: His way of swimming is strange.

example_sentences.japanese: 何その食べかた、口を閉じてよ。
example_sentences.english: What is that way of eating? Please close your mouth.

example_sentences.japanese: ネクタイの結びかたを弟に教える。
example_sentences.english: I will teach my brother the way to tie a necktie. (How to do it)

example_sentences.japanese: 外国語の勉強のしかたが分からない。
example_sentences.english: I do not know how to study a foreign language. (The way to do it)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩、ファックスのしかたを教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Senpai, can you teach me how to fax?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は高校の時に母から貯金のしかたを教わりました。
example_sentences.english: I learned how to save money from my mother, when I was in highschool.

example_sentences.japanese: お菓子のつくりかたを学ぶ。
example_sentences.english: I will learn how to make sweets.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法のべんきょうのしかたを教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach me how to study grammar.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻はリモコンのつかいかたが分からない。
example_sentences.english: My wife doesn't know how to use the remote.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のスパゲッティのたべかたは良くない。
example_sentences.english: His way of eating spaghetti is not good.

example_sentences.japanese: 面白いいいかたをするね。
example_sentences.english: That's a funny way of saying it.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強のおしえかたが下手だ。
example_sentences.english: My way of teaching how to study is not very good.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のれんしゅうのしかたは厳しい。
example_sentences.english: His ways of practicing are very strict.

example_sentences.japanese: 変わったさきかたをする花がある。
example_sentences.english: There is a flower that has an odd way of blooming.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は作文のかきかたが上手い。
example_sentences.english: Her manner of writing essays is skillful.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のはなしかたは好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don't like his way of speaking.

example_sentences.japanese: 写真のとりかたを勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I am studying how to take pictures.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越し屋さんの家具の運びかたを見て、彼らの体力にビックリした。
example_sentences.english: After seeing the way the removalists were carrying the furniture, I was surprised by their strength.

formation: Verb + だけでNoun + だけで
casual_structure: Verb + だけでNoun + だけで
explanation: An expression used to highlight something that occurs only with (A).

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに行くだけで楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Just (by) going to a party is fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と話すだけで楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Just talking with my girlfriend is fun. (We don't need to do anything else, because talking is fun enough)

example_sentences.japanese: これは電子レンジだけでオーブンの機能はついていない。
example_sentences.english: This is just a microwave, an oven function is not included.

example_sentences.japanese: 顔を見ただけで、彼はいい人だと分かった。
example_sentences.english: I could tell he was a good person just by his face.

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に時間を過ごすだけで、仲良くなりました。
example_sentences.english: We became good friends just by spending time together.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼を見ただけで性格が悪いと分かった。
example_sentences.english: Just by looking at him I determined that he had a bad personality.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と一緒に居るだけで、幸せ。
example_sentences.english: Just by being with my family I am happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港と聞くだけで、飛行機に乗るのが怖くなる。
example_sentences.english: Just by hearing the word 'airport' I get scared of flying.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と話をするだけで、疲れますよ。
example_sentences.english: Just by talking to him I get tired.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことを言ってくれるだけで、君は優しいと分かる。
example_sentences.english: Just by you saying that, I know that you are nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人だけど、着物を着るだけで、日本人みたいになった。
example_sentences.english: I am a foreigner, but just by wearing a kimono I look Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 階段を上るだけで、しんどくなります。
example_sentences.english: Just by going up some stairs I become exhausted.

example_sentences.japanese: 行ってもいいって彼が言ってくれたが、言い方だけでダメだと分かった。
example_sentences.english: He said that it was okay to go, but just by the tone of his voice I knew it wasn't okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 辛いものを食べるだけで、お腹が痛くなる。
example_sentences.english: Just by eating something spicy my stomach starts to hurt.

formation: だが + Phrase
casual_structure: だが + Phrase
polite_structure: ですが + Phrase
explanation: A formal but short statement that indicates that even though the previous sentence has been determined, (B) is still important.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領が言いました。ですが、私は信じません。
example_sentences.english: The president said that. However, I don't believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじを１００枚買った。だが、当たらなかった。
example_sentences.english: I bought 100 lottery tickets. However, I didn't win.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は弁護士だが、頭が良くない、不思議だ。
example_sentences.english: He is a lawyer, but he is not very smart… How odd.

example_sentences.japanese: 君はいい人だと聞いた。だがね、まだ君を信用できない。
example_sentences.english: I have heard that you are a good person. However, I can't trust you yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日運動をしました。ですが、痩せていません。
example_sentences.english: I exercised everyday. However, I haven't lost any weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は私がしなくてはならない。だがね、君にしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: Really, it is I who has to do it. However, I want you to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: これが基本ルールだ。だが、例外もある。
example_sentences.english: This is a basic rule. However, there are also exceptions.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、旅行に行きます。ですが、まだチケットを買っていません。
example_sentences.english: I am going on a trip tomorrow. However, I still haven't bought my ticket.

example_sentences.japanese: あれは、温泉です。ですが、今はお湯がないです。
example_sentences.english: That is an onsen (hot spring). However, there is no hot water.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は早い時間に寝た。だが寝坊をした。
example_sentences.english: I went to sleep at an early time yesterday. However, I overslept.

example_sentences.japanese: 払いました。ですが、渡してくれませんよ。
example_sentences.english: I have paid. However, they won't hand it over to me!

example_sentences.japanese: このアイデアは面白い。だが、リスクも高い。
example_sentences.english: This is an interesting idea. However, the risk is high.

example_sentences.japanese: 君はよく頑張りました。ですが、答えは全部間違っています。
example_sentences.english: You did your best. However, all your answers are wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことは可能だ。だが、時間がかかるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Such a thing is possible. However, it will probably take time.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣りをするのが好きです。ですが、下手です。
example_sentences.english: I like fishing. However I am terrible at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 美容室に行ったのですが、高かったので帰りました。
example_sentences.english: I went to the hair salon, but since it was expensive, I came home.

formation: Verb［ない］+ な + くて［い］Adjective［い］ + くな + くて［な］Adjective + では(1)ない + な + くてNoun + では(1)ない + な + くてExceptions:いい ￫ よくなくてする ￫ しなくてくる ￫ こなくて(1) じゃ
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ な + くて［い］Adjective［い］ + くな + くて［な］Adjective + では(1)ない + な + くてNoun + では(1)ない + な + くてExceptions:いい ￫ よくなくてする ￫ しなくてくる ￫ こなくて(1) じゃ
explanation: A casual, simple negative conjunctive form, showing sequences of events in which (A) does not happen.

example_sentences.japanese: なる → ならなくて
example_sentences.english: To become → To not become and...

example_sentences.japanese: お金がなくて車が買えない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have money, and I can't buy a car.

example_sentences.japanese: あのケーキは甘くはなくてまずいです。
example_sentences.english: That cake is not sweet, and tastes bad. (は is frequently added between the stem form of adjectives and ない. Often, this is just for emphasis)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車は静かではなくてガソリンの減りも早い。
example_sentences.english: My car is not quiet, and runs out of gas quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: あれは犬ではなくて猫でもないです。
example_sentences.english: That is not a dog, and not a cat either.

example_sentences.japanese: この風呂は汚れはなくて、いつもいい匂いがする。
example_sentences.english: This bath is not dirty, so it always smells good. (Unnatural Japanese, as は will never come between a verb and ない)

example_sentences.japanese: この風呂は汚れなくて、いつもいい匂いがする。
example_sentences.english: This bath doesn't get dirty, and it always smells good. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌い → きらいではなくて
example_sentences.english: Dislike → Not dislike and...

example_sentences.japanese: 病気 → びょうきじゃなくて
example_sentences.english: Illness → Not an illness and...

example_sentences.japanese: 高い → たかくなくて
example_sentences.english: Expensive/tall → Not expensive/tall and...

example_sentences.japanese: いい → よくなくて
example_sentences.english: Good → Not good and...

example_sentences.japanese: 医者 → 医者ではなくて
example_sentences.english: Doctor → Not a doctor and...

example_sentences.japanese: 元気→ げんきじゃなくて
example_sentences.english: Energetic → Not energetic and...

example_sentences.japanese: 会う → あわなくて
example_sentences.english: To meet → To not meet and...

example_sentences.japanese: 眠い → ねむくなくて
example_sentences.english: Sleepy → Not sleepy and...

example_sentences.japanese: 完璧 → かんぺきでなくて
example_sentences.english: Perfect → Not perfect and...

example_sentences.japanese: バス → バスではなくて
example_sentences.english: Bus → Not the bus and...

example_sentences.japanese: くる → こなくて
example_sentences.english: To come → To not come and...

example_sentences.japanese: 歌手 → 歌手じゃなくて
example_sentences.english: Singer → Not a singer and...

example_sentences.japanese: すてき → すてきじゃなくて
example_sentences.english: Nice → Not nice and...

example_sentences.japanese: 問う → とわなくて
example_sentences.english: To ask → To not ask and...

example_sentences.japanese: トーマスにはまだプレゼントをあげないでね。
example_sentences.english: Please don't give Thomas his present yet. (No particular reason, simply implies 'without doing')

example_sentences.japanese: もらったクッキーを弟にあげなくて、妹にあげた。
example_sentences.english: I did not give the cookie I got to my brother, but to my sister. (Implies a specific reason for not giving it to the brother)

general_translation: Not ~ and, Not so, Because not (Examples)
formation: Verb［なくて］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［なくて］+ Phrase［な］Adjective + ではなくて(1) + PhraseNoun + ではなくて(1) + Phrase(1) じゃなくて、でなくて
casual_structure: Verb［なくて］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［なくて］+ Phrase［な］Adjective + ではなくて(1) + PhraseNoun + ではなくて(1) + Phrase(1) じゃなくて、でなくて
explanation: A casual, simple negative conjunctive form, indicating (A) as being the reason or cause for (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 重病じゃなくてホッとした。
example_sentences.english: I was relieved because it wasn't a serious illness.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが来れなくて残念です。
example_sentences.english: It is unfortunate that you were not able to come. (Not being able to come is the reason that it was unfortunate)

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我が治らなくて、今も病院に通っている。
example_sentences.english: Because the injury hasn’t healed, I’m still going to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: このスマホは便利ではなくて残念だ。
example_sentences.english: Since this smartphone is not useful, it's a letdown.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫歯ではなくて安心した。
example_sentences.english: I am relieved because it was not a cavity.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は良く寝れなくて、疲れている。
example_sentences.english: I am tired because I did not sleep well yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は仕事がなくて嬉しい。
example_sentences.english: I am happy because I don't have work tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お茶しかださなくてすみません。」
example_sentences.english: 'I am sorry because I cannot serve you anything but tea.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「試験に合格したかわからなくて不安だね。」
example_sentences.english: 'I don't know if I passed the exam, and I am anxious.' ('I am anxious because I don't know if I passed the exam')

example_sentences.japanese: 「孫がまだきていなくて心配です。」
example_sentences.english: 'My grandchild hasn't come yet and I am worried.' ('I am worried because my grandchild hasn't come yet')

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏が子猫が好きじゃなくて、がっかりした。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend doesn't like kittens and I was let down. (I was let down because my boyfriend doesn't like kittens)

example_sentences.japanese: 時間がなくて、今日も買い物ができなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn't have time, so I couldn't go shopping today either.

example_sentences.japanese: 店にトイレットペーパーがなくて大変です。
example_sentences.english: There is no toilet paper in the stores and it's terrible. (because)

example_sentences.japanese: おじいさんの具合がよくなくてお母さんが困っている。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather's condition is not good and Mom is worried. (Mom is worried because the condition of my grandfather is not good)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ごめんね。一緒に映画館にいけなくて。」
example_sentences.english: 'I was not able to go to the cinema (together) with you and I am sorry.'  ('I am sorry (because) I could not go to the cinema (together) with you')

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋があたたかくなくて全然寝られません。
example_sentences.english: The room is not warm and I cannot sleep at all. (I cannot sleep at all because the room is not warm)

example_sentences.japanese: 「新しいスマホが欲しいけどお金がなくて買えないんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'I want a new smartphone, but because I don't have any money, I can't buy one.'

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が静かじゃなくて全然集中できないよ！
example_sentences.english: The room is not quiet and I cannot focus! (I cannot focus because the room is not quiet)

formation: Verb［ない］+ で
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ で
explanation: A common way to indicate that (B) will be done without doing (A).

example_sentences.japanese: やすまないで仕事をする。
example_sentences.english: To work without taking a break.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に伝えないで休んだの！？
example_sentences.english: You took the day off without notifying your boss!?

example_sentences.japanese: 魚を焼かないで食べたから、お腹を壊した。
example_sentences.english: Since I ate fish without cooking it, I got a stomach ache. (Literally, to break one's stomach)

example_sentences.japanese: アミはドアのカギをかけないで寝るの？危ないよ。
example_sentences.english: Ami, you sleep without locking your doors? That's dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: 「後悔しないで生きたい。」
example_sentences.english: 'I want to live without regret.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの人は便所から手をあらわないで出てきたんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'That person left the toilet without washing their hands!'

example_sentences.japanese: 夕食をたべないで、寝る。
example_sentences.english: To go to bed without eating dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨日、うちの娘は頭をぶつけたけど、なかないで『大丈夫だよ』とだけ言ったんだ。本当に驚いた。」
example_sentences.english: 'Yesterday, my daughter hit her head, but without crying, she just said 'I'm fine.' I was really surprised.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あそばないで、勉強をしてください」ってお母さんが言いました。
example_sentences.english: My mother said 'Please study without playing!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「明日はどこにもいかないで家にいるつもりだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I plan to stay home tomorrow without going anywhere.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼はいつも朝ごはんをたべないで仕事に行くんだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'He always goes to work without eating breakfast.'

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんはまだ寝ているから、大きいこえをださないで遊んでね。
example_sentences.english: Since dad is still sleeping, play without talking loudly.

example_sentences.japanese: 何もいわないで、出て行った。
example_sentences.english: Without saying a word, he left.

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨日は夜遅く家に帰ったからシャワーをあびないで寝たんだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I came back home late at night, so I went to sleep without taking a shower.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行ったことがないから、勉強しないで行くのはやめたほうがいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: You have never been to Japan, so I think that you better refrain from going without studying (first).

example_sentences.japanese: 昼ご飯を温めないで食べた。
example_sentences.english: I ate my lunch without heating it up. (Event 2 happened without event 1)

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットが繋がらなくて困ってる。
example_sentences.english: I am bothered because the internet isn't connecting. (Event 2 happened because of event 1)

general_translation: Was done to ~ by ~, Done without consent, Done to one's dismay
formation: Examples:［る1］Verb ￫ 見（み）る + られる［る⁵］Verb ￫ 座（すわ）る + られる［う］Verb ￫ 歌（うた）う + われる［く］Verb ￫ 歩（ある）く + かれる［す］Verb ￫ 話（はな）す + される［つ］Verb ￫ 打（う）つ + たれる［ぬ］Verb ￫ 死（し）ぬ + なれる［ぶ］Verb ￫ 飛（と）ぶ + ばれる ［む］Verb ￫ 休（やす）む + まれる［ぐ］Verb ￫ 泳（およ）ぐ + がれるExceptions:する→されるくる→こられる

explanation: A common, sometimes negative way to express that someone is the receiver of an action.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のアイスクリームを兄にたべられた。
example_sentences.english: My ice cream was eaten by my brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬に噛まれるのが怖いから、犬には近づけない。
example_sentences.english: Because I am afraid of getting bitten by a dog, I can't approach them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はいつも彼と比べられる。
example_sentences.english: I always get compared to him.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らない人からいたずらをされるのがきらい。
example_sentences.english: I don't like being pranked by strangers.

example_sentences.japanese: 急に義理の母に来られると困る。
example_sentences.english: I feel troubled when my mother in law visits unannounced.

example_sentences.japanese: 変な話を親にきかれた。
example_sentences.english: My strange conversation was overheard by my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は部屋をきれいにして、ほめられた。
example_sentences.english: I was praised for cleaning my room.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題をしたけど、持って来るのを忘れた。何といわれるかな。
example_sentences.english: Even though I did my homework, I forgot to bring it with me. I wonder what will be said to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあいつらに何をされてもいいけど、あいつらには絶対に君の名前を教えない。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter what is done to me by them, I won't give up your name to them.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日友達の家が泥棒にはいられた。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, my friend's house was broken into by a robber.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄のクッキーを食べたから、兄になぐられた。痛かった。
example_sentences.english: I ate my older brother's cookie, so I was punched by my older brother. It hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の牛乳を全部誰かにのまれた。
example_sentences.english: All of my milk was drunk by someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 義理の母に家にこられたから、イライラしている。
example_sentences.english: I was paid a visit by my mother-in-law, so I am irritated. (came)

example_sentences.japanese: 私のお金で嫁に服をかわれた。
example_sentences.english: My wife bought clothes with my money.

example_sentences.japanese: 先月僕のパソコンがぬすまれたけど、犯人が捕まってパソコンが戻って来た。
example_sentences.english: Last month my computer was stolen, but the thief was caught and I got my computer back.

example_sentences.japanese: 留守番たのまれたから、僕はどこにも行けない。
example_sentences.english: I was entrusted with house-sitting, so I can't go anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はどこでも寝れます。
example_sentences.english: I can sleep anywhere. (I have the potential to sleep anywhere)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はどこでも寝られる。
example_sentences.english: I can sleep anywhere. (I have the potential to sleep anywhere)

grammar_point: 他動詞（たどうし）・自動詞（じどうし）
general_translation: Done through action vs. occurring on its own
