explanation: A type of verb that highlights either the subject or object of an action.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫を集めた・虫があつまった
example_sentences.english: I gathered bugs. The bugs gathered.

example_sentences.japanese: ローソクを消す。
example_sentences.english: To put out a candle.

example_sentences.japanese: 風でローソクが消える。
example_sentences.english: For a candle to be put out by the wind.

example_sentences.japanese: 木からバナナ​​が落ちる。
example_sentences.english: Bananas fall from trees.

example_sentences.japanese: 木からバナナを落とす。
example_sentences.english: To drop a banana from a tree.

example_sentences.japanese: 探していたカバンをみつけた。
example_sentences.english: I found the bag that I had been looking for.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人がみつかった。
example_sentences.english: The criminal has been found.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキの上に乗っていたロウソクをけした。
example_sentences.english: I blew out (extinguished) the candles on the cake.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所のライトがきえた。
example_sentences.english: The light in the kitchen went out.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこにある窓をあけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please open the window over there.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に気温が急にさがりましたね。
example_sentences.english: The temperature really has suddenly dropped (become low), hasn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 板をちょっとさげるから頭に気をつけてね。
example_sentences.english: I am going to lower the board, so watch your head.

example_sentences.japanese: 忘れ物をみつけた・忘れ物が見つかった
example_sentences.english: I found the lost item・The lost item was found.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合を始めた・試合がはじまった
example_sentences.english: I started the match • The match started.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降った時に窓があいていたから、床が濡れている。
example_sentences.english: Since the window had been open when it was raining, the floor is wet.

example_sentences.japanese: 家には誰も居なかったがテレビがついていた。
example_sentences.english: There was no one home, but the TV was on.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん。僕がテレビをつけたけれど、家を出る時に消し忘れた。
example_sentences.english: Sorry. I turned on the TV, but when I left the house I forgot to turn it off.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年からアメリカに住むことにした。
example_sentences.english: From next year I am going to live in America. (I have decided to live in America starting next year)

example_sentences.japanese: 来年からアメリカに住むことになる。
example_sentences.english: From next year I am going to live in America. (I will be living in America starting next year due to work/school/family matters beyond my direct control)

formation: Verb［stem］+ なおす
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ なおす
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ なおします
explanation: A common term which indicates that (A) will be redone, or fixed.

example_sentences.japanese: この文章をかきなおした方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should rewrite this sentence.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様に挨拶をしなおす。
example_sentences.english: To re-greet the customer.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪がちゃんと染まってなかったので染めなおします。
example_sentences.english: Because my hair wasn't properly dyed, I will redo it.

example_sentences.japanese: フェンスを塗りなおす。
example_sentences.english: To repaint the fence.

example_sentences.japanese: プロポーズはやりなおす事が出来ないから、緊張している。
example_sentences.english: Because you can't redo proposals, I am nervous.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お前」って言うな。いいなおしてください。
example_sentences.english: Don't say 'おまえ'. Please rephrase what you said!

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんに電話をかけなおしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please call the client again.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のことをみなおしました。
example_sentences.english: I renewed my view of her.

example_sentences.japanese: はい！急いでやりなおします。
example_sentences.english: Yes, sir! I will quickly redo it.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一度かんがえなおしませんか？
example_sentences.english: Won't you reconsider?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は色々とおもいなおす事が多い。
example_sentences.english: I tend to rethink about various things a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の家にはリビングがなかったので、家をたてなおしました。
example_sentences.english: My house didn't have a living room, so I rebuilt it.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗い物をやりなおさないとお母さんに怒られるよ。
example_sentences.english: Mom will get angry if you do not rewash the dishes.

example_sentences.japanese: その時は大変だったが、経済がもちなおしたから大丈夫。
example_sentences.english: That was a tough time, but the economy recovered, so we are alright.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題はかんがえなおす必要があると私は思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that this problem needs to be thought over again.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類はペンで書かないでください、鉛筆でかきなおしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't write on this document with a pen, please rewrite it in pencil.

formation: Phrase + ということ
casual_structure: Phrase + ということ
explanation: A phrase used to create noun-like phrases, or sometimes ask questions about what (A) means.

example_sentences.japanese: もう別れたいということ？
example_sentences.english: It means that you want to break up? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 宇宙人はいるということですか？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean aliens exist?

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に住んでいるけど付き合ってはいないの？ルームメイトだということだよね？
example_sentences.english: You are living together, but not dating? So that means they're your roommate, right?

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生の教え方が酷いということを聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the way that teacher teaches is harsh.

example_sentences.japanese: これが正しいってことですか？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean that this is correct?

example_sentences.japanese: 車が壊れたの？電車でくるってこと？遅れないで来てね。
example_sentences.english: Your car broke? Does that mean you are coming by train? Please don't be late.

example_sentences.japanese: これは人工ってこと？
example_sentences.english: You mean that this is man made?

example_sentences.japanese: この店は美味しいということをよく聞きます。
example_sentences.english: I often hear that this restaurant is delicious. (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 私がみんなの分を払うということですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you mean I should pay for everyone? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 私が、一人でお皿を洗わなくてはいけないということですか？
example_sentences.english: Do you mean that I have to wash the dishes all by myself? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 真面目になるということですね。
example_sentences.english: You mean that you will get serious? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本に行っていないということですか ？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean that he hasn't been to Japan? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はもっと頑張らなくてはいけないということですね。
example_sentences.english: It means that I should try harder, right? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 砂糖が沢山入っているって？体に悪いということ？
example_sentences.english: Did you say that there is a lot of sugar in this? So that means that it is bad for your body? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 病院にもう行かなくていいの？治ったということ？
example_sentences.english: You don't have to go to the hospital anymore? Does that mean that you are healed? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 来年から日本に住むということですか？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean that you will be living in Japan from next year? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつらがお金を全部盗んだということ？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean that they stole all of the money? (Phrase to noun)

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫にチーズしか残っていないということですか？
example_sentences.english: Does that mean that there is nothing but cheese in the refrigerator? (Phrase to noun)

formation: Verb + とき［い］Adjective + とき［な］Adjective + な + ときNoun + の + とき
casual_structure: Verb + とき［い］Adjective + とき［な］Adjective + な + ときNoun + の + とき
explanation: A common word, used for highlighting either broad or narrow time frames.

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩をするときに音楽を聴く。
example_sentences.english: I listen to music when I take a walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 狭い駐車場で車のドアを開けたときにドアを壁にぶつけた。
example_sentences.english: When I opened my car door in a small parking lot, I slammed it on the wall. (Individual event)

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いときはエアコンを点けましょう。
example_sentences.english: When it is hot, let's turn on the air conditioner. (Broad time)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は暇なときに本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: He reads books when he is bored. (Hobby)

example_sentences.japanese: 雨のときは家でゴロゴロしています。
example_sentences.english: When it rains, I laze around in my house. (Habit)

example_sentences.japanese: 授業のときは静かにしなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: When you are having class, you have to be quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: あの映画を見たとき、泣いた。
example_sentences.english: When I watched that movie, I cried.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変なときに彼の親は亡くなった。
example_sentences.english: His parents died when he was going through a difficult time.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いときは、お風呂に入りたくなる。
example_sentences.english: When it is cold, I want to take a bath.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京に行ったときに、スカイツリーを見た。
example_sentences.english: When I went to Tokyo, I saw the Skytree.

example_sentences.japanese: 写真を撮るときは、笑ってください。
example_sentences.english: When you take a picture, please smile.

example_sentences.japanese: 出かけるときは、「行ってきます」と言います。
example_sentences.english: When you go out (from your house) you say 'いってきます' (I'm off!).

example_sentences.japanese: 入院したとき、寂しかった。
example_sentences.english: When I was hospitalized I was lonely.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はカラオケに行くときに幸せな気持ちになります。
example_sentences.english: When I go to karaoke I feel happy.

example_sentences.japanese: そこの公園に遊びに行ったときに、お金を見つけた。
example_sentences.english: When I went to play at that park I found some money.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜布団に入ったときに、トイレに行きたくなった。
example_sentences.english: Last night when I got in my futon, I ended up needing to go to the bathroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校から家に帰った時に火曜日だった。
example_sentences.english: The time when I was going home from school was Tuesday. (Tuesday is a state, rather than an action, so とき will not be used to express something like this) (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は高校生の時に俺が好きな女の子に告白して、「え、無理...」って言われた。
example_sentences.english: When I was in highschool I asked out a girl I liked, and she said 'umm, no way…' (時（とき） is describing the broad event of 'being a highschool student', while て goes on to describe another single event that happened during that time)

formation: まず + Phrase
casual_structure: まず + Phrase
explanation: An expression used to show that (A) will be done firstly, or before anything else.

example_sentences.japanese: まず踊りに行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: First let's go dancing.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤い車がまず、ゴールをしました。
example_sentences.english: The red car finished to start with. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: まず宿題をしたほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: First, it would be best for me to do my homework.

example_sentences.japanese: まずエンジンをかけて。
example_sentences.english: First, please turn on the engine.

example_sentences.japanese: まず壁を塗ってください。
example_sentences.english: To start with, please paint the walls.

example_sentences.japanese: まずこれだよね。
example_sentences.english: This one first right?

example_sentences.japanese: まずこの部分を仕上げてください。
example_sentences.english: To start, finish this portion. (First)

example_sentences.japanese: まず買い物して、その後食べに行きましょうか。
example_sentences.english: First let's go shopping then after that, shall we go out to eat?

example_sentences.japanese: まず本を読んで、映画を見に行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: First read the book, then let's go see the movie.

example_sentences.japanese: まずお湯を沸かして、野菜を入れましょう。
example_sentences.english: To start, boil some water and put in the vegetables.

example_sentences.japanese: 行く前にまず何かを食べましょう。
example_sentences.english: Before we go, first let's eat something.

example_sentences.japanese: まず犬に餌をやってから、掃除機をかけましょう。
example_sentences.english: To start with, I will feed the dog, and then I shall do the vacuuming.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビを見たいけど、まず買い物に行かなくちゃいけない。
example_sentences.english: I want to watch TV, but first I have to go shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: まずひらがなとカタカナを覚えてから、漢字の勉強をしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Start with memorizing hiragana and katakana, then let's move on to studying Kanji. (First)

example_sentences.japanese: まず、この中で一番好きな飲み物を選んでください。
example_sentences.english: To start, please choose your favorite drink from these.

example_sentences.japanese: まず別れた方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think you should break up first.

general_translation: Even, To even, To the extent of
formation: Noun + まで(も)
casual_structure: Noun + まで(も)
explanation: A phrase which states that something is even to or until the surprising extent of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: こっちまでイライラしてきた。
example_sentences.english: Even I am starting to get annoyed. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 隣街の店舗まで行ったけど、そこでもお目当てのグッズは売っていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I even went to the store in the next town, but even there, the merchandise I was looking for wasn't being sold.

example_sentences.japanese: お腹が空きすぎて、大嫌いなバナナまで食べた。
example_sentences.english: Because I was so hungry, I even ate a banana, which I hate.

example_sentences.japanese: バイクまで持っているの？
example_sentences.english: You even have a bike?

example_sentences.japanese: 一回笑ったら、面白くない話までおかしくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you start laughing, even uninteresting topics become funny.

example_sentences.japanese: それまでやらなくてはいけないの？
example_sentences.english: I have to even do that? (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 頭まで痛くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: Even my head is starting to hurt. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 夜中まで日本語の文法を勉強している。
example_sentences.english: I'm studying Japanese grammar until the middle of the night. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: お腹が空いているとき、熊は果実まで食べる。
example_sentences.english: Bears will even go as far as to eat berries when they are hungry. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 私まで疑われるから、話しかけないで。
example_sentences.english: Even I will be suspected, so don't talk to me. (even...to the extent of)

example_sentences.japanese: 君たちがいたから、ここまで来られた。
example_sentences.english: Because you guys were here, we were able to come as far as this point. (to this extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は何年間も勉強したから、漢字まで書ける。
example_sentences.english: He has studied a number of years, so he can even write kanji. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は１年間で漢字をいっぱい覚えただけじゃなくて、日本語能力試験２級まで受けた。
example_sentences.english: That person not only remembered a lot of kanji in one year of study, but he even took the JLPT N2. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はアップルが好きで、アップルウォッチまで持っています。
example_sentences.english: He likes Apple, so he even has an Apple Watch. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は頭がいいから夜遅くまで勉強をしなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: He is smart, so it is okay if he doesn't go so far as to study all night. (to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は親切だが、家族と一緒とまでは言えない。
example_sentences.english: He is really kind, but I wouldn't go as far as calling him family. (even...to the extent・until)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はスポーツカーまでも持っています。
example_sentences.english: I even have a sports car.

general_translation: By ~, By the time that ~, Before ~
formation: Verb + までにNoun + までに
casual_structure: Verb + までにNoun + までに
explanation: A phrase commonly used to highlight a deadline by which something should be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに電話をください。
example_sentences.english: Please call by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: ５時までに駅に来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please come to the station by 5 o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 遊びに行くまでに片付けてね。
example_sentences.english: Please tidy up by the time you go out to play.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月までにレポートを書く。
example_sentences.english: I will write a report by next month. (Focus is on 'next month' being the deadline)

example_sentences.japanese: 来月までレポートを書く。
example_sentences.english: I am writing a report until next month. (Focus is on 'next month' being the end point for something that will continue until that point)

example_sentences.japanese: お昼までには着きます。
example_sentences.english: I will arrive by noon.

example_sentences.japanese: １０時までに帰ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Could you please come back home by 10?

example_sentences.japanese: 来週までには終わります。
example_sentences.english: I will be done by next week.

example_sentences.japanese: ８時までに学校につかなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to arrive at school by 8 o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: １１月末までに、クリスマスプレゼントを買いに行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go Christmas present shopping by the end of November.

example_sentences.japanese: １０時までに帰ってくることは無理です。
example_sentences.english: It will be impossible for me to be back by ten.

example_sentences.japanese: 下書きを見て欲しい人は、明日までに提出してください。
example_sentences.english: For those who want their first draft to be looked at, please turn it in by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りまでに出すことは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Turning it in by the deadline is going to be difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: ５時までに漢字１００文字覚えるのは大変です。
example_sentences.english: Remembering 100 kanji by five o'clock is going to be rough.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ全部覚えていませんが、来週までに絶対に覚えます。
example_sentences.english: I still haven't memorized it all, but I will definitely have it memorized by next week.

example_sentences.japanese: ２１歳までに、兄より背が高くなりたいです。
example_sentences.english: By the time I'm 21, I want to be taller than my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬が終わるまでにスキーをしたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go skiing by the end of winter. (Not just 'by winter', but specifically 'by the end of winter')

general_translation: Also, As well, Moreover, Again, Additionally
formation: また + Phrase
casual_structure: また + Phrase
explanation: A structure which indicates that (A) will be done again, or in addition to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: また寝坊したの？
example_sentences.english: You overslept again?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は宇宙飛行士であり、またアナウンサーでもある。
example_sentences.english: He is an astronaut, and also an announcer!

example_sentences.japanese: また遊ぼうね！
example_sentences.english: Let's hang out again!

example_sentences.japanese: また行こうね！
example_sentences.english: Let's go again!

example_sentences.japanese: またカンニングしたの？
example_sentences.english: You cheated again?

example_sentences.japanese: またその夢を見たい。
example_sentences.english: I want to dream that dream again.

example_sentences.japanese: また、彼からチョコをもらった。
example_sentences.english: Moreover, I received chocolate from him.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、また旅行に行くつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I intend to go on another trip. (again)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、また授業が始まります。
example_sentences.english: Class will start again from tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までにまた連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: Please contact me again by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: えっ？また病院に行くの？
example_sentences.english: What? You are going to the hospital again?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日ピザを食べたけど、今日もまたピザを食べる？
example_sentences.english: You had pizza yesterday, but you are going to have pizza again today?

example_sentences.japanese: また子供が「スマートフォンが欲しい」と言っている。
example_sentences.english: My kid is saying that he 'wants a smartphone' again.

example_sentences.japanese: また同じことが起きたから、どんどんイライラしてきた。
example_sentences.english: The same thing happened again, so I am quickly getting irritated.

example_sentences.japanese: また授業にノートを持っていくのを忘れたね。
example_sentences.english: You forgot to bring your notebook to class again, I see.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は晩ご飯を食べてから、また勉強した。
example_sentences.english: Once he ate dinner he studied again.

formation: Verb［stem］+ はじめる
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ はじめる
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ はじめます
explanation: A construction that indicates that an action is being started.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、雪がふりはじめた。
example_sentences.english: It started to snow this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月からお金をためはじめます。
example_sentences.english: I will start saving money from next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌を歌いはじめる。
example_sentences.english: To start singing a song.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から日本語をならいはじめる。
example_sentences.english: I will start learning Japanese from tomorrow. (Will start)

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がふりはじめてきた。
example_sentences.english: It is starting to rain. (Is starting)

example_sentences.japanese: 高校生の時にお金をためはじめた。
example_sentences.english: I started saving up money when I was in high school. (Has started)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、日本語をならいはじめます。
example_sentences.english: I will start learning Japanese from tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 練習しはじめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please begin to (do) practice.

example_sentences.japanese: ９時になってから、はたらきはじめた。
example_sentences.english: I started working from nine.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がはなしはじめてから１時間経った。
example_sentences.english: It has been an hour since he started talking.

example_sentences.japanese: 海に行ってすぐおよぎはじめた。
example_sentences.english: I went to the ocean and started swimming at once.

example_sentences.japanese: またさわぎはじめた。本当にあいつらうるさいね。
example_sentences.english: They started being boisterous again. They are really noisy, aren't they?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行ってから、文法を勉強しはじめた。
example_sentences.english: I started studying grammar after going to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強しはじめてすぐ、日本語の難しさが分かった。
example_sentences.english: Right after I started studying Japanese, I realized the difficulty of the language.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業してから、仕事にいきはじめた。
example_sentences.english: I started going to work after graduating from college.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品をうりはじめてから、どんどんお客さんが増えています。
example_sentences.english: Since we started selling this product, customers have been on the rise.

example_sentences.japanese: まずひらがなとカタカナを勉強して、その後漢字を勉強しはじめた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: First study hiragana and katakana. After that it would be better if you began to study kanji.

formation: Verb［stem］+ 終（お）わる
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 終（お）わる
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 終（お）わります
explanation: A construction that indicates that an action is being completed.

example_sentences.japanese: ２時間もかかったけど、たべおわりました。
example_sentences.english: It took two hours but I finished eating.

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物は全部届けおわりました。
example_sentences.english: I have finished delivering all the packages.

example_sentences.japanese: この車のローンは明日払いおわる。
example_sentences.english: I will finish paying the loan for this car tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯を食べおわるまで、デザートは禁止だ。
example_sentences.english: You're not allowed to have dessert until you finish eating your food.

example_sentences.japanese: そのコーヒー、まだ飲みおわってないの？
example_sentences.english: Have you not finished  drinking that coffee?

example_sentences.japanese: 長いレポートでしたが、今日やっと読みおわりました！
example_sentences.english: It was a long report, but today I finally finished reading it!

example_sentences.japanese: ３時ごろにつくりおわる。
example_sentences.english: I will finish making it around three o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: この番組はみおわった。
example_sentences.english: I finished watching this program.

example_sentences.japanese: はしりおわったのは何時ぐらいでしたか？
example_sentences.english: Around what time did you finish running?

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題をなおしおわった人は教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Those who have finished correcting their homework, let me know.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビを見るのはたべおわってから。
example_sentences.english: You may watch TV after having finished eating.

example_sentences.japanese: 何になりたいかの文章をかきおわりましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you finish writing about what you want to be in the future?

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館から借りた本はよみおわった？
example_sentences.english: Did you finish reading the book that you borrowed from the library?

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がはなしおわるまで、良く聞いて下さい。
example_sentences.english: Until the teacher has finished speaking, please listen well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が説明しおわったから、先生に質問をした。
example_sentences.english: Because the teacher finished explaining, I asked the teacher a question.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はいつも朝ご飯をたべおわるまでに１時間もかかる。
example_sentences.english: It always takes more than an hour by the time that person finishes eating breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日覚えなくてはならない漢字をおぼえおわるまで部屋から出ないで。
example_sentences.english: Don't come out of your room today until you finish memorizing the kanji that you have to memorize.

formation: Verb + ころ［い］Adjective + ころ［な］Adjective + な + ころNoun + ごろNoun + の + ころ
casual_structure: Verb + ころ［い］Adjective + ころ［な］Adjective + な + ころNoun + ごろNoun + の + ころ
explanation: A word that is often used to approximate large periods of time, but not very specific points.

example_sentences.japanese: ８時ごろに帰りました。
example_sentences.english: I went home around eight o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: １１時ごろに帰ってくる。
example_sentences.english: I will be home around 11.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は大学生のころに富士山を登りました。
example_sentences.english: I climbed Mount Fuji around when I was a college student.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のくらいはよく親と動物園へ行きました。
example_sentences.english: When I was approximately a child, I often went to the zoo with my parents. (Unnatural Japanese, as being a child is a broad time frame)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころはよく親と動物園へ行きました。
example_sentences.english: Around when I was a child, I often went to the zoo with my parents. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 二メートルくらいの所に印をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please make a mark around the 2 meter point. (Natural Japanese, as an approximation is being discussed)

example_sentences.japanese: 二メートルごろの所に印をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please make a mark within the span of 2 meters. (Unnatural Japanese, as the listener would think that marking a line anywhere within the two meter space is fine)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は１２時くらいに帰る。
example_sentences.english: I will be home around 12.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は１２時ごろに帰る。
example_sentences.english: I will be home around 12.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京に行った友達は今ごろ着いているでしょう。
example_sentences.english: My friend who went to Tokyo is probably arriving around now...

example_sentences.japanese: 月曜日の夜ごろに、雨が降ります。
example_sentences.english: It will rain around Monday night.

example_sentences.japanese: 何時ごろ帰って来る？
example_sentences.english: Around what time will you come home?

example_sentences.japanese: １１時ごろに帰って来るから、ご飯はいらないです。
example_sentences.english: I will get home about 11, so I don't need dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: 家を出るのは何時ごろ？
example_sentences.english: Around what time will you leave (the house)?

example_sentences.japanese: 晴れていましたが、７時ごろに雨が降りました。
example_sentences.english: It was clear, but around seven it rained.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころはよく公園で遊びました。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, I often played in the park. (Around the time I was a child)

example_sentences.japanese: ３時ごろ昼ご飯を食べたから、今はあまりお腹が空いてない。
example_sentences.english: I ate lunch around three o'clock, so I am not really hungry now.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生のころ日本語を習い始めた。
example_sentences.english: Around the time I was an elementary student, I started learning Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が６時ごろに終わるから、ジムに行きませんか？
example_sentences.english: I will finish working around six o'clock, so why don't we go to the gym?

example_sentences.japanese: また１時ごろに仕事に戻らなくてはいけないので、１時までにご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I have to go back to work around one o'clock, so I will eat before one o'clock.

formation: Verb［た］+ あとでNoun + の + あとで後（あと）で + PhraseVerb + のは + あとで
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ あとでNoun + の + あとで後（あと）で + PhraseVerb + のは + あとで
explanation: A phrase that simply highlights that one action will take place after another.

example_sentences.japanese: あとで洗濯もの干してね。
example_sentences.english: Please hang the laundry later.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強するのは食べたあとでいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You can study after you finish eating. (With the time after eating)

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事のあとで、飲み会に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go to the party after work. (With the time after work)

example_sentences.japanese: コピーを取るのはあとでいいから、今は上司に電話して。
example_sentences.english: Since it's fine to make the copies later, please call the boss right now. (With the time after calling the boss)

example_sentences.japanese: またあとで、会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet again later.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強したあとで、遊んでもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: It is ok to play after you study.

example_sentences.japanese: あとで買い物に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go shopping later.

example_sentences.japanese: あとで話がある。
example_sentences.english: We will talk later.

example_sentences.japanese: 食事のあとで、お皿を洗わなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to wash dishes after a meal.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はアルバイトのあとで、疲れている。
example_sentences.english: I am tired after my part time job.

example_sentences.japanese: あとで返すから、１００円貸してください。
example_sentences.english: Since I will pay you back later, please lend me 100 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: あとで部屋の掃除をしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please clean your room later.

example_sentences.japanese: またグラスが割れている！あとであの子に話さなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: Another glass is broken! Later I will need to talk to that kid.

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜を切るのはあとでいいから、今お湯沸かして。
example_sentences.english: You can cut the vegetables later. Right now, boil some water.

example_sentences.japanese: 先にご飯を食べて、あとで映画館で会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: First, I'm going to eat. Later let's meet at the movie theater.

example_sentences.japanese: さっき駅で見た人が私の友達だったと、あとで分かった。
example_sentences.english: I found out later that the person I saw at the station earlier was my friend.

formation: Verb［ている］+ た
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ た
polite_structure: Verb［ている］+ ました
explanation: A phrase that shows when an action was continuing in the past.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をしていたけど、今は休んでいる。
example_sentences.english: I was studying but am taking a break right now.

example_sentences.japanese: シャワーが壊れていたから二日間もシャワーを浴びれなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because the shower was broken, I was not able to take a shower for 2 days. (Was in the state of being broken)

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は夜遅くまでカラオケで歌っていたので、のどが痛いです。
example_sentences.english: I was singing until late last night at karaoke, so my throat hurts. (Was doing karaoke)

example_sentences.japanese: 昔はパーマをかけていました。
example_sentences.english: In the past, I used to have my hair permed. (Was getting perms)

example_sentences.japanese: 窓が割れていました。
example_sentences.english: The window was smashed. (Was in the state of being smashed)

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんがその椅子に座っていたから、こっちに座りな。
example_sentences.english: Dad was sitting there, so sit here please.

example_sentences.japanese: 音楽をきいていたから、電話が聞こえなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because I was listening to music I couldn't hear the phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日１時ごろにねていた。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday around one o'clock I was sleeping.

example_sentences.japanese: ４時間も椅子にすわっていたから、お尻が痛い。
example_sentences.english: I was sitting for as much as four hours, so my butt hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが帰って来た時私はご飯をつくっていた。
example_sentences.english: When my mom came home I was making food.

example_sentences.japanese: あっ、ごめん。腰が痛いってわすれていた。
example_sentences.english: Oh, sorry. I was forgetting that your lower back hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 長い間ランニングをしていたから、喉が乾きました。
example_sentences.english: Because I was running for a long time, I became thirsty.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビをみていた時停電になった。
example_sentences.english: When I was watching TV the power went out.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で日本語がだんだん上手になっていたのに、アメリカに帰ってきて凄く下手になった。
example_sentences.english: In Japan my Japanese was getting better, but now that I have come back to America my Japanese ability has gone way down.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命はしっていたから、疲れた。
example_sentences.english: I was running my hardest, so I became exhausted.

example_sentences.japanese: また僕が勉強していた時邪魔したね。やめてくれる？
example_sentences.english: You bothered me again when I was studying, yeah? Would you cut it out?

example_sentences.japanese: 神田さんは増田さんより練習をしていたから、神田さんの方がうまいです。
example_sentences.english: Kanda-san was practicing more than Masuda-san, so Kanda-san is more skilled.

general_translation: Times (In each time period), Every, Frequency of
formation: Timeframe + に + Number of Times
casual_structure: Timeframe + に + Number of Times
explanation: A particle that often shows how frequently something occurs.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年に三回ぐらい海外旅行に行く。
example_sentences.english: I take trips abroad about three times in a year. (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一ヶ月に一回友達と遊園地に行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the amusement park with my friend every month. (One time per month)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一週間に２回しか歯を磨かないから、口が臭い。
example_sentences.english: Because he only brushes his teeth twice every week, his mouth stinks.

example_sentences.japanese: 一日に六時間は寝る必要がある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to sleep for six hours every day. (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 一時間に十本の電車がある。
example_sentences.english: There are ten trains every hour. (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 公務員は一年に一回ボーナスをもらう。
example_sentences.english: Public servants get a bonus every year. (Once each year) (Frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はタバコを１日に４０本ぐらい吸う。
example_sentences.english: He smokes about 40 cigarettes every day. (40 each day)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は子供たちに１週間に５００円のお小遣いをあげる。
example_sentences.english: I give my kids 500 yen every week for their allowance. (500 yen per week)

example_sentences.japanese: 給料は月に２０万円です。
example_sentences.english: I make 200,000 yen every month. (200,000 yen per month)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は１日に１時間日本語を勉強している。
example_sentences.english: She studies Japanese one hour every day. (One hour each day)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はよく運動するから、１日に３回プロテインを飲む必要がある。
example_sentences.english: Because I do a lot of exercise, I need to drink protein (shakes) three times every day. (three times each day) (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: この駅には１時間に２回電車が来ます。
example_sentences.english: At this station, two trains come every hour. (Two trains each hour) (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬は１日に２回餌をあげなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to feed my dog two times every day. (Two times each day) (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 週に二回は病院に来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please come to the hospital twice every week. (Two times each week) (frequency)

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を引きたくないから、１日に林檎を１個食べて、水を２リットル飲む。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to catch a cold, so I eat an apple and drink two liters of water every day. (Each day)

example_sentences.japanese: ２年間で５０万円も貯めた。
example_sentences.english: In two years, I saved up ￥500,000. (Natural Japanese, as this expresses the amount of time that something took)

formation: とうとう + Phrase
casual_structure: とうとう + Phrase
explanation: A phrase meaning finally, which focuses on arriving at the head of some long journey or effort.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう休みだ。
example_sentences.english: Finally it is my day off.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとうロシアに行く。
example_sentences.english: I will finally go to Russia. (After all this time, I can finally go to Russia)

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう夏休みだ！
example_sentences.english: It's finally summer break! (Good result)

example_sentences.japanese: とうとうお前が大学生か...
example_sentences.english: So you're finally a college student... (After all this time, have you finally become a college student?)

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう夏休みが終わる日が来た。
example_sentences.english: The day that summer break ends has finally arrived. (Bad result)

example_sentences.japanese: とうとうタバコをやめた。
example_sentences.english: I finally quit smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: それをとうとう捨てた。
example_sentences.english: I finally threw that away. (I threw that away after all)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日痛みがとうとうなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Today the pain finally went away.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう漢字の勉強ができる。
example_sentences.english: I can finally study kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう日本に着いた。
example_sentences.english: I have finally arrived in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう明日で最後だ。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow is finally the last day.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう昼食の時間だ。
example_sentences.english: It is finally time for lunch.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう真面目に日本語を勉強する。
example_sentences.english: I will finally study Japanese seriously.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう彼は注射をうった。
example_sentences.english: He administered the shot after all. (He finally administered the shot)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はとうとう失敗したと分かった。
example_sentences.english: He finally realized that he made a mistake. (Failed)

example_sentences.japanese: ２６時間もかかったけど、とうとう生まれた。
example_sentences.english: It took (as much as) 26 hours, but the baby was finally born.

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ夏が来た。
example_sentences.english: Finally, summer has come. (Natural Japanese)

formation: Verb + より + AdjectiveNoun + より + Adjective
casual_structure: Verb + より + AdjectiveNoun + より + Adjective
explanation: A word that is often used for highlighting comparisons between (A) and (B).

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの絵は私の絵より上手。
example_sentences.english: Your paintings are better than mine.

example_sentences.japanese: パンダはバナナより重い。
example_sentences.english: Pandas are heavier than bananas.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽はロウソクより明るい。
example_sentences.english: The sun is brighter than a candle.

example_sentences.japanese: 月曜日より日曜日がいい。
example_sentences.english: Sunday is better than Monday.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は英語より話しにくい。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is harder to speak than English.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも飲んでいる水より好き。
example_sentences.english: I like this (drink) more than the water that I usually drink.

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツをするより、ゲームの方が楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Video games are more exciting than sports.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生は高校生より宿題が少ない。
example_sentences.english: College students have less homework than high school students.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は警察官より消防士になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to become a firefighter more than a police officer.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ物は、お寿司より、ピザの方が好きです。
example_sentences.english: If it's food, I like pizza more than sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: あの家よりこの家の方が好き。
example_sentences.english: I like this house more than that house.

example_sentences.japanese: カタカナよりひらがなの方が覚えやすい。
example_sentences.english: Hiragana is easier to memorize than katakana.

example_sentences.japanese: 私より勉強が出来る人はいないだろう。
example_sentences.english: There probably isn't anyone who can study more than me.

example_sentences.japanese: この飲み物よりその飲み物の方が美味しいね。
example_sentences.english: That drink is more delicious than this drink.

example_sentences.japanese: これがより高いものになります。
example_sentences.english: This is the thing that would be more expensive. (Compared to everything else that is here)

formation: Verb + ごとにNoun + ごとに
casual_structure: Verb + ごとにNoun + ごとに
explanation: A structure that highlights something occuring every (A), focusing on every individual interval.

example_sentences.japanese: あのチームは、試合をするごとに強くなっている。
example_sentences.english: That team is getting stronger with every match.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗をする経験は無駄ではありません。失敗をするごとに上達します。
example_sentences.english: Failing is not a pointless experience. Every time you fail, you improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は３時間ごとにお菓子を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I eat snacks every 3 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏ごとにアメリカに帰ります。
example_sentences.english: Every summer I go back to America.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒ごとに紙を渡した。
example_sentences.english: I gave a paper to every student. (Each)

example_sentences.japanese: 二日ごとに友達とサッカーをする。
example_sentences.english: I play soccer with my friend every two days. (at two day intervals)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は会う人ごとに笑顔で握手します。
example_sentences.english: That person greets every person they meet with a smile and a handshake.

example_sentences.japanese: ３時間ごとに水一杯を飲んで下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please drink a glass of water every 3 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生ごとにお土産をもらった。
example_sentences.english: I received a souvenir from each teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: ５時間ごとにこの不味い薬を飲まなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to drink this awful medicine at five hour intervals.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスは私の近所で家ごとにイルミネーションをしている。
example_sentences.english: During Christmas, every house in my neighborhood hangs Christmas lights.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で日本語能力試験が１年ごとに２回行われます。
example_sentences.english: The JLPT is held twice each year in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は運転中、赤信号ごとに、携帯を見る。
example_sentences.english: She looks at her phone at every red light while driving.

example_sentences.japanese: 出来るだけ、１週ごとに漢字を２０字覚えたい。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want to memorize 20 kanji each week.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一週間ごとに実家に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: I go to my parents' home every week. (Every single one)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一週間おきに実家に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: I go to my parents' home every other week. (With 'spaces' or 'gaps' of 1 week)

formation: なるべく + (Action) Phrase
casual_structure: なるべく + (Action) Phrase
explanation: An expression which indicates that (A) should be done as often as possible, or whenever it becomes permissable.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく速く行きます。
example_sentences.english: I will go as fast as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 外に出かけるときはなるべくドアのカギをかけてください。
example_sentences.english: When you go out, lock your doors as often as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事で疲れていても、なるべく夕食は食べてください。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are tired from work, please eat dinner whenever possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はできるだけ早く来てね。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, please make sure to come as early as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はなるべく早く来てね。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, please come as early as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく早めに連絡してください。
example_sentences.english: Please contact me as soon  as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく正直に話してください。
example_sentences.english: Please speak as honestly as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく早めに犯人を捕まえるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: We intend to catch the criminal as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく沢山の人気な場所へ行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to as many famous places as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: なるべくわかりやすく説明してください。
example_sentences.english: Please explain so that it is as easy to understand as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: インフルエンザにかかった時は、なるべくゆっくり休むほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: When you catch the flu, you should rest as much as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行く前になるべくお金を貯めた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Before going to Japan you should save as much money as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 机の上をなるべく綺麗にしたほうが仕事がしやすい。
example_sentences.english: It is easier to work if the top of your desk is as clean as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転している時はなるべく注意してください。
example_sentences.english: While driving, please be as careful as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 死ぬ前になるべく多くの国へ行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to as many countries as possible before I die.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来るので、なるべく綺麗にしてください。
example_sentences.english: We are having guests, so please be sure to make (the house) as tidy as possible.

general_translation: About to, On the verge of
formation: Verb［る］ + ところ + だ
casual_structure: Verb［る］ + ところ + だ
polite_structure: Verb［る］ + ところ + です
explanation: An expression that highlights the situation or place when an action is just about to start.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から帰るところです。
example_sentences.english: I am just about to go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は手紙を書くところだ。
example_sentences.english: He is about to write a letter.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から友達と会うところです。
example_sentences.english: I'm about to meet my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど出かけるところだ。
example_sentences.english: I am about to leave right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪の毛を切るところでした。
example_sentences.english: I was on the verge of cutting my hair. (just about to)

example_sentences.japanese: 出かけるところなので洗い物ができない。
example_sentences.english: I am just about to go out, so I cannot do the dishes.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題をするところで、友達から電話が入った。
example_sentences.english: Just when I was about to do my homework I got a call from a friend.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンの電源を切るところで、あの音を聞いた。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to turn off my computer, I heard that sound.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べるところで、焦げた匂いがした。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to eat, I smelled something burning.

example_sentences.japanese: 番組が始まるところで赤ちゃんが泣いた。
example_sentences.english: Just as the show was about to start, the baby cried.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい言語を習い始めるところです。
example_sentences.english: I am about to start learning a new language.

example_sentences.japanese: 富士山がやっと見えるところでまた天気が悪くなって見えなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Just as we were about to finally see Mt. Fuji, the weather got bad again and it disappeared from view.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が話し手を待っている時、電話：「家から出るところだから、もうすぐ着くよ。」
example_sentences.english: When a friend is waiting on the speaker, phone call: 'I am about to leave home, so I will be there soon.'

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯を食べるところで、友達が家に来た。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to eat dinner, my friend came to my house.

example_sentences.japanese: いまの所...
example_sentences.english: This current place…

example_sentences.japanese: いまのところ...
example_sentences.english: This current situation…

formation: Verb + のに［い］Adjective + のに［な］Adjective + な + のにNoun + な + のに
casual_structure: Verb + のに［い］Adjective + のに［な］Adjective + な + のにNoun + な + のに
explanation: A word that often expresses mild frustration that (A) has not led to (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 無理って言ったのにまだやるの？
example_sentences.english: Even though I said it was impossible, you're still going to do it? (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日テストがあるのに彼は勉強をしないでゲームをしている。
example_sentences.english: Despite having a test tomorrow, he is playing games without studying.

example_sentences.japanese: 何で納豆は臭いのに美味しいの？
example_sentences.english: Why does natto taste good, despite smelling bad?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はイケメンなのにいつも汗臭い。
example_sentences.english: Even though he is a good looking guy, he always smells like sweat.

example_sentences.japanese: この車はスポーツカーなのに遅い。
example_sentences.english: Despite being a sports car, this car is slow.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫歯だのに、チョコレートを食べたから歯が痛い。
example_sentences.english: I ate chocolate even though I have a cavity, so my tooth hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は忙しいのに、ゲームをしている。
example_sentences.english: Despite being busy, he is playing video games. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報は悪かったのに、晴れた。
example_sentences.english: Despite the weather forecast being bad, it was sunny. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: あの女の人はきれいなのに、彼氏がいない。
example_sentences.english: Despite being pretty, that woman doesn't have a boyfriend. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: あまり牛乳がないのにスーパーに行った時買わなかったの？
example_sentences.english: Even though we are running low on milk, you didn't buy any when you went to the store? (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しいのに、駅まで送ってくれるの？ありがとう！
example_sentences.english: You are going to take me to the station even though you are busy? Thank you! (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 君の息子が公園で遊びたがっているのに、公園に行かないの？
example_sentences.english: Despite your son wanting to play in the park, you won't go to the park? (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に行くって言ったのに結局行かない。
example_sentences.english: Although you said that you were going to go to Japan, you're not going after all. (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 鉛筆が必要と書いてあったのに、持って来なかった。
example_sentences.english: Despite it saying that a pencil was required, I didn't bring one. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころほうれん草が好きだったのに、今は嫌い。
example_sentences.english: Despite liking spinach when I was a child, I don't like it now. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は難しいのに、頑張って学んでいる。
example_sentences.english: Despite Japanese being difficult, I am doing my best to learn it. (even though)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は毎日運動をしているのに、だんだん太ってきた。
example_sentences.english: Despite exercising everyday, I am gradually gaining weight. (even though)

formation: Verb + と思（おも）う(1)［い］Adjective + と思（おも）う(1)［な］Adjective + だ + と思（おも）う(1)Noun + だ + と思（おも）う(1)(1) と思（おも）っている
casual_structure: Verb + と思（おも）う(1)［い］Adjective + と思（おも）う(1)［な］Adjective + だ + と思（おも）う(1)Noun + だ + と思（おも）う(1)(1) と思（おも）っている
polite_structure: Verb + と思（おも）います(1)［い］Adjective + と思（おも）います(1)［な］Adjective + だ + と思（おも）います(1)Noun + だ + と思（おも）います(1)(1) と思（おも）っています
explanation: A very common way to express your thoughts or opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: このズボンはいいとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think these pants are good.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、ちょっと遅れるとおもう。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, I think I'm going to be a little late.

example_sentences.japanese: その言い方は酷いとおもうよ。
example_sentences.english: I think the way you said that was harsh.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はあの人が綺麗だとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think that person looks pretty.

example_sentences.japanese: これはフランス語だとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think this is French.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本が安全とおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think Japan is safe. (Ungrammatical Japanese, but quite common)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、雨が降るとおもった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that it was going to rain today.

example_sentences.japanese: そうだとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think so.

example_sentences.japanese: それは凄いとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think that is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: ダメだとおもいますよ。
example_sentences.english: I think it is no good. (Not allowed)

example_sentences.japanese: あの時かっこよかったとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think you were cool at that time.

example_sentences.japanese: このスーツ、君に似合うとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think this suit looks good on you.

example_sentences.japanese: 最新のゲームは高いとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think that the latest video games are expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店に行ったことがあるとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think that I have been to that store before.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカと日本の文化は違うとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think that American and Japanese cultures are different.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明が分かりやすいとおもいました。
example_sentences.english: I thought that the explanation was easy to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は、映画を見に行くとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will go see a movie tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日には退院出来るとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think that I will be able to be discharged from hospital tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: ジェームスは自分が賢いと思っている。
example_sentences.english: James thinks he is smart.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年に新しいオートバイを買いたいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking that I want to buy a new motorcycle next year.

general_translation: Such as, Things like, Etc., And so on
formation: Noun + などNoun + など + の  + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + などNoun + など + の  + Noun
explanation: A word that expresses (A), and things in the same category as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: イタリアやアメリカなどに行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to places such as America and Italy. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつもルームメイトなどの悪口を言っています。
example_sentences.english: He is always badmouthing people, like his roommates.

example_sentences.japanese: この公園では石などを投げないでください。
example_sentences.english: Do not throw rocks and so on in this park.

example_sentences.japanese: フルーツはぶどうなどが好きです。
example_sentences.english: As for fruits, I like grapes and such. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 趣味などを教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me things like your hobbies. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、準備などをするつもりです。
example_sentences.english: From tomorrow, I plan on doing things like preparing. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 数学などを勉強します。
example_sentences.english: I study things like math. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 腰や背中などが痛い。
example_sentences.english: Things like my hips and back hurt. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生などが行きます。
example_sentences.english: People such as college students go. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんはバスなどで来ます。
example_sentences.english: Customers come by things like the bus. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: お土産などを買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought things like souvenirs. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: カレーなどの辛いものが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like spicy things such as curry. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説などを読むのが好き。
example_sentences.english: I enjoy reading things such as novels. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題をしてから、ゲームなどをゆっくりする。
example_sentences.english: After doing my homework, I relax with things like video games. (etc. / and so on)

example_sentences.japanese: 鞄や靴等を川に捨ててはならない。
example_sentences.english: You mustn't discard things such as bags and shoes into the river.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつ等本当にうるさいね。
example_sentences.english: Those people are very noisy, don't you think.

casual_structure: Verb + みたい + だ［い］Adjective + みたい + だ［な］Adjective + みたい + だNoun + みたい + だ

explanation: A confident, yet somewhat casual expression to highlight the way something looks.

example_sentences.japanese: この犬は熊みたいです。
example_sentences.english: This dog looks like a bear.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は雪が降るみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like it will snow tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: そこのプールは浅いみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: That pool over there seems shallow.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は地下鉄が嫌いみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he does not like subways.

example_sentences.japanese: その携帯はパソコンみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: That cellphone looks like a computer.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は今日は来ないみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like senpai is not coming today.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はスポーツ選手みたいな体をしている。
example_sentences.english: He has a body like an athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は有名人みたいです。
example_sentences.english: That person looks like a famous person.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の昼から雨が降るみたいです。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it will rain this afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: あの雲は馬みたい。
example_sentences.english: That cloud resembles a horse. (Looks like)

example_sentences.japanese: あのビルは会社じゃなくて病院みたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like that building is a hospital, and not a company.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあの人が好きみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he likes that person.

example_sentences.japanese: これ、オレンジジュースみたいだけど、違うんだって。
example_sentences.english: This looks like orange juice but (someone said) it is not.

example_sentences.japanese: あの車、戦車みたいだ。
example_sentences.english: That car resembles a tank.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんはまだ留守みたいなので、伝言しましょうか。
example_sentences.english: It seems that my mother is still out. Shall we leave a message?

example_sentences.japanese: この学校の生徒はうるさすぎて、動物園みたいだ。
example_sentences.english: This school's students are so loud it resembles a zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: トムと彼女は喧嘩になって、彼女が出て行ったみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems that Tom and his girlfriend got into a fight and she left.

example_sentences.japanese: この公園で遊んでもいいみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems it is okay to play in this park.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは勉強のしすぎで疲れて、図書館で寝たみたい。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san got tired from studying too much and seems to have fallen asleep at the library.

general_translation: Converting a verb into a noun
formation: Verb + こと
casual_structure: Verb + こと
explanation: A word that transforms whole phrases into single, noun-like expressions.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を話すことは難しい。
example_sentences.english: Speaking Japanese is difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 近所の迷惑になることをしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You should not do things that will cause annoyance to your neighbors. (That which is 'causing a problem in the neighborhood')

example_sentences.japanese: ファックスをすることが嫌い。
example_sentences.english: I dislike things like faxing. (That which is 'faxing')

example_sentences.japanese: お金を使い過ぎないことが大事です。
example_sentences.english: It is important to not use too much money. (That which is 'not using too much money')

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツをすることが好き。
example_sentences.english: I like playing sports.

example_sentences.japanese: ダンスをすることは楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Dancing is fun!

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい声でしゃべらないこと。
example_sentences.english: Not talking loudly.

example_sentences.japanese: フォークじゃなくて、お箸をつかうこと。
example_sentences.english: Not using a fork, using chopsticks.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康にいいのはねることです。
example_sentences.english: Sleeping is good for your health.

example_sentences.japanese: 職場でワープロをつかうことはある？
example_sentences.english: Are there times when you are using a word processor at work?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日日本語を勉強することは楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: Studying Japanese every day is fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 想像することは大切なことです。
example_sentences.english: Using your imagination is important.

example_sentences.japanese: プラスチックをすてることは環境に悪いよ。
example_sentences.english: Throwing away plastic is bad for the environment, you know.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋の中であそぶことはしないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not play in this room. (Not playing in this room)

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん太るから、寝る前に甘いものをたべないことが大事です。
example_sentences.english: Not eating sweets before bed is important because you will rapidly gain weight (if you do).

example_sentences.japanese: 1．クラスメイトをいじめないこと。
example_sentences.english: 1. Do not bully your classmates.

general_translation: Look like, Appear, Seem, Have a feeling that

explanation: A word used to make guesses about appearances, often with low confidence.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪がふりそうです。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it is going to snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は毎日走っていそうだ。
example_sentences.english: She seems like she runs every day.

example_sentences.japanese: これは正しそうだ。
example_sentences.english: This seems correct.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店員は丁寧そうだ。
example_sentences.english: That clerk seems like he is attentive.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の仕事はむずかしそうです。
example_sentences.english: The job of being a teacher looks difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の宿題はかんたんそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Today's homework looks easy.

example_sentences.japanese: その食べ物はたべやすそう。
example_sentences.english: That food looks easy to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: この教科書はとてもむずかしそうです。
example_sentences.english: This textbook seems very difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: けっこう難しいけど、だいじょうぶそうですか？
example_sentences.english: It is pretty hard, does it look like you'll be okay?

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランの寿司はおいしそうです。
example_sentences.english: That restaurant's sushi looks delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの小さい車でもこの駐車場にはいらなそうです。
example_sentences.english: Even your small car doesn't look like it will fit in the parking spot.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカには大きいハンバーガーがありそうですね。
example_sentences.english: It would seem that there are big hamburgers in America.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯でニンニクを食べたら、口が臭くなりそうです。
example_sentences.english: If I eat garlic at dinner, I have a feeling that my breath will become stinky.

example_sentences.japanese: 「仲直りできそうですか？」「いいえ、出来なそうです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Does it look like you can work it out?' 'No, it does not appear so.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの遊園地のジェットコースターはたのしくなさそうです。
example_sentences.english: That amusement park's rollercoaster doesn't seem fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の部屋は汚くなさそうだ。
example_sentences.english: His room doesn't seem messy.

example_sentences.japanese: あの車は小さくて便利じゃなさそう。
example_sentences.english: That car is small and seems inconvenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はもうイギリスに帰らなそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It appears that he is not going back to England.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は朝から雨が降るみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it is going to start raining tomorrow morning. (Higher confidence)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は朝から雨が降りそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like it is going to start raining tomorrow morning. (Lower confidence)

formation: ［い］Adjective［い］+ さ［な］Adjective + さ
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective［い］+ さ［な］Adjective + さ
explanation: An expression that can turn adjectives into nouns that express an amount.

example_sentences.japanese: このうつくしさは初めてです。
example_sentences.english: This beauty is a first for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が道の長さを測ります。
example_sentences.english: I will measure the length of the road. (The road's lengthiness)

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になってから家族の大切さが分かってきた。
example_sentences.english: After becoming an adult, I came to understand the importance of family. (Family's importantness)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のげんきさは子供みたい。
example_sentences.english: His energy is like that of a child.

example_sentences.japanese: このあまさは美味しい。
example_sentences.english: This sweetness is delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 箱のおもさを測ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please weigh the heaviness of the box for me.

example_sentences.japanese: このさむさだけで死ぬよ。
example_sentences.english: Just by this coldness you will die.

example_sentences.japanese: 琵琶湖のふかさって知っている？
example_sentences.english: Do you know the depth of Lake Biwa?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のすばらしさを体験したいよ。
example_sentences.english: I want to experience Japan's greatness.

example_sentences.japanese: 何このきたなさ！早く掃除をしてください。
example_sentences.english: What is this filthiness! Please hurry up and clean it.

example_sentences.japanese: この景色のきれいさは言葉では説明できない。
example_sentences.english: I am unable to explain the prettiness of this scenery with words.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べたことのないあまさのクッキーを作りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to make a cookie that has a sweetness that I have never tasted before.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日食べたラーメンのおいしさを友達に教えたい。
example_sentences.english: I want my friend to know the deliciousness of the ramen I ate yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がやったことのひどさは永遠に忘れない。
example_sentences.english: I will never forget the harshness of what he did.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校からの帰るさにお金を拾った。
example_sentences.english: On the way back from school, I picked up some money. (At the 'point' of returning home)

example_sentences.japanese: 行くさで家に忘れ物をしたことを思い出した。
example_sentences.english: When I was on my way there, I remembered that I had left something at home. (At the 'point' of going somewhere)

general_translation: Among other things, For example, Such as
formation: Verb (A) + とか + Verb (B) + （とか）Adjective (A) + (だ) + とか + Adjective (B) + (だ) +（とか）Noun (A) + とか + Noun (B) + （とか）
casual_structure: Verb (A) + とか + Verb (B) + （とか）Adjective (A) + (だ) + とか + Adjective (B) + (だ) +（とか）Noun (A) + とか + Noun (B) + （とか）
explanation: A word which may be used with either verbs or nouns, to express a variety of non-specific actions or things.

example_sentences.japanese: 青とか水色が好き。
example_sentences.english: I like colors such as blue and light blue. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: 亀とかすっぽんとかは美味しいんですか。
example_sentences.english: Are things like turtles and softshell turtles delicious?

example_sentences.japanese: 健康のために野菜を食べるとか水を飲むとかをしています。
example_sentences.english: For my health, I do things like eat vegetables and drink water.

example_sentences.japanese: かぼちゃとかサツマイモとか白菜とかシイタケが入っている鍋が好き。
example_sentences.english: I like hot pots that include things like pumpkin, sweet potato, cabbage, and shiitake.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日とか今週末とか、暇なら、映画を見に行こう。
example_sentences.english: If you are free tomorrow or, for example this weekend, let's go watch a movie. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: トム・クルーズとかブラッド・ピットとかがかっこいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think people like Tom Cruise for example, or Brad Pitt are cool. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本とか、韓国とかに行ってみたいですね。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to places such as Japan and Korea. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で「th」の音とかはないです。
example_sentences.english: Japanese doesn't have a 'th' sound (among other things).

example_sentences.japanese: 私は色々なフルーツが好きだけど、苺とか、りんごとかは嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: I like a variety of fruits, but I don't like (fruits) such as strawberries and apples.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来るのに、掃除とか、料理とか、何もしていない！
example_sentences.english: Even though we are having guests, I haven't done things such as cleaning or cooking! (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンの中ではとんこつラーメンとか、味噌ラーメンが好きですね。
example_sentences.english: Among (types of) ramen, I like Tonkotsu and Miso (among others). (such as)

example_sentences.japanese: テストを受ける人は、鉛筆とか、消しゴムとかが必要でしょう。
example_sentences.english: People who are going to take a test will need things such as a pencil and an eraser, right? (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: まだ家事とかしなくてはいけないから今日は遊べない。
example_sentences.english: I still have to do things such as cleaning, so I can't hang out. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語はひらがなとか、カタカナとか、漢字もあるから、勉強をするのが大変です。
example_sentences.english: In Japanese, there are things such as hiragana, katakana and kanji that make studying the language tough. (among others)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人凄いね。人の顔を見るだけで性格とか分かるって。
example_sentences.english: That person is amazing. I heard that she can determine someone's personality (among other things) just by looking at their face.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中にあるものを食べるとかしてください。
example_sentences.english: Eat what's in the refrigerator or something. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中にあるものを食べるやしてください。
example_sentences.english: Eat things in the refrigerator or something. (Unnatural Japanese, as や cannot be used with verbs)

casual_structure: こういう + Nounそういう + Nounああいう + Nounどういう + Noun

example_sentences.japanese: そういう人もいるよ。
example_sentences.english: There are also people like that (you know).

example_sentences.english: This is my first time watching a movie like this. (This 'kind' of movie)

example_sentences.japanese: そういう人は嫌い。
example_sentences.english: I don't like people like that. (That 'kind' of people)

example_sentences.japanese: ああいう車に乗ってみたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to try to drive a car like that one. (That 'kind' of car)

example_sentences.japanese: あなたはどういう音楽を聴きますか？
example_sentences.english: What kind of music do you listen to?

example_sentences.japanese: どういう意味ですか。
example_sentences.english: What do you mean? (Literally - What kind of meaning?)

example_sentences.japanese: ああいう消しゴムが好き。
example_sentences.english: I like erasers like that one over there.

example_sentences.japanese: こういう人形がほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want a doll like this.

example_sentences.japanese: こういう仕事をしなくちゃいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to do this kind of job.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうところに行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to a place like that.

example_sentences.japanese: どういうことですか。
example_sentences.english: What do you mean? (in what way / how do you mean?)

example_sentences.japanese: ああいう人になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to become that kind of person.

example_sentences.japanese: こういう車でもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is this kind of car, is it okay?

example_sentences.japanese: そういうプレゼントをあげます。
example_sentences.english: I will give a present like that.

example_sentences.japanese: そういう授業は難しいですね。
example_sentences.english: That kind of class is difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: どういう服をお探しですか？
example_sentences.english: What kind of clothes are you searching for?

example_sentences.japanese: また雨が降っている。今日も野球をするのをあきらめよう。
example_sentences.english: It's raining again. I'll give up on playing baseball today too.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日日本語で話したら、どんどん上手になるから、頑張って日本語ではなそう。
example_sentences.english: If you speak Japanese every day, you will get better in strides, so let's do our best to speak together.

example_sentences.japanese: この店は毎週月曜日がセールだから、牛乳を買うのを月曜日までまとう。
example_sentences.english: Since this store has a sale every Monday, let's wait until Monday to buy milk.

general_translation: It seems that, It appears that, It looks like
formation: Verb + よう + だ［い］Adjective + よう + だ［な］Adjective + な + よう + だNoun + の + よう + だ
casual_structure: Verb + よう + だ［い］Adjective + よう + だ［な］Adjective + な + よう + だNoun + の + よう + だ
polite_structure: Verb + よう + です［い］Adjective + よう + です［な］Adjective + な + よう + ですNoun + の + よう + です
explanation: A semi-formal construction that expresses the manner in which (A) exists.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんど無くなっているようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that most of it is gone.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのプールは深いようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like the pool over there is deep.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに大きなビルが出来るようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like a big building will be made here.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は明日のテストに自信があると皆に言っているが、本当は不安なようだ。
example_sentences.english: He is telling everyone that he is confident about the test tomorrow, but it seems like he is actually worried.

example_sentences.japanese: ヨーダは宇宙人のようだ。
example_sentences.english: Yoda appears to be an alien.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はここに来ないようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he won't come here.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の天気は台風のようだ。
example_sentences.english: Today's weather looks like  a typhoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の話し方は歌っているようだ。
example_sentences.english: His way of speaking seems like singing.

example_sentences.japanese: このコーラは苦い。まるでコーヒーのようだ。
example_sentences.english: This cola is bitter. It tastes like coffee.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はお金を持っていないようだが、本当はお金持ち。
example_sentences.english: That person seems like he doesn't have any money, but he really is rich.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも変な事言っているけど、本当は真面目なようだ。
example_sentences.english: He is always saying strange things, but it appears that he is really a serious person.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は誕生日にグーグルピクセルが欲しいけど、もらえないようだ。
example_sentences.english: I want a Google Pixel for my birthday, but it appears that I won't get one.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は話しにくいようだが、話しやすい。
example_sentences.english: She seems to be difficult to talk to, but she is actually quite friendly.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません！私の荷物を勘違いして、持って行ったようだ。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me! It appears that you have made a mistake and taken my luggage.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手はこの選手より速く走れるようだ。
example_sentences.english: It looks like that athlete can run faster than this athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は先週もらったゲームにもう飽きたようだ。
example_sentences.english: It appears that the child has already grown tired of the game he received last week.

formation: ぜんぜん + Phraseぜんぜん + (Negative) Phrase
casual_structure: ぜんぜん + Phraseぜんぜん + (Negative) Phrase
explanation: A casual way to express that something is not (A) at all, but also often used in positive phrases in modern Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 着物がぜんぜん似合わない。
example_sentences.english: Kimonos don't look good on me at all.

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、トイレットペーパーがぜんぜんない。
example_sentences.english: Oh shoot, I don't have any toilet paper at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は家事の手伝いをぜんぜんしなかったので別れました。
example_sentences.english: I broke up with her because she didn't help out at all with house chores.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月もお金がぜんぜん無いからパンだけを食べる。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any money this month either, so I am only eating bread.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日後輩からもらったお土産は全く美味しくありませんでしたね。
example_sentences.english: The souvenir we got from our junior member yesterday was not tasty at all, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: ぜんぜん頑張りたいと思わない。
example_sentences.english: I don't feel like trying at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はぜんぜん英語を話せないです。
example_sentences.english: I can't speak English at all.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたはぜんぜん理解が出来ていないね。
example_sentences.english: You don't understand at all do you?

example_sentences.japanese: 今、機嫌が悪くて、ぜんぜん嬉しくならない。
example_sentences.english: I'm in a bad mood right now and there's no way at all I'll become happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の髪型はぜんぜん好きじゃないから、明日切りに行く。
example_sentences.english: I don't like my current hair style at all, so I'll go get my hair cut tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故にあったけど、私はぜんぜん大丈夫。
example_sentences.english: I was in an accident, but I am completely fine.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が何言っているかぜんぜん分からないんですけど。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand what you are saying at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の競争にぜんぜん自信がない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any confidence about tomorrow's competition at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の締め切りにはぜんぜん間に合わなそう。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't look like I will make tomorrow's deadline at all. (Not even close)

example_sentences.japanese: この川の水はぜんぜん綺麗じゃない。
example_sentences.english: This river's water is not clean at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と話さない方がいいよ。ぜんぜん気分が良くないみたい。
example_sentences.english: You had better not talk to him. He is not in a good mood at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日？全然いいよ！
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow? That's completely fine!

formation: Sentence + かな
casual_structure: Sentence + かな
explanation: A word used to casually express uncertainty, or soften personal opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ食べに行くかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if we will go eat soon...

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が道の真ん中で倒れてるけど、大丈夫かな。
example_sentences.english: That person over there is laying collapsed in the middle of the street, but I wonder if they are okay.

example_sentences.japanese: このコンロにこの魚が入るかな？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if the fish will fit in this stove.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は運動をした方がいいかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder, if I should exercise tomorrow...

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末に友達と会えるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if I can meet my friends this weekend...

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫にケーキまだあるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if there is still cake in the fridge.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんは何をくれるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what my mom will give me.

example_sentences.japanese: 松本さんは図書館に居るかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if Matsumoto-san is at the library.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は何を考えているのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what you are thinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 大分元気になったから、薬は飲まなくていいかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it is okay not to take any medicine because I feel much better.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉が居ないから、誰かとどこかに行ったのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if my older sister went somewhere with someone because she is not around.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は外国人と付き合ったことがあるのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if she has ever dated a foreigner.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の日本語は上手だね。日本に行った事があるのかな。
example_sentences.english: That person's Japanese is really good, don't you think? I wonder if that person has been to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: ユウキがあそこのレストランが美味しいって言っていたけど、本当に美味しいのかな。
example_sentences.english: Yuki said that that restaurant was good, but I wonder if it really is or not.

example_sentences.japanese: この通帳はお母さんのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if this is my mother's checkbook. (Slightly masculine)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は本当に弁護士なのかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that person is really a lawyer. (Commonly used by anybody)

general_translation: Not very, Not much, Not really, Hardly
formation: あまり(1) + Verb［ない］あまり(1) + ［い］Adjective［ない］あまり(1) + Noun + ではない(2)あまり + ［な］Adjective + ではない(2)(1) あんまり(2) じゃない
casual_structure: あまり(1) + Verb［ない］あまり(1) + ［い］Adjective［ない］あまり(1) + Noun + ではない(2)あまり + ［な］Adjective + ではない(2)(1) あんまり(2) じゃない
explanation: A structure indicating that (A) is not an excessive amount, or being done excessively.

example_sentences.japanese: このケーキはあまり美味しくない。
example_sentences.english: This cake isn't very delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はどこもあまり平和ではない。
example_sentences.english: Recently, nowhere has been very peaceful.

example_sentences.japanese: そこの肉屋の肉はあまりいい肉ではない。
example_sentences.english: Meat from that butcher over there is hardly good.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時間だったらあまり並ばないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: At this time, I think we would not have to stand in line for very long.

example_sentences.japanese: 私には犬がいるからあまり寂しくない。
example_sentences.english: I have a dog, so I don't feel lonely very much.

example_sentences.japanese: あまり肉を食べない。
example_sentences.english: I don't eat very much meat.

example_sentences.japanese: あまり大変なことではないから、心配いらないよ。
example_sentences.english: It is not really a big deal, so you don't have to worry. (isn't that)

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司をあまり食べたいと思わない。
example_sentences.english: I don't really think I want to eat sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字の意味があまり分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't really understand the meaning of this kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と時間を過ごすのはあまり好きではない。
example_sentences.english: I don't enjoy spending time with him very much.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の気持ちをあまり理解していないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that she doesn't really understand how I feel.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は彼の事をあまり考えていない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't been thinking about him very much recently.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりいい車ではないけど、走れるからいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: This car is hardly great, but it runs so that's good enough, right? (not that great)

example_sentences.japanese: あまり好きじゃない食べ物もたまに食べなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes you also have to eat food that you don't really enjoy.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明してくれたけど、あまり意味が分からない。
example_sentences.english: You provided an explanation, but I don't really understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の授業がとても分かりやすかったけど、テストの点数があまり良くなかった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's class was really easy to understand, but my test scores were not very good.
