explanation: A grammar point that expresses hypothetical situations and their potential, sometimes expected outcomes.

example_sentences.japanese: ヘルメットをかぶらなければ、バイクに乗れない。
example_sentences.english: If (you) do not wear a helmet, then (you) cannot ride a motorbike.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事を辞めれば自由時間が増えるけど、お金が無くなる。
example_sentences.english: If I quit work, I will have more free time, but I will have no money.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が止めば、今日も釣りに行くつもりです。
example_sentences.english: If it stops raining, I intend to go fishing today also.

example_sentences.japanese: そこの信号で右に曲がれば病院に着きます。
example_sentences.english: If you turn right at the light just there, you will get to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 店に電話をすれば、すぐに予約ができるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you call the store, you will be able to make a reservation immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつがくればパーティーが楽しくなると思う。
example_sentences.english: If he comes to the party, I think it will be more fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 頭が痛ければ、薬を飲んで寝た方がいい。
example_sentences.english: If your head hurts, it would be better if you take some medicine and then sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメン屋のチャーハンが不味ければ、そこのラーメンも不味いだろう。
example_sentences.english: If a ramen shop's fried rice tastes bad, then the ramen probably tastes bad too, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 刺身が嫌いならば 、寿司も嫌いでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you do not like sashimi, then you probably don't like sushi either, right?

example_sentences.japanese: バイクならば、バイク専用の駐輪場に止めてください。
example_sentences.english: If it's a motorcycle, please park it in the designated bike parking lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が作ったクッキーを食べたくなければ、捨ててもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't want to eat the cookie that I made, you can throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: カレーが辛くなければ、いっぱい食べれる。
example_sentences.english: If the curry isn't spicy, I can eat a lot of it.

example_sentences.japanese: トラックの運転手でなければ、この仕事の辛さが分からない。
example_sentences.english: If you aren't a truck driver, then you wouldn't understand the hardships of this job.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホがあれば、財布はいらない。
example_sentences.english: If one has a smartphone, they don't need a wallet.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日サッカーの練習にいけば、プロのサッカー選手になれる。
example_sentences.english: If you go to soccer practice every day, then you can become a professional soccer player.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週の金曜日までにできなければ、来週末に終わらせなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: If (you) cannot do it by this Friday, then (you) have to finish it next weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 展覧会にいけば、色々なことを学べる。
example_sentences.english: If (you) go to an exhibit, then (you) can learn a variety of things.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報をみれば、明日の天気が分かるだろう。
example_sentences.english: If (you) look at the weather forecast, then (you) will know tomorrow's weather (yeah?).

example_sentences.japanese: 地図をよくみれば迷子にならないから、よく見てね。
example_sentences.english: Since you won't get lost if you look at the map well, please look properly.

example_sentences.japanese: そのコーヒーを好きでなければ、この飲み物も絶対好きじゃないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you do not like that coffee, then you most certainly will not like this drink.

example_sentences.japanese: この本をよめば、日本の文化が分かる。
example_sentences.english: If you read this book, then you will understand Japan's culture.

example_sentences.japanese: 丁寧にはなせば、面接がうまく行くと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: If you speak politely, then I think that your interview will go well.

example_sentences.japanese: ＬＥＤをつかえば、電気代が大分減ります。
example_sentences.english: If you use LEDs, then your electric bill will go down greatly.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日運動をして、プロテインをのめば、筋肉が増えると思う。
example_sentences.english: If you exercise every day and if you drink protein shakes, then you will gain muscle.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をすれば痩せるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you exercise, you will lose weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜遅くに電話をされると迷惑です。
example_sentences.english: It is very inconsiderate of you to call this late at night.

general_translation: Were it, If, If it's the case, As for (Conditional)
formation: Verb＋（の）＋なら（ば）［い］Adjective＋（の）＋なら（ば）［な］Adjective＋なら（ば）Noun＋なら（ば）
casual_structure: Verb＋（の）＋なら（ば）［い］Adjective＋（の）＋なら（ば）［な］Adjective＋なら（ば）Noun＋なら（ば）
explanation: A phrase that expresses something hypothetical, but is often used in same way as は.

example_sentences.japanese: 君なら、できる。
example_sentences.english: If it's you, you can do it. (if it is the case)

example_sentences.japanese: デザートなら何でも食べられます。
example_sentences.english: If it is a dessert, I can eat anything. (If it is dessert, I like anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎に住むのならば、車を買ったほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to live in the countryside, it would be better to buy a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いのならば、ジャケットを着るといいだろう。
example_sentences.english: If it is cold, you should wear a jacket.

example_sentences.japanese: 無理ならいいよ。
example_sentences.english: If it is not possible, it's okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の車を使うなら、いつ使うか教えてください。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to use my car, please let me know when.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いなら、その上着を脱いでください。
example_sentences.english: If you are hot, please take off that jacket.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことなら、聞かなくていい。
example_sentences.english: If it's something like that, you don't have to ask. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題が難しいなら、一緒にしよう。
example_sentences.english: If the homework is hard, let's do it together. (if it is the case)

example_sentences.japanese: また行くなら、帰って来ないでください。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to go again, please don't come back. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いなら、扇風機を点けてください。
example_sentences.english: If it's the case that it is hot, please turn on the fan.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か言いたい事があるなら、言えば？
example_sentences.english: If you have something that you want to say, then how about you say it?

example_sentences.japanese: 切手を買いたいなら、郵便局に行ってきて。
example_sentences.english: If you want to buy stamps, go to the post office. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツをしているなら、鍛えているでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If it's the case that you are playing sports, you are training, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行くなら、おみやげを買ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: If you are going on a trip, please buy me some gifts. (if it is the case)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から日本語の勉強を始めるなら、教科書を買ってください。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to start studying Japanese tomorrow, please buy a textbook. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語のことなら、先生に聞いた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: As for Japanese, it would be better if you asked the teacher. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいおもちゃが欲しいなら、自分のお金で買ってね。
example_sentences.english: If you want a new toy, buy it with your own money. (in the case of)

example_sentences.japanese: 練習をするなら、漢字を書くのが上手になる。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to practice, you will get good at writing kanji. (Unnatural Japanese, as becoming 'good' is a natural result of practicing)

general_translation: To feel, To think, To act as if, To want, To desire
formation: ［い］Adjective［い］+ がる［な］Adjective + がる
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective［い］+ がる［な］Adjective + がる
polite_structure: ［い］Adjective［い］+ がります［な］Adjective + がります
explanation: A word that describes the way that others are acting, or may be feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の猫はこわがる。
example_sentences.english: My cat is jumpy. (Acts scared)

example_sentences.japanese: キムは新しいパソコンをほしがっている。
example_sentences.english: Kim is wanting a new computer.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも女の子の前では強がるけど友達の中では彼は一番の怖がりだ。
example_sentences.english: He always acts tough in front of girls, but amongst our friends he is the biggest scaredy-cat.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が嫌がる事をしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You must not do anything that the dog would not like.

example_sentences.japanese: トムはこの新しいゲームを欲しいと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I think Tom would want this new game.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人、寒がっている。ジャケット着ればいいのに。
example_sentences.english: That person seems like they feel cold. It would be better if he wore his jacket. (Natural Japanese, as がる shows how he 'appears to be acting', rather than what he is actually feeling)

example_sentences.japanese: この子はいつも新しいおもちゃを欲しがる。
example_sentences.english: This kid always wants new toys.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟はつよがる。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother acts tough.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子はゲームをほしがる。
example_sentences.english: That kid (always) wants games.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画を見て、おもしろがっています。
example_sentences.english: Watching a movie and showing signs of interest.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の車をほしがる人はいないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I don't think that anyone feels like they want your car.

example_sentences.japanese: はずかしがらないで。スピーチが上手だったよ。
example_sentences.english: Don't feel ashamed. Your speech went well.

example_sentences.japanese: 飼い猫を外に出してみれば？おもしろがるよ！
example_sentences.english: Why don't you try letting your cat outside? It seems like they'd enjoy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の時宇宙人のことをこわがっていた。
example_sentences.english: When they were a child they felt terrified of aliens.

example_sentences.japanese: いやがっているから、ちょっと離れて。
example_sentences.english: He doesn't like (that). Give him a bit of space. (showing signs of distaste)

example_sentences.japanese: 家の子供たちは家事の手伝いをいやがっている。
example_sentences.english: Our kids show signs of distaste to helping with house chores.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めての飛行機なので怖いと思うけど、こわがらないでね。
example_sentences.english: This is your first time on an airplane so I think it might be scary, but please don't act scared.

example_sentences.japanese: 今Ｎｉｎｔｅｎｄｏスイッチを持っている人は皆ゼルダの伝説ブレスオブザワイルドをほしがっているだろう。
example_sentences.english: Everyone who has a Nintendo Switch now is wanting The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はいつも人の前では強がる。
example_sentences.english: I always act tough in front of people. (I probably always appear to act tough)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は今、犬をほしがっているけど、マンションに住んでいるからまだ飼えない。
example_sentences.english: Right now, I am wanting a dog, but since I live in an apartment, I can't get one yet. (I am currently acting like I want a dog)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人、暑がっているね。
example_sentences.english: That person looks like they are hot, don't you think. (They're acting like they're hot)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人、暑そうだね。
example_sentences.english: That person looks like they are hot, don't you think. (They seem hot)

general_translation: To give off, Smell, Sound, Taste, Sensation
formation: Noun + が + する
casual_structure: Noun + が + する
polite_structure: Noun + が + します
explanation: An expression used to highlight that something is causing a specific sensory experience, or that that sense is going.

example_sentences.japanese: 車の音がする。
example_sentences.english: A car is making a sound.

example_sentences.japanese: この石鹸はバラの匂いがするから好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like this soap because it smells like roses. (Literally, 'it gives off a rose smell')

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かが階段を上がっている音がする。
example_sentences.english: I hear someone coming up the stairs. (Literally, 'the sound of someone coming up the stairs is being made')

example_sentences.japanese: このバナナが変な味がする。
example_sentences.english: This banana tastes weird. (Literally, 'it gives off a strange flavor')

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かに見られている感じがする。
example_sentences.english: It feels like I'm being watched by someone. (Literally, 'the feeling of being watched is happening')

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋はコーヒーの匂いがします。
example_sentences.english: This room is giving off a coffee smell.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は塩の味がします。
example_sentences.english: This food gives off a salty taste.

example_sentences.japanese: 変な味がするのでこれを捨てます。
example_sentences.english: This gives off an odd flavor, so I will throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: お砂糖を入れ過ぎたから、甘い味がする。
example_sentences.english: I put too much sugar in, so it gives off a sweet taste.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が吹いて、いい匂いがした。
example_sentences.english: As the wind blew, it made a good smell.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがギターを弾いている音がする。
example_sentences.english: The sound of someone playing the guitar can be heard. (Literally 'the sound is being made')

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが料理しているでしょう。いい匂いがします。
example_sentences.english: Mom is cooking, right? It's making a nice smell.

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーは苦い味がするから、お砂糖を入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Because this coffee gives off a bitter taste, please use sugar.

example_sentences.japanese: この食べ物は嫌な味がするので、犬にあげましょう。
example_sentences.english: Since this food gives off an unpleasant taste, let's give it to the dog.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人と一緒に居るだけで、変な感じがする。
example_sentences.english: Just being with him gives off a weird feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: 爆発音がしたから、テーブルの下に隠れた。
example_sentences.english: Because the sound of an explosion rang out, I hid under the table.

example_sentences.japanese: ヤバい、鍵をかけるのを忘れた気がする。
example_sentences.english: Shoot, I feel like I forgot to lock my door. (Literally, 'my attention is being drawn to that I may have forgotten to lock the door')

example_sentences.japanese: なんか忘れた気がする。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I forgot something. (Literally, 'my attention is being drawn to that something was forgotten')

formation: Noun + を + しているNoun + を + する
casual_structure: Noun + を + しているNoun + を + する
polite_structure: Noun + を + していますNoun + を + します
explanation: An expression used to describe wearing accessories or similar items. It is also sometimes used to describe a person’s facial expression or appearance.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜はメガネをしています。
example_sentences.english: I wear glasses at night.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は優しそうな顔をしているけど、本当は意地悪な人なんです。
example_sentences.english: That person has a kind face, but they are actually a mean person.

example_sentences.japanese: 黒い髪で、目が大きくて、ゴールドの指輪をしている女性を探しています。
example_sentences.english: I am looking for a woman with black hair, big eyes, who is wearing a gold ring.

example_sentences.japanese:
娘：「お母さん、どうして悲しそうな顔をしているの？」
母：「大丈夫よ。ごめんね。」
example_sentences.english:
Daughter: 'Mom, why do you have a sad expression?' 
Mother: 'I'm fine. Sorry.'

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは太くていい声をしているので、歌手になれると思う。
example_sentences.english: Because my dad has a deep and nice voice, I think he could become a singer.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこに立っている手袋をしている男の人を知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know the man standing over there who is wearing gloves?

example_sentences.japanese: 青い目をしている猫を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a cat that has blue eyes.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人が暗い顔をしているので、たくさんのチョコレートをあげました。
example_sentences.english: My friend had a gloomy expression, so I gave them a lot of chocolate.

example_sentences.japanese: 正月にサンタが家に来たので、子供たちはびっくりした顔をしていました。
example_sentences.english: Because Santa came to the house on New Year's, the children had surprised expressions.

example_sentences.japanese: 明るい性格をしている人が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like people who have a cheerful personality.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は細くて長い足をしているので、みんなに見られます。
example_sentences.english: Because I have long, thin legs, everyone looks at me.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は特別なデートの日に赤いネクタイをするけど、それをもう３回も見ているよ。
example_sentences.english: My older brother wears a red tie on special date days, but I have already seen it three times.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はすぐ怒った顔をする。
example_sentences.english: She quickly makes an angry face.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の猫は僕がベッドに行く時、泣きそうな顔をする。
example_sentences.english: My cat has an expression like it is about to cry when I go to bed.

example_sentences.japanese: 親戚の子供が悲しそうな顔をして、「それ、僕のアイス。」と言った。
example_sentences.english: My relative's child had a sad expression and said, 'That's my ice cream.'

example_sentences.japanese: 兄はきれいな声をしています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother has a beautiful voice.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人は赤い時計をしている。
example_sentences.english: The criminal is wearing a red watch.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のお母さんは大きい目をしています。
example_sentences.english: My mother has big eyes.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は鼻にピアスをしています。
example_sentences.english: She has a nose piercing.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は困った顔をしています。
example_sentences.english: He has a troubled expression.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は毎日白い靴下を履いています。
example_sentences.english: I wear white socks every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は仕事でスーツを着ています。
example_sentences.english: My father wears a suit for work.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は高い声がある。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister has a high voice. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が怒った顔をしています。
example_sentences.english: The teacher has an angry expression.

formation: Verb［たい］+ がる
casual_structure: Verb［たい］+ がる
polite_structure: Verb［たい］+ がります
explanation: A phrase used to make guesses about what others want to do, or speak in the third person.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は動物園にいきたがる。
example_sentences.english: He is acting like he wants to go to the zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: ジョンはなんでいつも悪口を言いたがるんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why John always wants to talk badly about people.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆は彼が作ったケーキを食べたがる。
example_sentences.english: Everyone always wants to eat the cakes that he makes.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘はいつもスポーツをしたがる。
example_sentences.english: My daughter always wants to play sports.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は最近の映画をみたがる。
example_sentences.english: My girlfriend wants to see a recently released movie.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子がかえりたがるならいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: If that kid wants to go home, that's alright, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はパソコンをかいたがって、週末も働いた。
example_sentences.english: He wanted to buy a PC, so (and) he even worked weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: リサがあのサンドイッチを見て、たべたがった。
example_sentences.english: Risa saw that sandwich and wanted to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆はポップコーンをたべたがると思う？
example_sentences.english: Do you think that everyone wants to eat popcorn?

example_sentences.japanese: 君のようになりたがっている人が居ますよ。
example_sentences.english: There are people that are wanting to become like you, you know.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームをしたがる子供には外で遊んでもらった方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think it's better for children who want to play video games to play outside instead.

example_sentences.japanese: 使いやすいアプリを作れば、皆がつかいたがる。
example_sentences.english: If you make an app that is easy to use, everyone will want to use it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語を勉強したがるから、きっと上手になるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: He wants to study Japanese, so he will surely become proficient, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 皆が楽しんでいたから、レナもしたがると思った。
example_sentences.english: Because everyone was having fun, I thought that Rena also would want to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はこのステーキを食べたがる。
example_sentences.english: He wants to eat this steak. (He acts like he wants to)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にこのステーキを食べてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want him to eat this steak. (I want him to)

example_sentences.japanese: 田中君は新しいゲームを見つけると、そのゲームをほしがる。
example_sentences.english: When Tanaka-kun sees a new game, he always wants it.

formation: Verb + かもしれない［い］Adjective + かもしれない［な］Adjective + かもしれないNoun + かもしれない
casual_structure: Verb + かもしれない［い］Adjective + かもしれない［な］Adjective + かもしれないNoun + かもしれない
polite_structure: Verb + かもしれません［い］Adjective + かもしれません［な］Adjective + かもしれませんNoun + かもしれません
explanation: A phrase that expresses uncertainty, but is also frequently shortened.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: そうかもね。
example_sentences.english: That might be right.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年から観光客が増えるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: From next year, the number of tourists might increase.

example_sentences.japanese: あの建物は教会かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: That building might be a church.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は無理かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It might not be possible today.

example_sentences.japanese: そこの池は深いかもしれないから気を付けてね。
example_sentences.english: That lake over there might be deep, so please be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は休むかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I might take the day off tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は休みだからドライブするかも。
example_sentences.english: I have a day off tomorrow, so I might go for a drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を家に忘れてきたかもしらん。
example_sentences.english: I might have left my wallet at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は夜遅くまで仕事があるから、行かないかもしれん。
example_sentences.english: I have to work late tomorrow night, so I probably won’t go.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がまた遅れるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: She might be late again.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年アメリカに行くかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I might go to America next year.

example_sentences.japanese: このいい服を買えば、人気になるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: If I buy these nice clothes, then I might become popular.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことを言わないほうがいいかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It is maybe better to not say such things.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は何も調べないで、日本に行くかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: He might go to Japan without researching anything.

example_sentences.japanese: この時期は晴れの日が続くから、富士山を綺麗に見られるかも。
example_sentences.english: This time of year has a surplus of clear weather days, so you might be able to see Mt. Fuji clearly.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は専門家だから、説明が分かりやすいかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: He is an expert so his explanation might be easy to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の近くにある寿司屋より、こっちの寿司屋のほうが美味しいかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: This sushi restaurant might be more delicious than the one close to my house.

example_sentences.japanese: あの鞄は本当にあの人のものかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: That bag might actually be that person's bag.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近勉強してないから、明日のテスト落ちるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't been studying recently, so I might fail the test tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はこんな綺麗なものを見たことがないから、面白がるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: That person has never seen something so beautiful before, so she might feel fascinated.

example_sentences.japanese: このいい服を買ったら、人気になるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: If I buy these nice clothes, I might become popular.

formation: Verb + みたいに + Verb(1)Noun + みたいに + Verb(1)Noun(2) + みたいな + Noun(1) Adverb、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(2) Verb
casual_structure: Verb + みたいに + Verb(1)Noun + みたいに + Verb(1)Noun(2) + みたいな + Noun(1) Adverb、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective(2) Verb
explanation: A somewhat casual expression that confidently highlights the way something looks, or is acting.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあの女の人みたいになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to become like that woman.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はイルカみたいに、速く泳ぎたいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: He is saying that he wants to swim fast like a dolphin.

example_sentences.japanese: プロみたいに泳ぎたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to swim like a professional.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生みたいになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be like my teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生みたいな人になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to become someone like my teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 関西みたいな所に住みたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to live in a place like the Kansai region.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はイルカみたいに泳ぎたいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: He is saying that he wants to swim like a dolphin.

example_sentences.japanese: それは城みたいな家です。
example_sentences.english: That is a castle-like house.

example_sentences.japanese: 魚みたいに泳ぎたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to swim like a fish.

example_sentences.japanese: サンダルみたいに履きやすい。
example_sentences.english: They are easy to put on, just like sandals. (similar to)

example_sentences.japanese: お金持ちの人みたいな生活をしたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to live a life similar to a rich person.

example_sentences.japanese: 卵みたいに割れやすい。
example_sentences.english: Easy to crack, just like an egg.

example_sentences.japanese: サンドイッチみたいに、パンに挟んだ。
example_sentences.english: I sandwiched it between two pieces of bread, similar to a sandwich.

example_sentences.japanese: 山が砂みたいに崩れた。
example_sentences.english: The mountain crumbled like sand.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は冬みたいな天気ですよね。
example_sentences.english: Today's weather is like winter, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: こういちみたいに、日本語を教えたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to teach Japanese, just like Koichi.

example_sentences.japanese: 上手になりたいから、日本人みたいに漢字ドリルで漢字を練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Because I want to get better (at Japanese), I am practicing Kanji with Kanji drills like Japanese people.

explanation: An expression used when something seems to look a certain way, but the speaker isn't sure.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: これがはいりそうな箱はある？
example_sentences.english: Is there a box that looks like it might fit this?

example_sentences.japanese: さっき、先輩が怒りそうになってた。
example_sentences.english: Earlier, it seemed like senpai was going to get angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は忙しそうに仕事をしている。
example_sentences.english: He is working like he is busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はどんな仕事でも簡単そうにやるからうらやましいです。
example_sentences.english: She does all her work like it is easy, so I am very jealous of her.

example_sentences.japanese: つまらなそうなパーティーには行きません。
example_sentences.english: I don't go to parties that seem like they would be boring.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨がふりそうな日ですね。
example_sentences.english: It looks like today is going to be a rainy day doesn't it.

example_sentences.japanese: やさしそうに犬を撫でた。
example_sentences.english: She pet the dog in a way that seemed affectionate.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はわかりやすそうな説明をしたが、まだ理解ができない。
example_sentences.english: He gave an explanation that seemed easy to understand, but I still don't get it.

example_sentences.japanese: つまらなそうな話は聞きたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to hear a story that sounds boring.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は、たのしそうな授業をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は美味しくなさそうにご飯を食べている。
example_sentences.english: He is eating his food like it does not taste good.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は鳥のように自由だ。

example_sentences.english: My younger sister is spoiled rotten like a grandchild.

example_sentences.english: My siblings ate the food until it was completely gone similar to a pack of wolves.

grammar_point: う・よう + と思（おも）う
general_translation: I think I will, I think I shall, Going to, Gonna (Volitional + と思う)
formation: Verb［よう］ + と思（おも）う(1)(1) と思（おも）っている
casual_structure: Verb［よう］ + と思（おも）う(1)(1) と思（おも）っている
polite_structure: Verb［よう］ + と思（おも）います(1)(1) 思（おも）っています
explanation: A phrase that expresses when someone thinks that they are resolved to do (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、勉強をしようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will study tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームはもうあきらめようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will give up on this game already. (I have arrived at the conclusion that I will give it up)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は明日から電車で通おうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I shall commute by train from tomorrow. (I have arrived at the conclusion that I will do it)

example_sentences.japanese: 来月、バイクを買おうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will buy a bike next month. (I have arrived at the conclusion that I will buy one)

example_sentences.japanese: 今晩はレストランで美味しいものを食べようとおもっているけど、ナオミも来る？
example_sentences.english: I am thinking of eating something delicious at a restaurant tonight, but do you want to come too, Naomi?

example_sentences.japanese: タケル、お前は絶対サチコと別れようとおもっているでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Takeru, you are definitely thinking of breaking up with Sachiko, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、家をかおうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will buy a house next year.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰ってから、お菓子をたべようとおもいます。
example_sentences.english: I think I will eat candy after returning home.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日から文法の勉強をはじめようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I think I will start studying grammar from today.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はレゴを欲しがっているから、かってあげようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: My son wants lego, so I think I will buy him some.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳がないから、スーパーにいこうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: There is no milk, so I think I will go to the store.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫に入っているチーズを誰も食べないから、たべようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: Since no one is going to eat the cheese in the refrigerator I think I will eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: この週末は雪がいっぱい降るから、スキーをしにいこうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: This weekend it will snow a lot, so I think I will go skiing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は家事をしたくないから、弟にしてもらおうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to do housework, so I think I will have my little brother do it for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 後でクッキーをつくろうとおもっているけど、あなたも一緒に作る？
example_sentences.english: I am thinking I will make cookies later, but do you want to make them with me?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は面白そうなテレビ番組があるから、みようとおもう。
example_sentences.english: There is a TV program on today that looks interesting, so I think I will watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が説明をしてくれたことがあまり分からなかったから、後で先生にきこうとおもう。
example_sentences.english: I didn't really understand what the teacher was explaining, so I think I will ask the teacher about it later.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は彼女にあまく話しかけた。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供がしずかに遊んでいる。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は自慢話をあつく語った。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は古い本をたいせつに使った。

example_sentences.japanese: 母が部屋をきれいに片づけた。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理をかるく味見した。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はしんせつに道を教えてくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉はていねいにプレゼントを作った。
example_sentences.english: My older sister carefully made the present.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験前の夜ははやめに寝たほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: You should go to bed early the night before an exam.

example_sentences.english: To close tightly.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しく買う。
example_sentences.english: To buy new.

example_sentences.japanese: 丁寧に書く。
example_sentences.english: To write neatly.

example_sentences.english: To sing well.

formation: ［い］Adjective［く］+ は［い］Adjective［く］+ は + ない［い］Adjective［く］+ は + ある

example_sentences.japanese: この映画はおもしろくはない。
example_sentences.english: This movie isn't exactly interesting.

example_sentences.english: My fingers aren't exactly thin.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのコーヒーはおいしくはない。
example_sentences.english: The coffee over there isn't exactly delicious.

example_sentences.english: Senior: 'Are you busy tomorrow?' Junior: 'I'm not exactly busy tomorrow, but...'

example_sentences.english: My girlfriend isn't exactly cute, but she has a good personality.

example_sentences.japanese: そのニュースを聞いてうれしくはないよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm not exactly happy to hear that news.

example_sentences.japanese: 面接官：「あの子、わるくはないけど何かが足りないのよね。」
example_sentences.english: Interviewer: 'That kid isn't exactly bad, but they are missing something.'

example_sentences.english: I am not exactly close with the wife next door, but I know she sings with all her might in the bath every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 家からコンビニまでとおくはないのに、夏は暑すぎてよくウーバーイーツを頼みます。
example_sentences.english: It isn't exactly far from my house to the convenience store, but the summer is too hot so I often order Uber Eats.

example_sentences.english: It isn't exactly difficult to find the culprit who drank my coffee, but it is a complicated problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 母：「子供が一人暮らしを始めてさびしくはあるけど、一人の時間も楽しいよ。」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'It *is* lonely since my child started living alone, but alone time is fun too.'

example_sentences.japanese: 父：「あのゲームが欲しいのか？」息子：「別にほしくはないよ。ただ見ているだけ。」
example_sentences.english: Father: 'Do you want that game?' Son: 'I don't especially want it. I'm just looking.'

example_sentences.japanese: このコートはあたたかくはないです。

example_sentences.japanese: 父はきびしくはあるが、愛がある人だ。

example_sentences.japanese: このチョコレートは甘くはない。
example_sentences.english: This chocolate isn't exactly sweet.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は働いてはいる。
example_sentences.english: He *is* working.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の部屋は広くない。
example_sentences.english: My room is not spacious.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の部屋は広くはない。
example_sentences.english: My room isn't exactly spacious (but it is big enough for what I need).

example_sentences.japanese: 私の彼氏は優しくはないけど、背が高いんです。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend isn't exactly kind, but he is tall.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は楽しくはないけど……。
example_sentences.english: Work isn't exactly fun, but...

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のベッドは古くはあるけど、気に入っています。
example_sentences.english: My bed *is* old, but I like it.

example_sentences.japanese: これは桜の木ではない。
example_sentences.english: This is *not* a cherry tree.

general_translation: Adjective + する, To make something/someone (more)
formation: ［な］Adjective + に + する［い］Adjective［く］+ するNoun + に + する

example_sentences.japanese: 頑張って部品をちいさくしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try your best to make the parts smaller.

example_sentences.english: Is there any way to make this building more durable?

example_sentences.japanese: 汚い部屋を綺麗にするのは大変だ。

example_sentences.japanese: 風呂を熱くするよ。いい？

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーを甘くするために、砂糖をください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me sugar to make this coffee more sweet.

example_sentences.japanese: 布団をあたらしくしたから気持ちいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 歯医者さんで歯をしろくしてもらった。
example_sentences.english: I had the dentist make my teeth whiter. (Literally - Do white)

example_sentences.japanese: お花見にはあたたかくして行った方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You should make yourself warm when going to a flower-viewing party. (Literally - Do warm)

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋をおおきくしたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to make this room bigger. (Literally - Do big)

example_sentences.japanese: 昼休みをみじかくして早く帰りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to make my lunch break shorter and go home earlier. (Literally - Do short)

example_sentences.japanese: 翻訳をおもしろくするアプリがある。
example_sentences.english: There is an app that makes translating (more) fun. (Literally - Do fun)

example_sentences.japanese: 法律をあたらしくしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want them to renew (make new) the law. (Literally - Do new)

example_sentences.japanese: 庭をげんきにするアイデアはない？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any ideas on how to make the yard (more) healthy? (Literally - Do healthy)

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命しんせつにしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: (They) went all out to make (themselves) generous (for me). (Literally - Do kindness)

example_sentences.japanese: 顔をくろくしすぎです。

example_sentences.japanese: もっと簡単にべんりにする方法がありますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜の花火は綺麗だといいなぁ。

example_sentences.english: I have been busy lately, so I hope I have this weekend off.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝に荷物が届くといいんだけど。（今夜から雪が降るから配達が大変そう）
example_sentences.english: I hope my package arrives tomorrow morning. (However, it is going to start snowing tonight, so delivery seems like an issue)

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじに当たるといいんだが。（一枚しか買っていないから当たらないと思う）
example_sentences.english: I hope I win the lottery. (But since I only bought one ticket, I don't think I will)

general_translation: To reach the point that, To come to be that, To turn into
formation: Verb［できる］(1) + ように + なる(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［る］
casual_structure: Verb［できる］(1) + ように + なる(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［る］
polite_structure: Verb［できる］(1) + ように + なります(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［る］
explanation: A grammar point that expresses something becoming the manner or style of (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと英語を勉強すれば、話せるようになる。
example_sentences.english: If you study English diligently, then you will reach a point where you can speak it.

example_sentences.japanese: 速く走れるようになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to reach the point where I can run faster.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、漢字の練習をすれば綺麗に漢字を書けるようになります。
example_sentences.english: If you practice kanji every day, you will reach the point where you can write them neatly.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年から現金が使えないようになる。
example_sentences.english: From next year, it will reach the point where you will not be able to use cash.(Starting next year, you will not be able to use cash)

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から会社で喫煙できないようになります。
example_sentences.english: Starting next month, it will reach the point where you will not be able to smoke at the company. (Starting next month, smoking will be banned)

example_sentences.japanese: 泳げるようになった。
example_sentences.english: I reached the point that I was able to swim.

example_sentences.japanese: 理解出来るようになった。
example_sentences.english: I reached the point that I could understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理ができるようになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to reach a point where I can cook.

example_sentences.japanese: １００メートルを１０秒で走れるようになった。
example_sentences.english: I reached the point that I could run 100 meters in 10 seconds.

example_sentences.japanese: そうするようになったが、もうそうしたくない。
example_sentences.english: I reached the point that I would do it, but I don't want to anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前はお金が足りなかったけど、スマートフォンを買えるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Before, I didn't have enough money, but I have reached the point where I can buy a smartphone. (Afford)

example_sentences.japanese: 皆があの人はもう歩けないと言っていたが、歩けるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Even though everyone said that he would never walk again, he reached the point that he could walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 前はだめでしたが、納豆を食べられるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Before, I couldn't, but I reached the point that I can eat natto.

example_sentences.japanese: どんどん日本語を聞き取れるようになってきた。
example_sentences.english: I've reached the point where I can pick up (spoken) Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日勉強をしたから、日本語を上手に話せるようになった。
example_sentences.english: I studied everyday, so I reached the point that I could speak Japanese competently.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は何か決める時に、誰かに相談するようになった。
example_sentences.english: I have come to the point of discussing it with someone whenever I will decide on something.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪を綺麗にカット出来るようになるのが夢です。
example_sentences.english: It is my dream to reach the point where I can cut my hair nicely.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分から行動が出来るようになってください。
example_sentences.english: Please turn into someone who can act on their own. (Please become more self sufficient)

general_translation: Almost every ~, Nearly every ~, On a ~ basis
formation: 毎（まい） + Time Expression + のように
casual_structure: 毎（まい） + Time Expression + のように
explanation: A grammar point which highlights when something is done in the manner of every (A), but not necessarily every (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: ともきさんは仕事前にまいにちのように釣りに行った。
example_sentences.english: Tomoki-san went fishing almost every day before work.

example_sentences.japanese: まい日のようにポテトチップス食べてるから太ってきた。
example_sentences.english: Because I eat potato chips almost every day, I am starting to gain weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 渋谷にはまい週のように行っているよ。
example_sentences.english: I go to Shibuya almost every week.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は８月になるとまい年のように平和記念資料館へ行く。
example_sentences.english: When August comes, he goes to the peace memorial museum almost every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事を終わったときはまいばんのようにジムに行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the gym nearly every night when I finish work.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は彼に出会う前は、まいにちのように高校をサボっていた。
example_sentences.english: Before she met him, she used to skip school almost every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はその後、故郷に まいつきのように帰った。
example_sentences.english: After that, he returned to his hometown almost every month.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では まいとしのように少なくとも１回は地震が起こる。
example_sentences.english: There is at least 1 earthquake in Japan nearly every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、雨に濡れてひどい風邪を引いたので、出かけるときはまいかいのように傘を持っていく。
example_sentences.english: Since I caught a terrible cold after getting soaked when I was a kid, I take an umbrella with me almost every time I go out.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はまいにちのように砂糖を食べすぎたので、病気になった。
example_sentences.english: He fell ill because he ate too much sugar nearly every single day.

example_sentences.japanese: そのころ、私の父は昇進したのでまいしゅうのように出張をし始めた。
example_sentences.english: Around that time, because my father got promoted, he started going on business trips nearly every week.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のＩＳＰはＩＰアドレスが足りていないので、ユーザーはまいあさのようにインターネットに接続が出来なくなる。
example_sentences.english: Because my ISP does not have enough IP addresses, users lose internet connection almost every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏にはまいばんのようにコオロギの鳴き声が聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: In summer, you can hear the chirping of crickets almost every evening.

example_sentences.japanese: １０歳になってからはまいとしのようにお父さんと一緒に初日の出を見に行った。
example_sentences.english: Nearly every year since I was 10, I went to see the first sunrise with my father.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は死ぬまでまいつきのように彼女の墓の上にバラを置いた。
example_sentences.english: He put a rose on her grave nearly every month until his death.

formation: Phrase + じゃない + か
casual_structure: Phrase + じゃない + か
explanation: A casual phrase that presents negated questions.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: そのことじゃなかったか。
example_sentences.english: It was about that, wasn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: キヨコはもうすぐ来るんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Isn't Kiyoko coming soon?

example_sentences.japanese: そのカメラは高いんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: That camera is expensive, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: この着物は綺麗じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: This kimono is beautiful, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの車は私の車より速いじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Your car is faster than my car, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: これは台風の影響ではないか。
example_sentences.english: This is the typhoon's effect, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 遊んでないで明日のテストの勉強をした方がいいんではないか。
example_sentences.english: Without mucking around, wouldn't it be better if you studied for the test tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: もう終わるんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: It is already over, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: あれカメラじゃないか！
example_sentences.english: Isn't that a camera!?

example_sentences.japanese: 次の駅で降りるんじゃないか？
example_sentences.english: The next station is the one we get off at, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: この橋を渡るのが怖いんじゃないか？
example_sentences.english: It is scary crossing this bridge, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日１２時ごろ帰って来たんじゃないか？
example_sentences.english: You came home around midnight last night didn't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせに来るのが早いんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You came a little early for the meeting, didn't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日日本語を勉強したほうがいいんじゃないか？
example_sentences.english: Wouldn't it be better to study Japanese today?

example_sentences.japanese: ハイキングに行くならリュックサックが必要じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: If you are going hiking, a rucksack is needed, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのお母さんは九時までに帰ってきてと言っていたじゃないですか。
example_sentences.english: Didn't your mom tell you to be home by nine?

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いたの？明日旅行に行くんじゃないか？
example_sentences.english: You caught a cold? Isn't it that you leave for a trip tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手が勝ったじゃないか。どうしてメダルをもらっていないんだ？
example_sentences.english: Isn't that the player that won? Why didn't he get a medal?

formation: Verb + らしい［い］Adjective + らしい［な］Adjective + らしいNoun + らしい
casual_structure: Verb + らしい［い］Adjective + らしい［な］Adjective + らしいNoun + らしい
polite_structure: Verb + らしい + です［い］Adjective + らしい + です［な］Adjective + らしい + ですNoun + らしい + です
explanation: A structure that presents a presumption based on information about (A) having the appearance that one would expect of (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はダイエットを続けるらしいです。
example_sentences.english: He seems likely to continue his diet.

example_sentences.japanese: ねえ、聞いた？タケシ君がキヨミちゃんにプロポーズするらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Hey, did you hear? It seems that Takeshi-kun is proposing to Kiyomi-chan.

example_sentences.japanese: カシキさんの彼氏はカッコいいらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Kashiki-san's boyfriend is handsome.

example_sentences.japanese: タカギ先輩がさっき言っていた事は本当らしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently the thing that Takagi senpai was talking about earlier is true.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はフランス人らしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that person is French.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、新聞で読んだんだけど、明日から雪が降るらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I read this in the newspaper this morning, but it appears as though it is going to start snowing tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は姉のタイプじゃないらしい。
example_sentences.english: It appears that he is not my older sister's type.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの元彼女が婚約したらしいです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that your ex-girlfriend got engaged.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は会社の社長らしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he is a president of a company.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を話せなくても、日本に行けるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that you can go to Japan even if you cannot speak Japanese. (It seems like you can)

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領がキューバに行くらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the president is going to Cuba. (It appears that he is going)

example_sentences.japanese: ブックオフに沢山の安い漫画があるらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like there are many cheap mangas at Bookoff.

example_sentences.japanese: 明々後日退院出来るらしい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he will be discharged (from hospital) in three days time. (It appears that he will be discharged)

example_sentences.japanese: 魔王さまはしばらくマクロナルドで働いていたらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the Demon King worked at McRonald for some time.

example_sentences.japanese: また中東で戦争が起こるらしい。信じられない。
example_sentences.english: It seems like there is going to be another war in The Middle East. I can't believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: O型（血液）は誰にでも使えるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the O bloodtype can be used by anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風が日本の西の方に向かうらしい。
example_sentences.english: It appears that the typhoon is going towards the western part of Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは本当に男らしいね。
example_sentences.english: You are really manly, aren't you. (You exhibit the typical qualities of a man)

example_sentences.japanese: やっと１１月らしい天気になったね。
example_sentences.english: The weather is finally becoming November-like, don't you think? (Weather that is typical of November)

formation: Verb［て］+ おくVerb［て］ +とく
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ おくVerb［て］ +とく
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ おきますVerb［て］ + ときます
explanation: A grammar point that expresses an action done either to enable or prevent something else.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: ここにリモコンをおいておくね。
example_sentences.english: I will put the remote here (in advance for future use).

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前に食器を洗っておく。
example_sentences.english: Before sleeping, I will wash the dishes in advance. (So that it does not need to be done later)

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの財布を鞄に入れておきます。
example_sentences.english: I am going to put your wallet in your bag. (So that you won't forget it later)

example_sentences.japanese: 予約しておくね。
example_sentences.english: I am going to make a reservation in advance. (So that the bookings don't fill up while we wait)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日歯を磨いておくと、虫歯が防ぎます。
example_sentences.english: If you brush your teeth everyday (in advance), you will be able to prevent cavities. (That may or may not come in the future)

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとしらべておきます。
example_sentences.english: I will do a little research in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰ってくるのが遅くなるから、ご飯をつくっておいた。
example_sentences.english: I won't get home until late, so I made food in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日のパーティーのためにジュースをかっておきました。
example_sentences.english: I bought juice (in advance) for the party tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜明日のお弁当をつくっておいてくれますか？
example_sentences.english: Will you make tomorrow's bento (in advance) for me tonight?

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行く前にトイレにいっておく。
example_sentences.english: Before going on a trip I will go to the bathroom in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカに帰る前に円をドルにかえておく。
example_sentences.english: Before returning to America, I will change my yen into dollars in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週までに漢字を３０字おぼえておかなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: By next week, I have to memorize 30 kanji in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫でひやしておいていたコーラを二つください。
example_sentences.english: Could I have two of the colas that were being chilled (in advance) in the refrigerator?

example_sentences.japanese: またバカなことしないで、ちゃんとおぼえておこうね。
example_sentences.english: Don't do something stupid again. Let's remember this (experience) well in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 後でスーパーに行くの？お菓子をいっぱいかっておいて。
example_sentences.english: You are going to the store? Please buy a lot of snacks (in advance for future eating).

example_sentences.japanese: 砂漠に入る前に水を沢山のんでおいた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Before you go into the desert, you had better drink a lot of water in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 暖房をつけておいたから、家が暖かい。
example_sentences.english: I turned on the heater in advance, so the house is warm.

example_sentences.japanese: 机の上に明日の旅行に必要なパスポートを置いとくね。
example_sentences.english: I am going to leave the passport we need for the trip tomorrow on top of the table in advance. (So that I won't forget it later)

example_sentences.japanese: 水筒に水を汲んどくね。
example_sentences.english: I am going to fill this thermos up with water in advance. (So that it is available when I am thirsty)

general_translation: To want something, To be in need of
formation: Noun + が + ほしい
casual_structure: Noun + が + ほしい
polite_structure: Noun + が + ほしい + です
explanation: A common structure that identifies things that are desired.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 機会がほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want a chance.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車がほしいけど、今はお金が無いから買えない。
example_sentences.english: I want a new car, but I don't have any money right now, so I can't buy one.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬がほしいけどスペースが無い。
example_sentences.english: I want a dog, but I don't have space.

example_sentences.japanese: 君がほしい！
example_sentences.english: I want you!

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がほしくないです。
example_sentences.english: I don't want a cat.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はいい服などがほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want things such as nice clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 使いやすい箸がほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want chopsticks that are easy to use.

example_sentences.japanese: あの綺麗な着物がほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want that beautiful kimono.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いから、手袋がほしい。
example_sentences.english: Because it is cold, I want some gloves.

example_sentences.japanese: 誕生日にお金がほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want money for my birthday.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、もっと時間がほしかった。
example_sentences.english: I wanted more time yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、子犬がほしくなった。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I have come to want a puppy. (I want [a/an] + became)

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスに、乗りやすい自転車がほしい。
example_sentences.english: For Christmas, I want a bicycle that is nice/easy to ride.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい靴より、新しいカバンの方がほしい。
example_sentences.english: More than new shoes, I want a new bag.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのラーメン屋の餃子を食べたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat gyoza from that ramen shop over there.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼氏に大事にしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want my boyfriend to treat me like I am important.

formation: Verb［て］+ ほしい
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ ほしい
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ ほしい + です
explanation: A phrase which expresses that the speaker wants someone else to do something.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 車できてほしかった。
example_sentences.english: I wanted you to come by car.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一回説明してほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want you to explain it one more time.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆に俺が書いた漫画を読んでほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want everyone to read the manga that I wrote.

example_sentences.japanese: コーラをかってほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want you to buy (me) a cola.

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒にサッカーをしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to play soccer with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒にたべにいってほしいんです。
example_sentences.english: I want you to go out to eat with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日お弁当をつくってほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want you to make me a bento every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が言ったことをかんがえてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to think about what I said.

example_sentences.japanese: 「どうぞ、食べてください」っていってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to say, 'Please, eat.'

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に勉強してほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want you to study together with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅いから、とまってほしい。
example_sentences.english: Because it is late, I want you to stay the night.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯したり、掃除したりしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to do things like laundry and cleaning.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ家を出ていないので、まっていてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I haven't left the house yet, so I want you to wait. (State of waiting)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にこのお金をあげてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to give him this money.

example_sentences.japanese: キヨミがタケルに家事を手伝ってほしいと言っていた。
example_sentences.english: Kiyomi told Takeru that she wants him to help with chores.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってほしいの？
example_sentences.english: You want me to help you?

formation: Phrase + と聞（き）いたVerb + と聞（き）いた［い］Adjective + と聞（き）いた［な］Adjective + （だ） + と聞（き）いたNoun + （だ） + と聞（き）いた
casual_structure: Phrase + と聞（き）いたVerb + と聞（き）いた［い］Adjective + と聞（き）いた［な］Adjective + （だ） + と聞（き）いたNoun + （だ） + と聞（き）いた
polite_structure: Phrase + と聞（き）きましたVerb + と聞（き）きました［い］Adjective + と聞（き）きました［な］Adjective + （だ） + と聞（き）きましたNoun + （だ） + と聞（き）きました
explanation: A phrase that specifically expresses that you have heard something from someone or somewhere.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はテストがあるときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that there is a test tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年から先輩が私と同じマンションに住むときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that starting next year, my senpai is going to live in the same apartment that I do.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道の冬は、沖縄の冬より寒いときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that winter in Hokkaido is colder than winter in Okinawa.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達からあなたは歌うのが上手だときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard from a friend that you are good at singing.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の息子がもう大学生だときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the son of the company president is already a college student.

example_sentences.japanese: これは無理だときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this is impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは旅館に行ったことがないときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Tom has never been to a ryokan.

example_sentences.japanese: 市内にあるスーツ屋が安いときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that suit shops in the city are cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 近くの映画館のスクリーンが一番大きいときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the screens at the movie theater nearby are the biggest.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故の原因はスピード違反だとききました。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the cause of the accident was speeding.

example_sentences.japanese: 水族館のイルミネーションが素晴らしいときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the light display at the aquarium is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供を育てるのは大変ときいた。それは本当なのか？
example_sentences.english: I heard that raising children is tough. Is that really true?

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのイタリアンレストランがあまり美味しくないときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that Italian restaurant over there isn't very delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 宮崎駿監督がもう映画を作らないときいたけど。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Hayao Miyazaki won't be making any more movies.

example_sentences.japanese: 家事とか、洗い物とか、全部彼氏がしているときいた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that her boyfriend does all the stuff like housework and laundry.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が陸上部に入ったときいたから、僕も入りたくなった。
example_sentences.english: Because I heard that my senior (senpai) joined the track and field team, it made me want to join.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは泳ぐのが下手と聞いたけど、本当なの？
example_sentences.english: I heard that you are bad at swimming, but is that true?

example_sentences.japanese: あれが世界一高い山と聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that mountain over there is the tallest in the world.

general_translation: To be audible, To sound (like), (Can) hear, To be heard
formation: Noun + が + 聞（き）こえる［い］Adjective［く］+ 聞（き）こえる［な］Adjective + に + 聞（き）こえるNoun + に + 聞（き）こえる
casual_structure: Noun + が + 聞（き）こえる［い］Adjective［く］+ 聞（き）こえる［な］Adjective + に + 聞（き）こえるNoun + に + 聞（き）こえる
polite_structure: Noun + が + 聞（き）こえます［い］Adjective［く］+ 聞（き）こえます［な］Adjective + に + 聞（き）こえますNoun + に + 聞（き）こえます
explanation: An expression highlighting that (A) is audible, due to it making some specific sound. Does not require concentration to hear.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 「今のノックきこえた？」「ううん、きこえなかったよ。空耳じゃない？」
example_sentences.english: 'Did you hear a knock just now?''Nope, I didn't hear it. Aren't you hearing things?'

example_sentences.japanese: 車の音がきこえる。
example_sentences.english: I can hear the sound of a car.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメに出てくる女の子の声は可愛くきこえるけど、声優はいつもおばさんだ。
example_sentences.english: Voices of girls that appear in anime sound cute, but the voice actor is always an old lady.

example_sentences.japanese: こう歌うと上手にきこえる。
example_sentences.english: If you sing like this, you will sound good.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の音のようにきこえるけどあれは隣の人のいびきだ。
example_sentences.english: It sounds like the noise from a train, but it's the neighbor's snoring.

example_sentences.japanese: 「西山さんは生まれつき耳がきこえないんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Nishiyama has been deaf since birth.'

example_sentences.japanese: 隣のセキくんはうるさすぎるわよ。彼が音楽を聴くときいつもあたしのアパートにきこえるわ！
example_sentences.english: My neighbor Seki is too loud! Whenever he listens to music, I can hear it in my flat!

example_sentences.japanese: 「教師の声が小さすぎるから何もきこえないんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'The teacher is too quiet, so I cannot hear anything.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「外がうるさいからテレビの音がよくきこえない。」
example_sentences.english: 'Since it is loud outside, I cannot hear the TV very well.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「滝の音はすごく大きくてここからでもきこえます！」
example_sentences.english: 'The sound of the waterfall is really loud, and we can hear it even from here!'

example_sentences.japanese: 子牛は生まれた直後から耳がきこえるが、子猫はきこえない。
example_sentences.english: A calf can hear from birth, but kittens cannot (hear).

example_sentences.japanese: 試験官：「皆さん、録音がハッキリきこえますか？」
example_sentences.english: Examiner: 'Can everybody hear the recording well?'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女：「最近、私、パレオを買ったの。」彼氏：「パレオ？なんだ、それ？食べ物の名前のようにきこえるぞ。」
example_sentences.english: Girlfriend: 'Recently, I bought pareo.'Boyfriend: 'Pareo? What is that? It sounds like the name of a food.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「この店の中だと何もきこえないけど、階段を上がってロビーに行けば、電話がよくきこえるよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I can't hear anything inside this shop, but if I go upstairs to the lobby, I can hear you well on the phone.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はミサカとシライだけにきこえるように小声で言った。
example_sentences.english: He spoke in a low voice so that only Misaka and Shirai could hear him.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今の音、僕には小さな足音にきこえたよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'The sound just now sounded like small footsteps to me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 静かな部屋にいると聞こえるよ。
example_sentences.english: You can hear it if you are in a quiet room. (Without effort)

example_sentences.japanese: 静かな部屋にいると聞けるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are in a quiet room, you can hear it. (If you focus and try to hear the sound)

general_translation: To be visible, To seem, To be in sight
formation: Noun + が + 見（み）える
casual_structure: Noun + が + 見（み）える
polite_structure: Noun + が + 見（み）えます
explanation: A phrase showing that (A) is something that is visible and in plain sight. Does not require searching to see.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: 「遠すぎるから書かれていることがみえないよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Because it is too far, I cannot see what is written there.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの仕事は大変にみえるけど、簡単らしいよ。
example_sentences.english: That job looks difficult, but I heard that it is easy.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋からは富士山がみえます。
example_sentences.english: Mount Fuji can be seen from this room.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠くに建物がみえるけどあれは何？
example_sentences.english: I can see a building in the distance, but what is it?

example_sentences.japanese: パンツがみえるくらいズボンを下げて、先生に怒られた。
example_sentences.english: I sagged my pants to the point where my underwear was visible, and I got scolded by my teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: ここからだと小さくみえるけど、あのビルは１３０メートルもある。
example_sentences.english: From here, the building looks small, but it is 130 meters tall.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの看板は大きいので、どこからでもよくみえる。」
example_sentences.english: 'Since that signboard is big, it can be seen from anywhere.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「富士山はとても大きいから遠くからでもよくみえる！」
example_sentences.english: 'Mount Fuji is very big, so it can be clearly seen even from afar!'

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がやんで、今でははっきりとみえるよ♪
example_sentences.english: I can see clearly now, the rain is gone♪

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎は都会より明かりが少ないから星がよくみえる。
example_sentences.english: There is less light in the countryside than in cities, so stars are clearly visible.

example_sentences.japanese: 目がみえない人は聴覚が鋭い。
example_sentences.english: Blind people often have a sharp sense of hearing. (Literally - People who cannot see)

example_sentences.japanese: 子犬は生まれた直後は目がみえない。
example_sentences.english: Puppies cannot see immediately after being born.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験官：「皆さん、黒板の文字がハッキリみえますか？」
example_sentences.english: Examiner: 'Can everybody see the letters on the blackboard well?'

example_sentences.japanese: 「目にごみが入って何にもみえないよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Dust got into my eye and I cannot see anything!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「ベッドの下など、みえない所もきれいに掃除しましょう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Let's also thoroughly clean places that cannot be seen, like under the bed.'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は遠くからよくみえるように反射ベストを着ている。
example_sentences.english: Police officers wear reflective vests so that they are visible from afar.

example_sentences.japanese: 「東京タワーのみえる部屋を予約したいのですが。」
example_sentences.english: 'I would like to book a room with a view of Tokyo Tower.'

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋を暗くして外を見たら、星が見えるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you make your room dark and look outside, you will see the stars. (Even without trying, you will see them)

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋を暗くして外を見たら、星が見られるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you make your room dark and look outside, you will see the stars. (If you focus past the clouds, and give your eyes some time to adjust)

example_sentences.japanese: 若い時に大きな怪我をしたからなにも見えない。
example_sentences.english: Because of a big injury when I was young, I cannot see anything at all.

general_translation: To suddenly begin, To start doing
formation: Verb［stem］+ だす
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ だす
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ だします
explanation: An expression that highlights that (A) starts suddenly, or unintentionally.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は急になきだした。
example_sentences.english: That child suddenly started crying.

example_sentences.japanese: 最初から速く走りだすのは体に良くない。
example_sentences.english: It is not good for your body to suddenly start running fast.

example_sentences.japanese: 転んだ息子が泣きだす前に、あめをあげる。
example_sentences.english: I give my son candy before he bursts into tears after falling.

example_sentences.japanese: 面白いことを今おもいだした。
example_sentences.english: I suddenly remembered something funny.

example_sentences.japanese: 晴れていたのに、雨が急にふりだした。
example_sentences.english: Although it was clear, it suddenly began raining.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜中に夫が急に餃子をつくりだした。
example_sentences.english: My husband suddenly started to make dumplings in the middle of the night.

example_sentences.japanese: 何も言わないではしりだした。
example_sentences.english: Without saying a word, he suddenly began running.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語が出来ないと思っていたのに、日本語でしゃべりだした。
example_sentences.english: Although I thought that he couldn't speak any Japanese, he suddenly started speaking in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は公園に行きたかったが、雨がふりだしたから家でゲームをする。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to go to the park today, but because it started raining, I am going to play video games at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 乾杯と言わないで、のみだした。
example_sentences.english: Without saying 'cheers', I started drinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は答えをいいだす時に、くしゃみをした。
example_sentences.english: He sneezed just as he started to say the answer. (sudden)

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官が後ろを向いた時に犯人がにげだした。
example_sentences.english: When the police officer turned her back, the criminal suddenly began to run away.

example_sentences.japanese: 一番悲しいシーンで彼がわらいだした。
example_sentences.english: He suddenly started laughing at the most somber scene.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りは子供が多いので、急にとびだしてくることがあります。
example_sentences.english: There are many children in this area, so there are times when they suddenly jump out (e.g. in front of cars). (start to)

example_sentences.japanese: コンサートで歌手が歌を歌い始める。
example_sentences.english: At the concert, the singer will start singing. (Something that has been planned to be started)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、友達が授業中に歌いだした。
example_sentences.english: Recently, my friend suddenly burst into song during class. (Something that happened without any prior plan/expectation)

formation: Decade of age + 代だいDecade + 年代ねんだい
casual_structure: Decade of age + 代だいDecade + 年代ねんだい
explanation: A suffix highlighting a specific group of years, eras, or generations.

example_sentences.japanese: 街頭インタビュー、通行人：「１９８０ねんだいころからここに住んでいます。」
example_sentences.english: Street interview, passerby: 'I have been living here since (around) the 1980s.'

example_sentences.japanese: １０だいの頃によく怒られたよ。
example_sentences.english: I was scolded often when I was in my teens.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は２０だいの頃に沢山旅行をしました。
example_sentences.english: I traveled a lot in my twenties.

example_sentences.japanese: 六十だいの方はこちらにお並びください。
example_sentences.english: People in their sixties, please line up over here.

example_sentences.japanese: ７０年だいの音楽が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like music from the 70s.

example_sentences.japanese: ８０年だいのファッションはかっこいい。
example_sentences.english: Fashion from the 80s is cool.

example_sentences.japanese: 証人が警察官に言う：「泥棒は３０だい半ばだったと思います。」
example_sentences.english: A witness speaks to a policeman: 'I think that the thief was in their mid-thirties.'

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞記事：「Ｘさんは昭和５０ねんだいの終わりごろにお金持ちになった。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper article: 'Mr. X became rich toward the end of the 50s of the Showa era.'

example_sentences.japanese: 漫画のナレーター：「イラめぐみは３０だい前半で次長になった。」
example_sentences.english: Manga narrator: 'Megumi Ira became vice-director in her early thirties. '

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞記事：「２０１０ねんだいの終わりからハイエンドスマホの値段が上がり始めた。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper article: 'High-end smartphone prices started growing since the late 2010s.'

example_sentences.japanese: 就職の面接：「彼はプログラミングを４０だい後半に学び始めましたが、スキルがあると思います。」
example_sentences.english: Job interview: 'Even though he started learning to program in his late forties, I think he is skilled.'

example_sentences.japanese: 映画博物館のサイトのカテゴリ：「アメリカ映画の誕生から−１９８０ねんだいまで」
example_sentences.english: Category on the film museum website: 'From the birth of American film - till the 1980s.'

example_sentences.japanese: 孫：「おじいちゃんには、６０だいで引退して、７０だいはのんびりしてほしい。」
example_sentences.english: Grandchild: 'I want grandpa to retire in his his sixties, and spend his seventies relaxing.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が話している：「あのバスケットボールチームが最も強かったのは、１９８０ねんだいの終わりですね。」
example_sentences.english: Friends are talking: 'That basketball team was the strongest in the late 1980s.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「１０だいの若者は両親や教師の言うことを聞かなくてはいけない。」
example_sentences.english: 'Young people in their teens have to listen to the things that their parents and teachers say.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「武道アニメが初めて人気になったのは１９８０ねんだい半ばだった。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/thesis: 'Martial arts anime became popular for the first time in the mid-1980s.'

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんがおじいちゃんに言う：「一人でそれをするな！もう４０だいじゃないから。」
example_sentences.english: Grandmother speaks to grandfather: 'Don't do it by yourself! You are not in your forties anymore!'

example_sentences.japanese: 新生代は哺乳類時代とも言われています。
example_sentences.english: The Cenozoic era is also known as the era of mammals.

example_sentences.japanese: 第５代将軍徳川綱吉はとても有名な将軍です。
example_sentences.english: The fifth shogun, Tokugawa Tsunayoshi, is a very famous shogun.

formation: Noun + が + かかるAmount + かかる
casual_structure: Noun + が + かかるAmount + かかる
polite_structure: Noun + が + かかりますAmount + かかります
explanation: An intransitive verb that indicates the burden or the conditions necessary to complete something. Mainly used in sentences about money or time.

example_sentences.japanese: たける：「飛行機代、いくらかかった？」あつし：「意外と安くて、往復で５万円だったよ！」
example_sentences.english: Takeru: 'How much did the airfare cost?' Atsushi: 'It was surprisingly cheap, it was 50,000 yen for a round trip!'

example_sentences.japanese: この大学は、授業料だけで毎年８０万円かかる。
example_sentences.english: This university costs 800,000 yen every year just for tuition.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家から祖父の家まで、車で４時間かかります。
example_sentences.english: It takes 4 hours by car from my house to my grandfather's house.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京からカナダまで飛行機で１２時間かかるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: I hear it takes 12 hours by plane from Tokyo to Canada.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は３時間半かかるから、飲み物とかポップコーンとか買って行こう！
example_sentences.english: This movie takes 3 and a half hours, so let's buy drinks and popcorn before we go!

example_sentences.japanese: 前は、パスポートを作るまでの準備に時間がかかったが、今回はスマホで書類を頼んだので簡単だった。
example_sentences.english: Before, it took time to prepare to get a passport, but this time it was easy because I requested the documents on my smartphone.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい子供部屋の用意に３ヶ月かかる。
example_sentences.english: It will take 3 months to prepare the new children's room.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越しはお金がかかる。
example_sentences.english: Moving costs money.

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂のお湯が沸くまで２０分かかるので、その間に犬の散歩をしました。
example_sentences.english: It takes 20 minutes for the bathwater to heat up, so I took the dog for a walk in the meantime.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店のパンは大きすぎて、食べ終わるまでに１時間かかる。
example_sentences.english: The bread at that shop is so big that it takes an hour to finish eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: あの島までは船で３０分かかります。
example_sentences.english: It takes 30 minutes by boat to get to that island.

example_sentences.japanese: 客：「近くのスーパーまでどのくらいかかりますか？」オーナー：「歩いて５分ですよ！」
example_sentences.english: Customer: 'How long does it take to get to the nearby supermarket?' Owner: 'It's 5 minutes on foot!'

example_sentences.japanese: コンビニで現金を下ろすたびに手数料が２５０円かかる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I withdraw cash at a convenience store, it costs a 250 yen fee.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校まで３０分かかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes 30 minutes to get to school.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は化粧に１時間かかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes my daughter an hour to do her makeup.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外旅行はお金がかかる。
example_sentences.english: Traveling overseas costs money.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は時間がかかる。
example_sentences.english: This dish takes time (to cook).

example_sentences.japanese: 駅まで３時間かかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes 3 hours to get to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術に１００万円かかります。
example_sentences.english: The surgery costs 1,000,000 yen.

general_translation: Cost (money), Run you about (a certain price)
formation: Noun + が(1) + Price + するいくら + する(1)は
casual_structure: Noun + が(1) + Price + するいくら + する(1)は
polite_structure: Noun + が(1) + Price + しますいくら + しますか(1)は
explanation: A verb used to express the value of a specific object. Often used to emphasize that something is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: このイチゴは１個１，０００円します。
example_sentences.english: These strawberries run you about 1,000 yen each.

example_sentences.japanese: このバッグは５万円する。
example_sentences.english: This bag costs 50,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランはランチが３千円する。
example_sentences.english: Lunch at that restaurant costs 3,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: この時計は１０万円です。
example_sentences.english: This watch is 100,000 yen. (Neutral statement of fact)

example_sentences.japanese: このワンピースは２０万円する。
example_sentences.english: This dress will run you 200,000 yen. (Specifically noting the price)

example_sentences.japanese: この自転車はいくらしますか？
example_sentences.english: How much does this bicycle cost?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で１５０円のおにぎりが海外で５００円する。
example_sentences.english: A rice ball that is 150 yen in Japan will run you 500 yen overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の１億円する時計を落として祖母に怒られました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my grandfather's watch that costs 100 million yen and got yelled at by my grandmother.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式で８０万円するドレスを着ました。
example_sentences.english: I wore a dress that cost 800,000 yen at my wedding.

example_sentences.japanese: これは１０本で５００円する鉛筆です。
example_sentences.english: These are pencils that run you about 500 yen for 10.

example_sentences.japanese: 今はスマホが１台２０万円する時代だ。
example_sentences.english: We are in an era where a single smartphone runs you about 200,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: ５千円するぬいぐるみは買いたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to buy a stuffed animal that costs 5,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外に来た記念に３万円するディナーを食べました。
example_sentences.english: To commemorate coming overseas, I ate a dinner that cost 30,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔、タバコは１箱２００円だったのに今は６００円する。
example_sentences.english: In the past, a pack of cigarettes was 200 yen, but now it costs 600 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: ５０万円するベッドをリサイクルショップで３０万円で買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a bed that normally costs 500,000 yen for 300,000 yen at a thrift store.

example_sentences.japanese:
たくや：「５千円するランチって高すぎるよ。」
かな：「私もそう思う。」
example_sentences.english:
Takuya: 'A lunch that runs you about 5,000 yen is too expensive.'
Kana: 'I think so too.'

example_sentences.japanese:
あさみ：「このカバン高そうだね…。」
けいこ：「うん…。値段は…１００万円するって！！！」
example_sentences.english:
Asami: 'This bag looks expensive...'
Keiko: 'Yeah... They say the price...costs 1 million yen!!!'

example_sentences.japanese: 道で倒れていたお爺さんを助けて、お礼に５千万円する車をもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I helped an old man who had collapsed on the street, and as a thank you I received a car that costs 50,000,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 一泊７００万円するホテルに泊まった。
example_sentences.english: I stayed at a hotel that costs 7,000,000 yen a night.

example_sentences.japanese: 母の着けているスカーフは８千円する。
example_sentences.english: The scarf my mom is wearing costs 8,000 yen.

formation: Number + Counter + も
casual_structure: Number + Counter + も
explanation: A phrase that expresses surprise about the number of something.

example_sentences.japanese: １０万円も払わなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to pay as much as 100,000 yen!

example_sentences.japanese: １２時間も仕事をしたから疲れた。
example_sentences.english: I worked as long as 12 hours, so I am tired.

example_sentences.japanese: その携帯２０万円もしたの？！
example_sentences.english: That cellphone cost you as much as 200,000 yen?!

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一回も地下鉄に乗ったことが無い。
example_sentences.english: I have never taken the subway, not even once.

example_sentences.japanese: 私も行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go too.

example_sentences.japanese: １０回もやったけど、できなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to do it as many as 10 times but couldn't do it!

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカまで１５時間もかかりました。
example_sentences.english: It took as long as 15 hours to get to America!

example_sentences.japanese: １０時間も運転したけど、あまり疲れていない。
example_sentences.english: I did as much as 10 hours of driving, but I am not really that tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 「掃除をして」って何回も言ったでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I told you to clean many times, right? (as many as)

example_sentences.japanese: ティムは日本に五回も行ったことがあると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that Tim has been to Japan as many as 5 times.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校で鉛筆を１００本も売った。
example_sentences.english: I sold as many as 100 pencils at school.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が事故にあって、五日間も病院で寝たって。
example_sentences.english: They said that person was in an accident and slept in the hospital for as long as five days.

example_sentences.japanese: このビルは出口が何箇所もあるので、とても安全です。
example_sentences.english: This building has exits in many places, so it is very safe. (as many as)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は一回も日本に行ったことがない。
example_sentences.english: I have not been to Japan, not even once.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生の時毎日エナジードリンクを５杯も飲んでいました。
example_sentences.english: When I was a college student, I was drinking as many as five energy drinks a day.

example_sentences.japanese: この家にはお箸を一膳も置いてないの？
example_sentences.english: This house doesn't even have as much as one pair of chopsticks lying around?

general_translation: Almost all, Most, Hardly any, Few (Adverbial noun)
formation: ほとんど + Phrase ほとんど + (Negative) Phrase
casual_structure: ほとんど + Phrase ほとんど + (Negative) Phrase
explanation: A common phrase that highlights that (A) is mostly or hardly something, depending on if the sentence is positive or negative.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなは、ほとんど帰りました。
example_sentences.english: Almost everyone has gone home.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁当はほとんど食べてないけど、おやつは全部食べた。
example_sentences.english: I didn't eat most of my lunch, but I ate all the snacks.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの人は私の名前を読めません。
example_sentences.english: Most people can't read my name.

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの大学生は親と住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: Most college students live with their parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は屋台がほとんどないね。
example_sentences.english: There are hardly any food stalls this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に出かけることはほとんどないです。
example_sentences.english: I hardly go out during the weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題はほとんど終わっているよ。
example_sentences.english: Most of my homework is done.

example_sentences.japanese: ハンドバッグがほとんど売り切れでした。
example_sentences.english: The handbags were almost all sold out.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は宿題がほとんどない。
example_sentences.english: There is hardly any homework today. (almost/mostly none)

example_sentences.japanese: この湖はほとんど浅いと思う。
