example_sentences.english: This lake is mostly shallow, I think.

example_sentences.japanese: えっ！この魚ほとんど匂いがない。
example_sentences.english: Huh?! This fish hardly has any smell. (almost/mostly none)

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りまでに出す生徒がほとんどいなかった。
example_sentences.english: Hardly any students submitted (the paper) before the deadline. (almost/mostly none)

example_sentences.japanese: この店の品物の値段はほとんどが高いです。
example_sentences.english: Almost all of this store's products are expensive. (Have a high price)

example_sentences.japanese: 先週買ったケーキがほとんど残っている。
example_sentences.english: Almost all of the cake that I bought last week is left over.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は晴れているので、雲がほとんどない。
example_sentences.english: Today is a clear weather day, so there are hardly any clouds. (almost/mostly none)

example_sentences.japanese: ほとんどの会社が反対だった。
example_sentences.english: Most of the companies were against it.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんはまたどこかに行くのですか。彼はほとんどの国に行っているんじゃないですか。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is going somewhere again? He has been to almost all of the countries, hasn't he?

example_sentences.japanese: 褒めるだけでほとんどの子供が嬉しくなる。
example_sentences.english: Most children are content with just being praised.

formation: そんな + Noun こんな + Nounあんな + Nounどんな + Noun
casual_structure: そんな + Noun こんな + Nounあんな + Nounどんな + Noun
explanation: A casual phrase that highlights things such as this (A), or that (A), or whatever (A), focusing on likeness.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな車がいい。
example_sentences.english: What kind of car is good?

example_sentences.japanese: そんな言い方してはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You should not phrase it like that.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな高いものはもらえないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can't accept a gift this expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな大人にはなりたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to become an adult like that.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな靴が欲しい？
example_sentences.english: What kind of shoes do you want?

example_sentences.japanese: そのような商品はないです。
example_sentences.english: We don't have a product like that.

example_sentences.japanese: このような場合にはどうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What should we do in a situation like this?

example_sentences.japanese: あのような運転をしないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not drive like that.

example_sentences.japanese: どのような商品をお探しですか？
example_sentences.english: What kind of product are you looking for?

example_sentences.japanese: そんな技術は珍しい。
example_sentences.english: A skill such as that is rare. (close to listener)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな高いのは必要ですか。
example_sentences.english: Is such an expensive one necessary? (close to speaker)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな畳が大体寝やすい。
example_sentences.english: Tatami mats like these are generally easy to sleep on. (close to speaker)

example_sentences.japanese: あんな駐車場は使いにくい。
example_sentences.english: A parking lot like that (over there) is hard to use. (far from both speaker and listener)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことを言わないでくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Could you not say such things please. (Close to listener)

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が乗るなら、あんな車がいい。
example_sentences.english: If I am the one that is going to ride it, that kind of car is good. (Away from both speaker and listener)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が言っていたのはこんなコーヒーかな。
example_sentences.english: I wondered if this kind of coffee is what she was talking about. (close to speaker)

example_sentences.japanese: あんなところに入りたくない。暗すぎる。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to go into that kind of place. It is too dark. (Away from both speaker and listener)

example_sentences.japanese: 電気屋さんに行って来るけど、こんな電池でよかった？
example_sentences.english: I am going to go to the electronics store, were these (kind of) batteries the right kind? (close to speaker)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなものを飛行機に持ち込んではいけません。
example_sentences.english: You cannot bring such a thing on to an airplane. (Close to listener)

example_sentences.japanese: あんなテーブルは絶対に僕たちのダイニングに入らない。
example_sentences.english: That kind of table would definitely not fit in our dining room. (Away from both speaker and listener)

formation: 各（かく） + Noun
casual_structure: 各（かく） + Noun
explanation: A slightly formal word which highlights each respective (A) in a group or series.

example_sentences.japanese: かくファイルをかく自アップロードする必要がある。
example_sentences.english: Each person needs to upload their respective files.

example_sentences.japanese: このエレベーターはかく階で止まります。
example_sentences.english: This elevator will stop at each floor.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルはかく部屋に洗濯機がついている。
example_sentences.english: This hotel has a washing machine in every room.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは正月になると日本かく地からの観光客でいっぱいになる。
example_sentences.english: When it becomes New Year's, this place is filled with tourists from each and every place in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: このバスはかくバス停に止まります。
example_sentences.english: This bus stops at each station.

example_sentences.japanese: かく自で弁当を持ってきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring your own respective bento (individually).

example_sentences.japanese: この書類のかくページをプリントアウトしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please print each page of this document.

example_sentences.japanese: かく部屋に冷房がついている。
example_sentences.english: Each room is equipped with air conditioning.

example_sentences.japanese: このビルのかく階にトイレがある。
example_sentences.english: Each floor of this building has a toilet.

example_sentences.japanese: かくアカウントの名前はユニークである必要がある。
example_sentences.english: Each account name must be unique.

example_sentences.japanese: この旅館には日本かく地からお客さまが来る。
example_sentences.english: Customers from all over (each place) Japan come to this ryokan.

example_sentences.japanese: かくイベント時間と場所をこちらでチェックできます。
example_sentences.english: You can check each event's time and place here.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長：「かくモデルの価格を下げようと思っています」
example_sentences.english: Company president: 'We plan to decrease the prices of each model.'

example_sentences.japanese: ここに並んでいるかく製品はアルミ製品です。
example_sentences.english: Each product lined up here is an aluminum product.

example_sentences.japanese: かく学年、ホールに集まった。
example_sentences.english: Each class gathered in the hall.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁当は各々で用意してきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please come prepared with your own lunch. (Each person should bring their own lunch)

general_translation: Next to (rank), Second to, Ranked after
formation: Noun + の次（つぎ）に
casual_structure: Noun + の次（つぎ）に
explanation: An expression indicating that one thing follows another. It is used to express the relative order of things.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はラーメンのつぎに寿司が好きで、そのつぎに天ぷらが好き！
example_sentences.english: I like sushi second to ramen, and after that I like tempura!

example_sentences.japanese: 小鳥のつぎに猿が欲しい！
example_sentences.english: After a small bird, I want a monkey!

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は仕事のつぎに釣りが大事なんです。
example_sentences.english: To me, fishing is the most important thing after work.

example_sentences.japanese: 市民大会のつぎに県大会があります。
example_sentences.english: After the city tournament comes the prefectural tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: 机のつぎに床を掃除してくださいね。
example_sentences.english: After the desk, please clean the floor.

example_sentences.japanese: お姉ちゃんのつぎに身長が高いのは私よ！
example_sentences.english: I'm the second tallest after my older sister!

example_sentences.japanese: この地域で米のつぎに多く食べられるのはパンです。
example_sentences.english: In this region, bread is the most commonly eaten food after rice.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘：「お母さん、ケーキ食べてもいい？」母：「だめ。夜ご飯のつぎにデザートよ！」
example_sentences.english: Daughter: 'Mom, can I eat some cake?' Mother: 'No. Dessert comes after dinner!'

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランでは、パスタのつぎにピザが有名らしい。
example_sentences.english: At this restaurant, the pizza is apparently the most famous dish after the pasta.

example_sentences.japanese: 父：「ちょっとトイレに行ってくる。」息子：「わかった。お父さんのつぎに僕が行くね！」
example_sentences.english: Father: 'I'm going to the restroom for a bit.' Son: 'Got it. I'll go after you, Dad!'

example_sentences.japanese: 子供ができてから、子供のつぎに夫が大切になりました。
example_sentences.english: Since having a child, my husband has become the most important person to me after my child.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の中で一番観光客が多い場所は東京で、そのつぎに大阪と聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Tokyo gets the most tourists in Japan, and after that is Osaka.

example_sentences.japanese: この国では、教育産業のつぎにＩＴ産業が大きな収入で、世界中の若者がこの国に住みたいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: In this country, the IT industry brings in the largest income after the education sector, and young people from all over the world say they want to live here.

example_sentences.japanese: この駅のつぎに止まる駅はどこでしょう？
example_sentences.english: What is the station we stop at after this station?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はゲームのつぎに勉強をするつもりだったのに、ゲームで一日が終わった。
example_sentences.english: Today I intended to study after playing games, but the day ended with just games.

example_sentences.japanese: 簡単なテストの次に面接があります。
example_sentences.english: After the simple test, there is an interview.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界でインドの次に人口が多い国は中国です。
example_sentences.english: Second to India, the country with the largest population in the world is China.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康の次に大切なのはお金だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think the most important thing after health is money.

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ、私の隣に座ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please sit next to me.

example_sentences.japanese: この町では米の次にじゃがいもがよく作られています。
example_sentences.english: In this town, potatoes are the most commonly grown crop next to rice.

general_translation: More than (or equal to), Over・(and) above, Any more・Greater, Exceeding
formation: Noun + Amount + 以上（いじょう）それ(1) +  以上（いじょう）(1) これ、あれ
casual_structure: Noun + Amount + 以上（いじょう）それ(1) +  以上（いじょう）(1) これ、あれ
explanation: A phrase which expresses that (A) is the minimum amount, for which something is greater than or exceeds.

example_sentences.japanese: その時に１００人いじょうも参加した。
example_sentences.english: At that time, more than 100 people attended.

example_sentences.japanese: 七十歳いじょうの人は運転をしない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: It would be better if people over the age of 70 didn't drive.

example_sentences.japanese: コンサートには５００人いじょうのファンが集まった。
example_sentences.english: More than 500 fans gathered at the concert.

example_sentences.japanese: え～っと、ビッグマックのセットとクォーターパウンダーの単品とナゲットの３０ピースを下さい。いじょうです。
example_sentences.english: Uhhh, Can I have a Big Mac meal, a quarter pounder, and 30 nuggets? That's all.

example_sentences.japanese: 六歳いじょう。
example_sentences.english: Ages 6 and over. (and older)

example_sentences.japanese: これいじょうはもう聞きたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to listen to this any more (than this).

example_sentences.japanese: これいじょう運動をしたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to exercise more than this.

example_sentences.japanese: それいじょう私のお金を使わないで。
example_sentences.english: Please don't use any more of my money over that amount.

example_sentences.japanese: それいじょう運ぶのは、腰に悪いよ。
example_sentences.english: Carrying any more than that, it's bad for your back.

example_sentences.japanese: これいじょう走れません。吐きそうです。
example_sentences.english: I can't run any more than this, I might puke.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年３００日いじょうトレーニングが出来た。
example_sentences.english: Last year, I worked out more than 300 days.

example_sentences.japanese: カタカナを全部覚えたけど、二週間いじょうかかりました。
example_sentences.english: I memorized all of the katakana, but it took over two weeks. (more than)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに漢字１００個いじょう覚えなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to memorize over 100 kanji by tomorrow. (more than)

example_sentences.japanese: 普通は１日に５０人いじょうがこのホテルに泊まる。
example_sentences.english: Usually over 50 people stay at this hotel a day. (more than)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の誕生日パーティーに２０人いじょうの友達が来た。
example_sentences.english: More than 20 friends came to my birthday party.

general_translation: Less than (or equal to), Under・(and) below, Any less・fewer, Not exceeding
formation: Noun + Amount + 以下（いか）それ(1) +  以下（いか）(1) これ、あれ
casual_structure: Noun + Amount + 以下（いか）それ(1) +  以下（いか）(1) これ、あれ
explanation: A structure which highlights that (A) is the maximum amount, for which something is less than or under.

example_sentences.japanese: この家は２０００万円いかです。
example_sentences.english: This house costs less than 20 million yen. (or equal to)

example_sentences.japanese: 空港にはいかのものを持って来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring the following to the airport.

example_sentences.japanese: １７歳いかの方は保護者の方と来てください。
example_sentences.english: For those of the ages 17 and under, please come with a guardian.

example_sentences.japanese: この車は３０万円いかだった。
example_sentences.english: This car was under 300,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: いか同文。
example_sentences.english: The rest is the same. (Usually seen in documents to notify the reader that the rest of the document basically repeats what has already been said)

example_sentences.japanese: 五千円いかのコーヒーメーカーがないんですか。
example_sentences.english: Are there no coffee makers below 5000 yen? (not exceeding)

example_sentences.japanese: 残っているジュースは十本いかだ。
example_sentences.english: There are fewer than 10 juices left. (under・not more than)

example_sentences.japanese: これいかの値段がありません。
example_sentences.english: There are none under this price. (less than or equal to)

example_sentences.japanese: コンサートに行ったのは１００人いか。
example_sentences.english: 100 or less people went to the concert.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法が平均点いかだった。
example_sentences.english: My grammar score was less than average.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では１７歳いかの人は運転が出来ない。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, those 17 or younger cannot drive.

example_sentences.japanese: ８０点いかなら、もう一回テストを受けなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: If you get 80 points or less, you have to take the test one more time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の大学から日本に留学したのは１０人いかです。
example_sentences.english: Fewer than 10 people from my college studied abroad in Japan. (not more than)

example_sentences.japanese: それが少ないと思う？私の大学から、５人いかですよ。
example_sentences.english: You think that's low? Five or fewer people from my college went.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はテストで９８点いかを取ったことがありません。
example_sentences.english: I have never gotten a score lower than 98 on a test. (less than or equal to)

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業出来た人は１００人いかでした。
example_sentences.english: Less than 100 people were able to graduate. (...or equal to)

general_translation: Except・besides, Other than, With the exception of
formation: Verb + 以外（いがい）Noun + 以外（いがい）
casual_structure: Verb + 以外（いがい）Noun + 以外（いがい）
explanation: A word which indicates everything outside of (A), or except for (A).

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーいがい、誰も来なかった。
example_sentences.english: No one except Mary came.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は和食いがいのものが食べたい。
example_sentences.english: Today I want to eat something other than Japanese food.

example_sentences.japanese: タロウはゲームいがいに趣味はあるの？
example_sentences.english: Taro, do you have any other interests besides gaming?

example_sentences.japanese: それいがい、聞いてないよ。
example_sentences.english: I haven't heard anything other than that.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆いがい何でも食べられる。
example_sentences.english: I can eat anything other than natto.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は言われたこといがい何もしないよ。
example_sentences.english: He will not do anything other than what he is told.

example_sentences.japanese: それいがいに好きなことないの？
example_sentences.english: Don't you have anything you like besides that?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はエスプレッソいがいのコーヒーは飲まない。
example_sentences.english: He doesn't drink any other coffee than espresso.

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司いがいに何を食べたい？
example_sentences.english: Other than sushi, what do you want to eat?

example_sentences.japanese: 「関係者いがい入ってはいけない」と書いてあるよ。
example_sentences.english: It is written that 'With the exception of authorized personnel, entry is prohibited.'

example_sentences.japanese: ピザとコーラいがい他に頼みたい物ある？
example_sentences.english: Besides pizza and cola, is there anything else you want to order?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日日本語の勉強いがい何もしていない。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I didn't do anything other than study Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 今まで漢字いがい、何も勉強していなかった。
example_sentences.english: Until now, I haven't been studying anything except kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語と英語いがいに話せる言語はありますか。
example_sentences.english: Other than Japanese and English are there any other languages that you can speak?

example_sentences.japanese: たかし君もアニメ好きなの？ちょっと意外だね。
example_sentences.english: Takashi-kun, do you like anime too? I'm a little surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺こう見えても意外に肉を食べないの。
example_sentences.english: It may come off as a surprise based on how I look, but I don't eat meat.

general_translation: Continuously, All throughout, Entire time, Ever (since), The whole time, All the way
formation: ずっと + Phrase
casual_structure: ずっと + Phrase
explanation: A casual expression highlighting that (A) is continuing, or has continued endlessly, without ever ceasing. (A) is unwavering.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ずっと前から日本に行きたかったです。」
example_sentences.english: 'I have wanted to go to Japan for a long time.'

example_sentences.japanese: ずっとゲームをしないでたまには勉強もする。
example_sentences.english: Instead of continuously gaming, I occasionally also study.

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと立ってたから足が痛い。
example_sentences.english: I was standing the whole time, so my feet hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日からずっと寝てないからメチャ眠い。
example_sentences.english: I haven't slept at all since yesterday, so I am extremely tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝からずっと何も食べていないからお腹が空いたよ。
example_sentences.english: I haven't eaten anything at all since morning, so I am hungry.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝からずっと忙しいですよ。
example_sentences.english: I have been continuously busy since morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は子供の頃から彼にずっと会っていません。
example_sentences.english: I have not met him ever since I was a child.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は結婚してからずっとここに住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: Ever since we got married, we have always lived here.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬休みはノートパソコンを買えるようにずっと働いていた。
example_sentences.english: I worked all throughout winter vacation in order to be able to buy a new laptop.

example_sentences.japanese: たけしさんは両親が海外旅行に行っている間、ずっとゲームをやっていた。
example_sentences.english: Takeshi was playing video games the whole time his parents were abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 「怒ってる？」「怒ってるよ。わたしはずっとスーパーの前で君を待っていたよ！」
example_sentences.english: 'Are you angry?''I am mad! I was (continuously) waiting for you (the whole time) in front of the supermarket.'

example_sentences.japanese: その日からずっとこの時計を使ってきました。
example_sentences.english: I have been using this watch ever since that day.

example_sentences.japanese: 生まれてからずっとこの村に住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I have lived in this village ever since I was born.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏・彼女：「これからもずっと一緒にいよう。」
example_sentences.english: Boyfriend/girlfriend: 'Let's be together all the time from here on out!'

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った親：「テレビが昨日の夜からずっとついていた。」
example_sentences.english: Angry parent: 'The TV was on the whole night.'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察：「昨日の晩、何をしていたのですか。」容疑者：「ずっと家にいました。」
example_sentences.english: Policeman: 'What did you do last evening?'Suspect: 'I was at home the whole time.'

general_translation: Most・mostly, Adequately・generally, For the most part, Roughly・approximately, In the first place
formation: だいたい + Phraseだいたい + Number(1)だいたい + の + Noun(1) Degree
casual_structure: だいたい + Phraseだいたい + Number(1)だいたい + の + Noun(1) Degree
explanation: A word implying that something is, for the most part, (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「日本語がだいたいわかる。」
example_sentences.english: 'I roughly understand Japanese.' (for the most part)

example_sentences.japanese: だいたいでいいから何時くらいに着くか教えて。
example_sentences.english: Since a general time is okay, can you let me know around when you will arrive?

example_sentences.japanese: 水曜日はだいたい５時に起きています。
example_sentences.english: On Wednesdays, I generally wake up at 5 o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: だいたいの人たちが薔薇という漢字を書けません。
example_sentences.english: Most people do not know how to write the kanji 'bara'. (薔薇（ばら） is the kanji for 'rose')

example_sentences.japanese: だいたいなんでお前がここにいるの？
example_sentences.english: Why are you here in the first place? (No one wants you here)

example_sentences.japanese: 「だいたい３時間くらいでできます。」
example_sentences.english: 'It will be ready in approximately 3 hours.' (roughly)

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼女はだいたいの状況を知っています。」
example_sentences.english: 'She has the general idea of the situation.' (adequate・mostly)

example_sentences.japanese: 焼きたてパンについて話しているカップル、彼女：「どう？」彼氏：「だいたいいいと思うんだけど、」
example_sentences.english: Couple talking about freshly baked bread: Girlfriend: 'How is it?'Boyfriend: 'I think it is mostly good, but…'

example_sentences.japanese: 電話にでている子供：「父はだいたい５時ごろ帰ります。」
example_sentences.english: Child answering the phone: 'Dad usually comes home around 5.'

example_sentences.japanese: このサイトにいる人は、だいたい真面目な人だと思う。外国語を学ぶときはそれが必要だからね。
example_sentences.english: I think that people on this site are mostly diligent. Because you need that when learning a foreign language. (generally)

example_sentences.japanese: 文化祭の準備をしている生徒：「だいたいでいいから、午前中までにはおわらせておいて。」
example_sentences.english: Students preparing for the school festival: 'Adequately is good enough, so can you finish it during the morning?' (mostly)

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんと話しているテクニカルサポートスタッフ：「だいたいは、スマートフォンをリセットすればＯＫです。」
example_sentences.english: Tech support staff speaking with a customer: 'Generally, if you reset your smartphone it will be OK.' (generally)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「彼女はだいたい２８歳くらいかな。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I would guess that she is roughly about 28 years old.' (approximately)

example_sentences.japanese: 家族との話：「母はだいたいスマホを使えるようになった。」
example_sentences.english: Chat with family: 'For the most part, my mom has come to be able to use a smartphone.' (mostly・adequately)

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「だいたいの人は食べたり寝たりするのが好きです。」
example_sentences.english: Editorial: 'Most people enjoy doing such things like eating and sleeping.' (generally・for the most part)

example_sentences.japanese: 「だいたい、太郎が一人でそこへ行ったことが間違いなんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'In the first place, it was a mistake for Tarou to go there by himself.'

example_sentences.japanese: と言うことは私たちが言っていることはだいたい一緒なのね。
example_sentences.english: In that case, what we are both saying is the same in essence.

formation: Noun + の + 中（なか）でその(1) + 中（なか）で(1) この
casual_structure: Noun + の + 中（なか）でその(1) + 中（なか）で(1) この
explanation: A phrase used to select one thing from within a group, and then describe it further.

example_sentences.japanese: この三つのなかでは、赤色が好き。
example_sentences.english: Among these three, I like the red one. (within)

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンのなかでは味噌ラーメンが好き。
example_sentences.english: Among ramen, I like the miso type.

example_sentences.japanese: このバンドのなかでは誰が好き？
example_sentences.english: Who do you like in this band?

example_sentences.japanese: 車のなかで夕食を食べました。
example_sentences.english: I ate dinner in my car.

example_sentences.japanese: フルーツのなかで、イチゴとかパインが好き。
example_sentences.english: Among all fruits, I like strawberries and pineapple. (within)

example_sentences.japanese: このなかで一つを選んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please choose one from among these. (within)

example_sentences.japanese: 公園のなかで子供達が遊んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The children were playing in the park. (Within)

example_sentences.japanese: 全部の国のなかで、一番行ってみたいのはどこ？
example_sentences.english: Among all countries, which one do you want to go to the most? (within)

example_sentences.japanese: グループのなかで色々な意見がありました。
example_sentences.english: There were various opinions among the group. (Within)

example_sentences.japanese: 電車のなかで大きい声で喋らないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not speak loudly in the train. (Within)

example_sentences.japanese: ひらがなとカタカナと漢字のなかで、ひらがなしか書けない。
example_sentences.english: Among hiragana, katakana, and kanji, I can only write hiragana. (within)

example_sentences.japanese: この四つのなかで、三つも嫌いなの？
example_sentences.english: Among these four, you hate three? (within)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は雨のなかで歌っていたから、服が濡れている。
example_sentences.english: He was singing in the rain, so his clothes are wet. (Within)

example_sentences.japanese: チームのなかでコミュニケーション能力が必要だろう。
example_sentences.english: Communication among team members is important, yeah? (Within)

example_sentences.japanese: 今までの変顔写真のなかで、どれが好き?
example_sentences.english: Up to this point, out of (all) the strange-face pictures, which do you like? (among・within)

formation: Verb + よう + に + Verb(1)Verb + よう + な + Noun(1)  Adverb、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective
casual_structure: Verb + よう + に + Verb(1)Verb + よう + な + Noun(1)  Adverb、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective
explanation: A semi-formal expression used to confidently describe the manner in which something appears.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は食べすぎたような顔をしている。
example_sentences.english: He looks like he ate too much.

example_sentences.japanese: バケツをひっくり返したように雨が降っている。
example_sentences.english: It is raining like a bucket was flipped over. (It's pouring rain)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の車は工場のような臭いがする。
example_sentences.english: His car smells like a factory. (His car has an industrial smell)

example_sentences.japanese: キトウ先生は鬼のような怒り方をする。
example_sentences.english: The way Kito-sensei gets mad is like a demon.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は亀のように走る。
example_sentences.english: He runs like a turtle.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は今、人を殺すような目をしている。
example_sentences.english: Right now, his eyes look as if he is about to kill someone.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが言ったように、事故が起こった。
example_sentences.english: An accident happened just like you said.

example_sentences.japanese: 十代に戻ったように楽しかった。
example_sentences.english: It was fun, just like being in my teens again.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が言うように綺麗ですね。
example_sentences.english: It is beautiful, just like you say.

example_sentences.japanese: 驚くような景色を見た。
example_sentences.english: I saw mind-blowing-like scenery.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かを殺すような目をしていた。
example_sentences.english: He had eyes just like he was going to kill someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 想像できないようなアイディアが沢山ありました。
example_sentences.english: I had ideas like you couldn't imagine.

example_sentences.japanese: いっぱい宿題があるようなことを言っていたけど、本当は何もなかった。
example_sentences.english: They were talking like we would have a lot of homework, but we really didn't have any.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品がなくなるような状況だったけど、閉店まで大丈夫でした。
example_sentences.english: It seemed like we were going to run out of products, but we made it until closing time.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はまるで筆で書くように、綺麗な字を書けます。
example_sentences.english: That person is able to write beautiful letters as if (they were) written with a brush.

example_sentences.japanese: まずはウサインボルトが走るように走ってみて。
example_sentences.english: First, try running just like Usain Bolt.

example_sentences.japanese: 何か腐っているような臭いがするね。
example_sentences.english: It smells just like something is rotting, don't you think?

general_translation: At least, Sort of, Or so
formation: Number/Amount + Counter + （くらい(1)） + はNoun + くらい(1) + は(1) ぐらい
casual_structure: Number/Amount + Counter + （くらい(1)） + はNoun + くらい(1) + は(1) ぐらい
explanation: A structure which implies a general or approximate amount of (A). Often meaning at least.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスぐらいは家に帰って来てね？
example_sentences.english: Won't you come home for Christmas, at least?

example_sentences.japanese: ディズニーランドには年に５回は行っている。
example_sentences.english: I go to Disneyland at least 5 times a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日、テレビを５時間は見ている。
example_sentences.english: Every day, I watch TV for 5 hours or so.

example_sentences.japanese: ２キロくらいはあると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think it is at least 2 kilograms.

example_sentences.japanese: 倉敷には１回ぐらいは行った方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should go to Kurashiki at least once.

example_sentences.japanese: 少なくともこれぐらいは持って行ってください。
example_sentences.english: At the very least, at least bring this with you.

example_sentences.japanese: 囚人のうち少なくとも６人は逃げたらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that at least 6 prisoners have escaped.

example_sentences.japanese: この食べ物は少なくとも床に３秒は落ちていたから食べられない。
example_sentences.english: This food was on the floor for at least 3 seconds, so I can't eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: 付き合っているんだから手ぐらいはつないだでしょうね？
example_sentences.english: Since you are going out, you were at least holding hands, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏は１日８回は電話をかける。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend calls at least 8 times a day.

example_sentences.japanese: 心配な母親：「肉ぐらいは少し食べてよ。」
example_sentences.english: Worried mother: 'Please eat some meat at least!'

example_sentences.japanese: スティーブン・ホーキングに一回は会いたかったのに…
example_sentences.english: (But) I wanted to meet Stephen Hawking at least once…

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った親：「話す前にちょっとは考えるのが普通だろ！」
example_sentences.english: Angry parent: 'It is normal to think a little at least before you speak! Isn't it?'

example_sentences.japanese: ドミニク：「沖縄に一度は行こうと思っています。」
example_sentences.english: Dominic: 'I am thinking of going to Okinawa at least once.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の週末までに夏休みの宿題の半分ぐらいはやるよ。おかあさん、約束するよ。
example_sentences.english: I will do at least half of my summer homework by next weekend. I promise, Mom.

example_sentences.japanese: この箱の中には少なくともクッキーが百個は入っているだろう。
example_sentences.english: There are probably at least 100 cookies in this box.

formation: 何（なん） + Counter + かいく + Counter + かいくつか
casual_structure: 何（なん） + Counter + かいく + Counter + かいくつか
explanation: A common phrase used when exactly what amount of (A) is uncertain, so a rough estimate of several or some is given.

example_sentences.japanese: このアニメのなんわかを見たと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think I have seen a few episodes of this anime.

example_sentences.japanese: そこにはなん回か行ったことがあると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think I have been there several times.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、紙をなん枚かちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, may I have some paper?

example_sentences.japanese: この車はいくらですか？
example_sentences.english: How much is this car?

example_sentences.japanese: マリちゃんは幾つになったの？
example_sentences.english: How old did Mari-chan turn?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日なんだいかの車が盗まれたらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that several (some) cars were stolen yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 選手のなんにんかが負傷した。
example_sentences.english: Some athletes were wounded.

example_sentences.japanese: なんさつかの本が山のように床に積まれていた。
example_sentences.english: Some books were piled on the floor like a mountain.

example_sentences.japanese: なんぼんかの高級な木の幹を製材所に届けた。
example_sentences.english: I sent some high grade tree trunks to the sawmill.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなんびきかの猫を撫でるように命じられた。
example_sentences.english: He was ordered to pet several (some) cats.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らの写真をなんまいか撮れてよかった。
example_sentences.english: I am glad that I was able to take a few photos of them.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいくつかの言語をペラペラ話せるようになった。
example_sentences.english: She reached a point where she could speak in several languages fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: 紙をなんまいか持って行かなくちゃいけない。
example_sentences.english: I need to bring a few sheets of paper.

example_sentences.japanese: なんかいか電話が鳴ったけど、少しも構わない。
example_sentences.english: The phone rang several (a few) times, but I don't give a damn about it.

example_sentences.japanese: あたしでもときどきなんぼんかの花とかもらいたいわよ。
example_sentences.english: Even I want to get some flowers or something from time to time!

example_sentences.japanese: このビルのなんかいかはもう使用されているみたい。
example_sentences.english: It seems like a few floors of this building are already being utilized.

example_sentences.japanese: いらない本を何冊か妹にあげた。
example_sentences.english: I gave several books that I didn't need to my sister.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は何者だ！
example_sentences.english: Who are you! (What kind of person are you)

formation: 真ま(っ) + ［い］Adjective［い］真ま(っ) + Noun真まん + ま(*)・な(*):真まん中（なか）、真まん前（まえ）、真まん丸（まる）真まっ + か(*)・さ(*)・しゃ(*):真まっ黄色（きいろ）、真まっ白（しろ）、真まっ先（さき）、真まっ正直（しょうじき）真まっ + は(*)(**):真まっ平ぴら、真まっ裸ぱだかExceptions:青あおい ￫ 真まっ青さお赤あかい ￫ 真まっ赤か(*) column in the kana chart(**) H sound becomes P sound
casual_structure: 真ま(っ) + ［い］Adjective［い］真ま(っ) + Noun真まん + ま(*)・な(*):真まん中（なか）、真まん前（まえ）、真まん丸（まる）真まっ + か(*)・さ(*)・しゃ(*):真まっ黄色（きいろ）、真まっ白（しろ）、真まっ先（さき）、真まっ正直（しょうじき）真まっ + は(*)(**):真まっ平ぴら、真まっ裸ぱだかExceptions:青あおい ￫ 真まっ青さお赤あかい ￫ 真まっ赤か(*) column in the kana chart(**) H sound becomes P sound
explanation: A prefix that indicates a high level of (A), by stating that something is the true (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 道のまんなかに鹿がいた。
example_sentences.english: There was a deer right in the middle of the road.

example_sentences.japanese: まん中にある本をとってください。
example_sentences.english: Please take the book in the middle.

example_sentences.japanese: この猫はまん丸でかわいい。
example_sentences.english: This cat is completely circular and cute. (This cat is so fat that it is cute)

example_sentences.japanese: 体がまっ赤になるくらい お風呂が熱かった。
example_sentences.english: The bath was so hot that my body went completely red.

example_sentences.japanese: サルが木からまっ逆さまに落ちた。
example_sentences.english: The monkey fell completely upside down from the tree.

example_sentences.japanese: 道が雪でまっ白になった。
example_sentences.english: The road turned completely white with snow.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと、何でまっ裸なの？
example_sentences.english: Wait, why are you completely naked?

example_sentences.japanese: まっ昼間からこんな話をするの？
example_sentences.english: You are going to talk about this in the middle of the day? (Are you seriously going to talk about something like this in the middle of the day?)

example_sentences.japanese: まんまるの円を描ける人がいますか。
example_sentences.english: Is there anyone who can draw an exact circle? (perfectly circular)

example_sentences.japanese: この道路をまっすぐ行ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please go (exactly) straight down this street.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は竹を刀でまっぷたつに切った。
example_sentences.english: He cut the bamboo right in two with a sword.

example_sentences.japanese: 急に立ったから、目の前 がまっくらになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Because I stood up suddenly, everything went completely black.

example_sentences.japanese: 可愛い女の子に声をかけられたの？顔がまっか！
example_sentences.english: Did a cute girl talk to you? Your face is completely red.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝は空がまっさおで、今は雨が降りそう。
example_sentences.english: This morning the sky was completely blue, now it looks like it might rain.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ5時なのに外はまっくらです。
example_sentences.english: It is still only 5 o'clock, but outside is completely dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議のまっさいちゅうに携帯が鳴ったから、先輩に怒られた。
example_sentences.english: Because my phone rang right in the middle of the meeting, I was scolded by my senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議中に携帯が鳴ったから、恥ずかしくて、顔がまっかになったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Since my phone rang in the middle of the meeting, I was so embarrassed that my face turned completely red.

example_sentences.japanese: 富士山の頂上が雪でまっしろだから、上からスキーしてみたいな。
example_sentences.english: The summit of Mt. Fuji is completely white with snow, so I would love to try to ski down it.

example_sentences.japanese: そのことをまっさきに話して欲しかったですね。
example_sentences.english: I wanted you to talk about that from the very beginning.

example_sentences.japanese: 絵の具で絵を描いていたから、手がまっくろになった。
example_sentences.english: Because I was painting (with paint), my hands are completely black.

example_sentences.japanese: 空が真っ青できれいだね。
example_sentences.english: The sky is completely blue and beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 顔が真っ赤になってるよ、大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: Your face is completely red, are you okay?

general_translation: No more than, Not exceeding, As few as・as little as, Only
formation: Number + しか + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Number + しか + Verb［ない］
explanation: A phrase showing that the only things that exist are a specific number of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女にはまだ１回しかあっていない。
example_sentences.english: I have met her no more than once.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は五キロしか走れない。
example_sentences.english: I can only run 5 km today.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は１００円しか持っていない。
example_sentences.english: I have nothing but 100 yen on me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はたくさんの宿題があるから２時間しか遊べない。
example_sentences.english: I have a lot of homework today, so I can only hang out for 2 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 計画書は１枚しかていしゅつできない。
example_sentences.english: You can submit only one plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪の毛が３本しかはえていない。
example_sentences.english: He has no more than three hairs on his head.

example_sentences.japanese: 一ヶ月しかきかんがないのに、あなたは変われるの？
example_sentences.english: You only have (the period of) one month. Can you change?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼には１度しかかっていない。
example_sentences.english: I have only beaten him once.

example_sentences.japanese: 半年で１回しかけんかしなかった。
example_sentences.english: In half a year, we fought no more than once.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究したいけど４８時間しかない。
example_sentences.english: I want to do some research, but I have no more than 48 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: ５人しか見物客がいなくて寂しい。
example_sentences.english: It will be lonely with only five spectators.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの研究室には本が１０冊しかない。
example_sentences.english: There are no more than 10 books in our laboratory.

example_sentences.japanese: ２回しかけいけんしていないのに、自信満々だね。
example_sentences.english: (You) have experienced (it) no more than twice, and yet (you) are brimming with confidence.

example_sentences.japanese: お金持ちなのに現金は１０００円しかもっていない。
example_sentences.english: Even though (they) are rich, (they) have no more than 1000 yen in cash.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が厳しすぎて、２節しかすすまなかった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is so strict that he advanced through no more than two paragraphs.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中には色々な物が入っていたけど、リンゴだけを取り出した。
example_sentences.english: There were a lot of things in the refrigerator, but I just took out an apple.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中にはリンゴしかなかったから、リンゴを食べた。
example_sentences.english: Apples were all that was in the refrigerator, so I ate an apple.

formation: Noun (A) + は + (Category) Noun (B) + の一つ + だ
casual_structure: Noun (A) + は + (Category) Noun (B) + の一つ + だ
polite_structure: Noun (A) + は + (Category) Noun (B) + の一つ + です
explanation: An expression which shows that (A) is only one thing from within the whole category of (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ホンダは車のメーカーのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Honda is one of (many) car makers.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車は乗り物のひとつです。
example_sentences.english: Trains are one of (many) vehicles.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼も家族のひとりだ。
example_sentences.english: He is also one member of my family.

example_sentences.japanese: トマトはフルーツのいっしゅだ。
example_sentences.english: Tomatoes are one of many types of fruits.

example_sentences.japanese: このクレヨンはこのセットのいっぽんだ。
example_sentences.english: This crayon is part of this set.

example_sentences.japanese: アンドロイドはスマートフォンのＯＳのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Android is one of (many) smartphone operating systems.

example_sentences.japanese: アイフォンはスマートフォンのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: iPhone is one of (many) smartphones.

example_sentences.japanese: マクドナルドはファストフードのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: McDonald's is one of many fast food chains.

example_sentences.japanese: コカコーラはコーラのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Coca-cola is one of many colas.

example_sentences.japanese: キリスト教は宗教のひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Christianity is one of many religions.

example_sentences.japanese: ひらがなは日本のアルファベットのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Hiragana is one of the Japanese alphabets.

example_sentences.japanese: ルイ・ヴィトンはファッションブランドのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Louis Vuitton is one of many fashion brands.

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司は日本の有名な食べ物のひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Sushi is one of many famous Japanese foods.

example_sentences.japanese: 水は体に必要な物のひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Water is one of many things the body needs.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法は大事な勉強のひとつです。
example_sentences.english: Grammar is one of (many) important things to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 相撲は日本の伝統的なスポーツのひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: Sumo is one of many Japanese traditional sports.

example_sentences.japanese: ロード・オブ・ザ・リングはＪ・Ｒ・Ｒ・トールキンが書いた小説のひとつだ。
example_sentences.english: The Lord of the Rings is one of many novels written by J.R.R. Tolkien.

general_translation: There is not ~ that is not/does not
formation: Verb［ない］+ Noun + は + ない［い］Adjective［ない］+ Noun + は + Verb［ない］［な］Adjective + じゃない(1) + Noun + は + Verb［ない］(1) ではない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ Noun + は + ない［い］Adjective［ない］+ Noun + は + Verb［ない］［な］Adjective + じゃない(1) + Noun + は + Verb［ない］(1) ではない
explanation: A phrase expressing that there is not something which doesn't or isn't (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に書けない漢字はないの？
example_sentences.english: Is there really not a single kanji that you cannot write?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にはピアノで弾けない曲はない。
example_sentences.english: There is no song that he can't play on the piano.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は美味しくない食べ物は食べない。
example_sentences.english: I don't eat food that does not taste good.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は安くない靴は買わない。
example_sentences.english: He doesn't buy shoes that aren't cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢を見ない人はいないだろう。
example_sentences.english: There is not a single person who doesn't dream, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 紙をつかわない会社は一つもありません。
example_sentences.english: There is not a single company that does not use paper.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのカフェで美味しくないコーヒーは絶対ない。
example_sentences.english: There is no coffee at that cafe that is not delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強していない文法はなかったから、テストには合格しました。
example_sentences.english: There was not a single grammar point that I did not study, so I passed the test.

example_sentences.japanese: ボスの家にはテレビを置いていない部屋はない。
example_sentences.english: There is not a single room in my boss' house that does not have a TV.

example_sentences.japanese: この大学で日本語を勉強していない人はいません。
example_sentences.english: There is not a person who does not study Japanese at this university.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家族の中で海外に行ったことのない人はいない。
example_sentences.english: There is not a single person in my family who has not traveled abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の友達の中でピザが好きじゃない人は一人もいない。
example_sentences.english: There is not a single person in my group of friends that doesn't like pizza.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画が面白くて、笑わない人は一人もいなかった。
example_sentences.english: The movie was so funny that there was not a single person who did not laugh.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を持っていない人は買い物にいかない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: People who do not have money, should not go shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親：「新しいクラスはどう？友達を作ったの？」 子供：「好きじゃないクラスメイトはいないけど、まだ、できてないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Father: 'How is the new class? Did you make any friends?' Child: 'There are no classmates I don't like but I haven't made any new friends.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私に書けない漢字はない。
example_sentences.english: There is no kanji that I cannot write.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は漢字を書けなくはないけど...
example_sentences.english: It's not that I can't write kanji, but…

general_translation: Not even a little, Not at all, Not in the least, Never
formation: すこしも + Verb［ない］すこしも + ［い］Adjective［ない］すこしも + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
casual_structure: すこしも + Verb［ない］すこしも + ［い］Adjective［ない］すこしも + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
explanation: A structure highlighting that something is not even a little (A).

example_sentences.japanese: この景色はすこしも綺麗ではない。
example_sentences.english: This scenery is not pretty at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は人が多いからすこしも離れないでね。
example_sentences.english: There are a lot of people today, so don't stray off. Not even a little bit.

example_sentences.japanese: 何このケーキ、すこしもおいしくない！
example_sentences.english: What is this cake, it's not even a little good!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の彼氏はすこしもイケメンではない。
example_sentences.english: Her boyfriend is not even a little handsome.

example_sentences.japanese: あの店のケーキはすこしも美味しくない。
example_sentences.english: That store's cake is not delicious in the least.

example_sentences.japanese: すこしも暑くないのに、汗をかいている。
example_sentences.english: It is not in the least bit hot, but I am sweating.

example_sentences.japanese: ガソリンの値段がすこしも下がらないね。
example_sentences.english: The price of gasoline has not dropped in the least.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の話がすこしも理解出来なかった。
example_sentences.english: I did not understand the conversation in the least.

example_sentences.japanese: すこしも怖くないの？今幽霊を見たでしょう！
example_sentences.english: You are not scared at all? You just saw a ghost, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 君はすこしも太っていないのに、ダイエット頑張るの？
example_sentences.english: You are not overweight at all, but you still diet hard?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは子供の話をすこしも聞いてあげてない。
example_sentences.english: You never listen to what your kid has to say. (Not in the least)

example_sentences.japanese: この工場はすこしも安全じゃないけど、給料がいいって。
example_sentences.english: This factory is not the least bit safe, but I hear the pay is good.

example_sentences.japanese: 君はすこしもお金がないのにロレックスを買おうとしているの？
example_sentences.english: You do not have any money at all, but you are thinking about buying a Rolex?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は着物を着てみたいけど、すこしも似合わないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I want to try on a kimono, but it probably won't look good on me in the least.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近お母さんとすこしも連絡を取っていないから今日電話をする。
example_sentences.english: I have not contacted my mom in the least bit recently, so I will call her today.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月もお金がすこしもない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any money this month either.

general_translation: Quite a few, Quite a lot, Many, Not a few, Not a little
formation: Noun + は(1) + 少（すく）なくない(1) が、も
casual_structure: Noun + は(1) + 少（すく）なくない(1) が、も
polite_structure: Noun + は(1) + 少（すく）なくありません(1) が、も
explanation: A grammar point showing that there is many of (A), or not a few.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメと漫画が好きな人はすくなくないですよ。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few people that like anime and manga.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を書くのが嫌いな子はすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few children that dislike writing kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は好き嫌いがすくなくないんです。
example_sentences.english: I have many things that I like and dislike.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にお菓子を食べる人もすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: There are also many people that eat snacks before they sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: ハセガワ：「僕は友達がすくなくないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Hasegawa: 'I have quite a few friends.'

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ごはんを食べない人もすくなくないです。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few people who do not eat breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: そう思っている人もすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: Quite a few people think like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の欲しがっているものがすくなくないんだ。
example_sentences.english: There are many things that she wants.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのチームは勝つでしょう。サポーターの数はすくなくないからです。ですよね？
example_sentences.english: I guess our team will win. Because it has quite a few supporters. Right?

example_sentences.japanese: この教科書から学べることはすくなくないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think there are many things one can learn from this textbook.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の今までの行動を考えれば、そんなことが起こるポテンシャルはすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: Considering his behavior up until now, the potential of that happening is not small.

example_sentences.japanese: ひっきはとても優しい人よ。彼に世話になった人もいるし、助けられた人もすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: Hikki is a super kind person! There are quite a few people that received favors from him and that were also helped by him.

example_sentences.japanese: 人は家では、階段から落ちたり熱いお茶でやけどしたりする場合もすくなくない。
example_sentences.english: There are also many cases when people fall down the stairs or scald themselves with hot tea at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は去年より来るお客様もすくなくないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: This year, compared to last year, there may be quite a few more customers that come.

example_sentences.japanese: それに反対する人々もすくなくないと思うけど、彼らは目立たないようにしているだろう。
example_sentences.english: I think quite a few people oppose that, but they are probably doing their best to not stand out.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は去年よりも雨が降る日が少ない。
example_sentences.english: Compared to last year, there are fewer days with rain this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気が悪い時に釣りに行くのは危ない。
example_sentences.english: It is dangerous to go fishing when the weather's bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 手が汚いから手を洗う。
example_sentences.english: My hands are dirty so I will wash them.

general_translation: In the event of, In the case of
formation: Verb + 場合（ばあい）(は) ［い］Adjective + 場合（ばあい）(は)［な］Adjective + な + 場合（ばあい）(は) Noun + の + 場合（ばあい）(は)
casual_structure: Verb + 場合（ばあい）(は) ［い］Adjective + 場合（ばあい）(は)［な］Adjective + な + 場合（ばあい）(は) Noun + の + 場合（ばあい）(は)
explanation: A phrase which often highlights a potential occasion, or person in question.

example_sentences.japanese: 危険なばあいはここに電話をしてください。
example_sentences.english: In the event that it is dangerous, please call me.

example_sentences.japanese: オートバイに乗るばあいはヘルメットをかぶってください。
example_sentences.english: In the event that you will ride a motorbike, please wear a helmet.

example_sentences.japanese: 咳がひどいばあいはマスクをしてください。
example_sentences.english: In the case that you have a bad cough, please wear a mask.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が大変なばあいは私に電話をしてください。
example_sentences.english: In the case that your work is difficult, call me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のばあいは冬が好きです。
example_sentences.english: In my case, I like winter. (Personally I like winter)

example_sentences.japanese: 浅草駅に行くばあいはどの電車で行った方がいいですか？
example_sentences.english: If I were to go to Asakusa station, which train would be the best to take?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのばあい、こういう時はどうする？
example_sentences.english: In your case, what would you do in this situation?

example_sentences.japanese: 私の犬のばあいは家族と一緒です。
example_sentences.english: In the case of my dog, he is like family.

example_sentences.japanese: 遊んでいるばあいは、危ないことをしないで。
example_sentences.english: In the case that you are playing, don't do anything dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品が売り切れのばあいは買えないよ。
example_sentences.english: You cannot buy this product in the event that it is out of stock.

example_sentences.japanese: 山が崩れているばあいは運転をしないでください。
example_sentences.english: In the event of the mountain crumbling, please do not drive. (In the event of a landslide)

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーがあまり残っていないばあいは飲まない方がいい。
example_sentences.english: In the event that there is not much coffee left, you had better not drink any.

example_sentences.japanese: 景色が綺麗なばあいは写真を撮るでしょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はすごい優しい人だといってもいいでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It is safe to say that she is a very nice person.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はとてもいい人だといってもいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人が付き合っているといってもいいだろう。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は速くて、ウサインボルトに勝てるといってもいい。

example_sentences.japanese: このワインはお金持ちの人々だけが飲むといってもいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が凄い綺麗だから一生働かなくていいといってもいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日入院したから、明日退院出来るといってもいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画監督の中で 一番有名なのが、スピルバーグさんだといってもいい。

example_sentences.english: When there are a lot of snacks in my house, I completely eat them all, so I try not to buy them.

example_sentences.japanese: メニューにアイスクリームがあると頼んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: When there is ice-cream on the menu, I unfortunately order it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はよく舌を噛んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally bite my tongue often.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近運動をしてないから太っちゃう。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I haven't been exercising, so I'm totally going to get fat.

example_sentences.japanese: 花が死んじゃうから、花を踏むな。
example_sentences.english: Since the flowers will unfortunately die, don't step on them.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は私のケーキをたべてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My friend finished off my cake. (eaten completely)・(totally)

example_sentences.japanese: お皿がわれてしまった。
example_sentences.english: (Someone) accidentally broke a plate. (unfortunately・totally)

example_sentences.japanese: 今出ないとおくれてしまうよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't leave now, you will unfortunately be late. (totally)

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん！卵を全部つかってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Sorry! I completely used all the eggs. (Sorry! I totally used all the eggs)

example_sentences.japanese: スノーボードに行ったとき、腰をいためてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I unfortunately hurt my lower back when I went snowboarding. (totally)

example_sentences.japanese: あっ、鉛筆を持ってくるのをわすれてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Ah, I totally forgot to bring a pencil. (Ah, I totally forgot to bring a pencil)

example_sentences.japanese: よし！誰も食べないなら、僕がたべてしまおう。
example_sentences.english: Alright! Since no one is going to eat it, I will finish (eating) it off. (eat completely・totally)

example_sentences.japanese: あまりお腹が空いていなかったのに、ケーキをほとんどたべてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I wasn't that hungry, I unfortunately ate most of the cake. (totally)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は冬休みの宿題を全部してしまおう。
example_sentences.english: Today I shall completely finish (doing) all of the homework for winter break. (totally finish)

example_sentences.japanese: そんな大きい声を出さないで！子供がおきてしまうでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Please don't be so loud! You are totally going to wake up the kid. (unfortunately)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は信頼出来ると聞いたから、言ったことを全部しんじてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Since I heard that that person could be trusted, I totally believed everything I heard (from him). (unfortunately)

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームを始める前に宿題を終わらせてしまおう！
example_sentences.english: Let's completely finish my homework before I start playing video games! (I'm going to completely finish my homework before I start playing video games)

example_sentences.japanese: 青木先輩、定時までに社長に頼まれたレポートを完成させてしまいましょうよ。
example_sentences.english: Aoki senpai, let's completely finish the report that our boss has asked us to do before work is over.

general_translation: And・and so, Due to, Because of, Since, Conjunctive
formation: Verb［て］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［て］+ Phrase［な］Adjective + で + PhraseNoun + で + PhraseExceptions: いい ￫ よくて + B
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［て］+ Phrase［な］Adjective + で + PhraseNoun + で + PhraseExceptions: いい ￫ よくて + B
explanation: A casual, simple conjunctive form indicating (A) as being the reason or cause of (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 文字もちいさすぎて読めないよ。
example_sentences.english: The characters are too small and I cannot read them. (I cannot read the characters because they are too small)

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎は静かで落ち着きます。
example_sentences.english: I can relax in the countryside because it is quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: 虫歯で歯が痛い。
example_sentences.english: My tooth hurts because of a cavity.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人が捕まって安心です。
example_sentences.english: I feel safe because the criminal got caught.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は宿題が多くて行けなかった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't go today because I had a lot of homework.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋がきれいでのんびりできます。
example_sentences.english: I can relax because the room is clean. (The room is clean and I can relax)

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーがアメリカにかえって悲しいです。
example_sentences.english: Mary returned to the USA and I am sad. (I am sad because Mary returned to the USA)

example_sentences.japanese: おとなしさんは病気で参加できませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Otonashi was sick and could not participate. (Mr. Otonashi was unable to participate due to being ill)

example_sentences.japanese: おっちゃんのコンサートは雨で中止になった。
example_sentences.english: O-chan's concert has been canceled due to the rain.

example_sentences.japanese: ルームメートがうるさくて全然勉強できない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot study at all because my roommate is noisy. (My roommate is noisy and I cannot study at all)

example_sentences.japanese: たなかさんはベジタリアンだときいてびっくりしました。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Mr. Tanaka is vegetarian and it surprised me. (I was surprised because I heard that Mr. Tanaka is a vegetarian)

example_sentences.japanese: 「お菓子をたくさんたべてお腹が痛いよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I ate many sweets and I have an upset stomach!' ('I have an upset stomach because I ate many sweets')

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にブラックコーヒーをのんで寝られないんだ。
example_sentences.english: I cannot sleep because I drank black coffee before going to bed. (I drank black coffee before going to bed, and cannot sleep)

example_sentences.japanese: 勇者さまは５年前に、交通事故で死んだ。
example_sentences.english: The hero died due to a car accident 5 years ago. (The hero got into a car accident 5 years ago and died)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に合格して嬉しかったです。
example_sentences.english: I passed the Japanese Language Proficiency Test, so I was glad.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週、インフルエンザにかかって、仕事を休んだのです。
example_sentences.english: I was absent from work because I caught the flu last week. (I caught the flu last week and was absent from work)

general_translation: Verbs (Causative-passive voice), To be made to do something, To be forced to do
formation: Examples:［る1］Verb ￫ 見（み）る + させられる［す］Verb ￫ 話（はな）す + させられる［る5］Verb ￫ 座（すわ）る + らせられる座（すわ）る + らされる［う］Verb ￫ 歌（うた）う + わせられる歌（うた）う + 歌（うた）わされる［く］Verb ￫ 歩（ある）く + かせられる歩（ある）く + 歩（ある）かされる［つ］Verb ￫ 打（う）つ + たせられる打（う）つ + 打（う）たされる［ぬ］Verb ￫ 死（し）ぬ + なせられる死（し）ぬ + 死（し）なされる［ぶ］Verb ￫ 飛（と）ぶ + ばせられる飛（と）ぶ + 飛（と）ばされる ［む］Verb ￫ 休（やす）む + ませられる 休（やす）む + 休（やす）まされる［ぐ］Verb ￫ 泳（およ）ぐ + がせられる泳（およ）ぐ + 泳（およ）がされるExceptions: する ￫ させられる くる ￫ こさせられる
