polite_structure: Examples:［る1］Verb ￫ 見（み）る + させられます［す］Verb ￫ 話（はな）す + させられます［る5］Verb ￫ 座（すわ）る + らせられます座（すわ）る + らされます［う］Verb ￫ 歌（うた）う + わせられます歌（うた）う + 歌（うた）わされます［く］Verb ￫ 歩（ある）く + かせられます歩（ある）く + 歩（ある）かされます［つ］Verb ￫ 打（う）つ + たせられます打（う）つ + 打（う）たされます［ぬ］Verb ￫ 死（し）ぬ + なせられます死（し）ぬ + 死（し）なされます［ぶ］Verb ￫ 飛（と）ぶ + ばせられます飛（と）ぶ + 飛（と）ばされます ［む］Verb ￫ 休（やす）む + ませられます 休（やす）む + 休（やす）まされます［ぐ］Verb ￫ 泳（およ）ぐ + がせられます泳（およ）ぐ + 泳（およ）がされますExceptions: する ￫ させられます くる ￫ こさせられます
explanation: An expression used when someone is made to do something, almost always against their will.

example_sentences.japanese: お腹がいっぱいなのに、ケーキをたべさせられた。
example_sentences.english: I was forced to eat the cake even though I was full.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんの家に行くとお腹がいっぱいでもいっぱい食べさせられる。
example_sentences.english: When I go to my grandma's house, she makes me eat a lot, even if I am full.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな事させられるとは思わなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn't think that I would be forced to do something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に色んなお酒を飲ませられたから頭が痛い。
example_sentences.english: Because my senpai made me drink all sorts of alcohol, my head hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に冷たい水を浴びさせられるのが嫌いだ。
example_sentences.english: I don't like it when my friend douses me with cold water.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に力仕事をさせられる。
example_sentences.english: My boss forces me to do physical labor.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に知らないバンドのコンサートに連れてこさせられる。
example_sentences.english: My friend forces me to go to the concert of bands that I do not know.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は兄に宿題をさせられた。
example_sentences.english: I was forced to do homework by my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなことをさせられたの？
example_sentences.english: What kind of things were you forced to do?

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌なことをさせられた。
example_sentences.english: I was made to do awful things.

example_sentences.japanese: あまり見たくない動画をみさせられたのです。
example_sentences.english: I was forced to watch a video I didn't really want to watch.

example_sentences.japanese: 母に掃除とか、洗い物とかさせられた。
example_sentences.english: I was made to clean and wash dishes by my mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に腐った牛乳をのませられた。
example_sentences.english: I was forced to drink spoiled milk by my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: クラスメイトに嫌なことをたくさんさせられたから、明日先生に言う。
example_sentences.english: My classmate made me do a lot of things I don't like, so I am going to tell the teacher tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームを楽しんでいたのに、やめさせられた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I was enjoying the videogame, I was forced to stop.

example_sentences.japanese: 算数だけでなく、理科の勉強もさせられます。
example_sentences.english: I will be forced to study not only math but science too.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を出せば、全部はらわせられるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you take out your money, you will be made to pay, you know.

example_sentences.japanese: 少しも喉が渇いていなかったのに、ジュースをのませられた。
example_sentences.english: I wasn't thirsty in the least bit, but I was forced to drink juice.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は全然お金を持っていないのに、皆の分をださせられた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I have absolutely no money, I was made to pay for everyone's share. (made to take out)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃は兄が勉強をさせられていた。
example_sentences.english: When we were still kids, my older brother was forced to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃は兄に勉強をさせられていた。
example_sentences.english: When we were still children, my older brother forced me to study.

general_translation: By, With, On, By means of, ~ing with
formation: Verb［て］+ PhraseNoun + で + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ PhraseNoun + で + Phrase
explanation: A casual, simple conjunctive form showing that (B) was done in the way of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: フライパンをつかって、料理をします。
example_sentences.english: I am making a meal with a frying pan.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はハサミで野菜を切ります。
example_sentences.english: I cut my vegetables using scissors.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝坊をしたので慌てて準備をした。
example_sentences.english: Since I overslept, I got ready in a flurry.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日泳いでトレーニングをしています。
example_sentences.english: I train by swimming every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は車で仕事に行く。
example_sentences.english: My father goes to work by car.

example_sentences.japanese: あるいて帰るつもりだよ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to come home on (by) foot.

example_sentences.japanese: けいまくんは自転車にのって学校に行っています。
example_sentences.english: Keima goes to school by (riding a) bike.

example_sentences.japanese: 総理大臣は新幹線を利用して東京に戻りました。
example_sentences.english: The prime minister returned to Tokyo by (using the) shinkansen.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあの船にのってアメリカに来た。
example_sentences.english: He came to the USA on that/by riding that ship.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのすみません、駅までどのくらいありますか。」「駅はここから徒歩で５分くらいです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Excuse me, how far is the railway station?''The station is about 5 minutes on (by) foot from here.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「毎日ＮＨＫニュースをよんで日本語を勉強しています。」
example_sentences.english: 'I study Japanese by reading NHK news every day.'

example_sentences.japanese: 洗っていない手で目や鼻などを触ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not touch things like your eyes and nose with unwashed hands.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代人は絵文字をつかってＳＮＳやメールなどで感情を表すことができる。
example_sentences.english: Modern people can express emotions via social networking, mail, etc. by using emoji. (with)

example_sentences.japanese: チャイムの音が聞こえた時、いそいで服を着て下まで走った。
example_sentences.english: When I heard the sound of the door chime, I put clothes on in a hurry (with haste), and ran down the (stairs).

example_sentences.japanese: 水と石鹸で手を丁寧に洗いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's wash hands carefully (thoroughly) with soap and water.

example_sentences.japanese: お祖母さん：「はるこちゃん、どうやってスマホで写真をとるの？」孫、はるこ：「こうやって。(撮り方を示す）」
example_sentences.english: Grandmother: 'Haruko, how do I take photos with my smartphone?'Granddaughter, Haruko: 'Like this.' (Showing how to take photos)

general_translation: Something is done, Has been done, Remaining state
formation: (Transitive) Verb［て］+ ある
casual_structure: (Transitive) Verb［て］+ ある
polite_structure: (Transitive) Verb［て］+ あります
explanation: An expression that is used with transitive verbs, to show that something has been left a certain way.

example_sentences.japanese: このドアはあけてある。
example_sentences.english: This door has been left open.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭にトウモロコシが植えてあるから気を付けてね。
example_sentences.english: Corn has been planted in the yard, so please be careful. (Literally 'corn is in the state of having been planted')

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの弁当は机の上に置いてあるよ。
example_sentences.english: I have left your lunch on the desk. (Literally 'your lunch is in the state of having been left on the desk')

example_sentences.japanese: 車は駐車場の真ん中に止めてある 。
example_sentences.english: I parked the car in the middle of the parking lot. (Literally 'your car is in the state of having been stopped in the carpark')

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ台の上においてあるよ。
example_sentences.english: It has been placed on top of the TV stand.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の準備してあるんですか。
example_sentences.english: Have tomorrow's preparations been done?

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の準備をしてあるので、もう寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I have done my preparation for tomorrow so I am going to bed.

example_sentences.japanese: １０００年前に建てられたビルがまだのこしてある。
example_sentences.english: The building that was built 1000 years ago is still standing.

example_sentences.japanese: もう晩ご飯をつくってあるから、早く帰って来て。
example_sentences.english: Dinner has already been made, so hurry home.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の劇のセリフをもうかんがえてあるから、早く書きたい。
example_sentences.english: I have already thought about my lines for the next play, so I want to write them quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の部屋にはってあったポスターはどこにいったんですか。
example_sentences.english: Where did the poster that had been hanging in my room go?

example_sentences.japanese: ここにおいてあった漢字テストがどこに行ったか分かる？
example_sentences.english: Do you know where the kanji test that had been placed here went?

example_sentences.japanese: 和室においてある布団をこっちに持って来てくれる？
example_sentences.english: Can you bring the futon that is in the Japanese-style room here for me?

example_sentences.japanese: ツリーにかざってあるオーナメント(の写真)を撮り直さなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to retake the photo of the ornaments that are on the tree.

general_translation: Want ~ to ~ like ~, Want ~ to be able to ~, Want ~ to ~ in the way of ~
formation: Verb + ように + Verb［て］ + ほしいNoun + のように + Verb［て］ + ほしい
casual_structure: Verb + ように + Verb［て］ + ほしいNoun + のように + Verb［て］ + ほしい
polite_structure: Verb + ように + Verb［て］ + ほしい + ですNoun + のように + Verb［て］ + ほしい + です
explanation: A phrase used to highlight that someone wants another person to do something in the manner of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ブラジルのようにまけてほしくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want (you) to lose like Brazil.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたに漢字を書けるようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to be able to write kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁護士になれるように頑張ってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to work your hardest, so that you can become a lawyer.

example_sentences.japanese: このチームが大会で勝てるようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want this team to be able to win a tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: お前にはスポーツ選手のように走ってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to run like an athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: もっとアナウンサーのように話してほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to talk more like an announcer.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故が無くなるように運転をしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want people to drive in a way that will reduce accidents.

example_sentences.japanese: どのようにかいてほしいですか。
example_sentences.english: In what way do (you) want me to write this?

example_sentences.japanese: ウサイン・ボルトのようにはしってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want (you) to run like Usain Bolt.

example_sentences.japanese: 頭がよくなるようにべんきょうしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want (you) to study in a way that allows you to become smart.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちの子供には君のようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want our children to become like you.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリが役に立つようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want this app to become useful. (in the way of)

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの前でも大人のようにしゃべってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want (you) to talk like an adult even in front of my baby.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が出来るようになってほしいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think I want you to be able to make friends. (in the way of)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を話せるようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want (you) to be able to speak Japanese. (in the way of)

example_sentences.japanese: この電車にも新幹線のようにはやくはしってほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want this train to run fast like a bullet train.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家をあなたの家のようにあつかってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to treat my house like it's your house. (in the way of)

example_sentences.japanese: イーロン・マスクさんがロードスターを火星に送るようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want Elon Musk to become able to send a roadster to Mars. (in the way of)

example_sentences.japanese: トムに友達ができるようになってほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want Tom to be able to make some friends.

formation: Verb［ている］+ 間（あいだ）に
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ 間（あいだ）に
explanation: A phrase that highlights when something happens during the broad time frame of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 妻がねているあいだに、私は好きなことができる。
example_sentences.english: While my wife is sleeping, I can do what I like.

example_sentences.japanese: ねえ、数えているあいだには話しかけないで。
example_sentences.english: Hey, don't talk to me while I'm counting.

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物を運んでいるあいだに転んで怪我をした。
example_sentences.english: I tripped and hurt myself when I was carrying luggage.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行っているあいだに家に泥棒が入った。
example_sentences.english: While I was on a trip, a burglar came into my house.

example_sentences.japanese: サッカーをしているあいだに電話がかかってきました。
example_sentences.english: I got a phone call while playing soccer.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をしているあいだにお腹が空いてきた。
example_sentences.english: I became hungry while studying.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理をしているあいだに子ども達が帰って来た。
example_sentences.english: While I was cooking, my kids came home.

example_sentences.japanese: パンをやいているあいだにお皿を出した。
example_sentences.english: While I was toasting some bread, I took out a plate.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢をみているあいだに目が動いていたよ。
example_sentences.english: While you were dreaming your eyes were moving (you know).

example_sentences.japanese: 留守しているあいだに泥棒が 入った。
example_sentences.english: While I was out, a thief came into my house.

example_sentences.japanese: お湯をわかしているあいだにティーバッグを用意した。
example_sentences.english: While I was boiling water, I readied a tea bag.

example_sentences.japanese: ハイキングをしているあいだに狼の鳴き声が聞こえた。
example_sentences.english: While I was hiking I heard a wolf's howl.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みをとっているあいだにボスに話しかけられた。
example_sentences.english: While taking a break, my boss chatted to me unfortunately.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画をみているあいだに、お父さんが帰って来た。
example_sentences.english: While I was watching a movie, my father came home.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転をしているあいだに、目の前で事故が起こった。
example_sentences.english: While I was driving, an accident happened right before my eyes.

formation: Verb［なくて］ + （も） + いい
casual_structure: Verb［なくて］ + （も） + いい
polite_structure: Verb［なくて］ + （も） + いい + です
explanation: A grammar point used to highlight that not doing something is okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しいなら、いかなくてもいいです。
example_sentences.english: If you are busy, you do not have to go.

example_sentences.japanese: ミカは悪くないから謝らなくてもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Mika, you are not in the wrong, so you don't have to apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: その手紙はもう届けなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: It's okay if you don't deliver that letter anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は会社に来なくていいよ。
example_sentences.english: It is fine if you don't come to the office today.

example_sentences.japanese: 掃除をしなくてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: It is alright even if I don't clean?

example_sentences.japanese: その青いセーターをきなくてもいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: It is alright even if you do not wear that blue sweater.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにおこらなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to be that angry.

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上のまなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to drink more than this.

example_sentences.japanese: 何もしなくてもいい？
example_sentences.english: I don't have to do anything?

example_sentences.japanese: それをしなくてもいいと聞いたよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that it is alright even if you don't do that.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日掃除をしたから、今日はしなくてもいいだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since I cleaned yesterday, I don't have to clean today, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にはバスと電車とタクシーがあるので、車をかわなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: In Japan there are buses, trains and taxis, so you don't have to buy a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日買い物に行けば、週末はいかなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: If I can go shopping today, then I don't have to go on the weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 全部の漢字をおぼえなくてもいいよ。２０００字覚えたら新聞を読めるよ。
example_sentences.english: It is okay even if you don't remember all of the kanji. If you remember 2000 characters, you can read the newspaper.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日試合があるでしょう？練習をしなくてもいいの？
example_sentences.english: You have a match tomorrow, right? Is it alright even if you don't practice?

formation: Verb［て］+ みる
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ みる
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ みます
explanation: A common way to express that (A) will be attempted. To do (A) and see how it goes.

example_sentences.japanese: イルカとおよいでみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to try swimming with dolphins.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当においしいの？今度食べてみるよ！
example_sentences.english: Is it really delicious? Next time I'll try it!

example_sentences.japanese: これ飲んでみる？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to try this drink?

example_sentences.japanese: だまされたと思って食べてみてよ。
example_sentences.english: Try and eat it as if I tricked you into eating it. (Believe it or not, this tastes good)

example_sentences.japanese: もう一度電源を切ってみてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try to turn it off once more.

example_sentences.japanese: このボール投げてみ。
example_sentences.english: Try and throw this ball.

example_sentences.japanese: まず、たべてみてください。
example_sentences.english: First, please try to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: 柔道をしてみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to try to do Judo.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で、しらべてみるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I intend to try to look it up at the library.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週末、スキーをしてみた。
example_sentences.english: I tried skiing last weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の夏は、海でおよいでみたいんです。
example_sentences.english: I want to try to swim in the ocean this summer.

example_sentences.japanese: これをけしてみてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try to erase this.

example_sentences.japanese: このコーラをのんでみます。
example_sentences.english: I will try to drink this cola.

example_sentences.japanese: あの赤い靴をはいてみたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to try on those red shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の金曜日は仕事に電車でいってみます。
example_sentences.english: On Friday of next week, I will try to go to work by train.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜はフランス料理をつくってみます。
example_sentences.english: Tonight I will try to make French cuisine.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から、フランス語をまなんでみるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: From tomorrow, I intend to try learning French. (Try to learn)

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末に野球をしてみる。
example_sentences.english: I will try playing baseball this weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: あの新しいショッピングモールに行ってみたよ！すごい良かった！
example_sentences.english: I tried going to that new shopping mall! It was so good!

example_sentences.japanese: タケルにもらった靴を履いてみたけど、俺の足がデカすぎるから入らなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to wear the shoes that Takeru gave me, but my feet were too big so they didn't fit.

formation: Verb［て］+ すみません
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ すみません
explanation: A polite phrase that expresses the speaker's apologetic feelings for doing (A).

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのケーキをたべてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for eating your cake.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせの時間に遅れてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry for coming later than the arranged meeting time.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子さんの髪をピンクに染めてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry for dyeing your son's hair pink.

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯を残してすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I didn't eat all the food. (It unfortunately resulted in that I did not finish eating all the food)

example_sentences.japanese: 遅くなってすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I am late.

example_sentences.japanese: 約束をやぶってすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for breaking my promise.

example_sentences.japanese: おこってすみません。怒りたくなかった。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for getting angry. I didn't want to be angry.

example_sentences.japanese: しゃべりすぎてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for talking too much.

example_sentences.japanese: 家事をしなくてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for not doing any housework.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗してすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for failing/messing up.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りまでにできなくてすみませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for not being able to do it by the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに招待できなくてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for not being able to invite you to the party.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのお金を別の人にわたしてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I gave another person your money.

example_sentences.japanese: 分かりにくい説明をしてすみませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry for providing a difficult-to-understand explanation.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式なのにこの格好でいってすみません。
example_sentences.english: I’m sorry for going dressed like this, even though it’s a wedding.

general_translation: To do something for someone, As a favor for
formation: Verb［て］+ あげる
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ あげる
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ あげます
explanation: A polite, yet sometimes insulting expression, used when giving something to another.

example_sentences.japanese: 母に花をかってあげた。
example_sentences.english: I bought flowers (as a favor) for my mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が妹にお菓子を買ってあげる。
example_sentences.english: My father buys snacks for my sister.

example_sentences.japanese: いいよ、俺がやってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: It's okay, I'll do it for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は私が送ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, (as a favor) I will send you off.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのおばあさんをてつだってあげましょうか。
example_sentences.english: Shall we give assistance to (as a favor for) that lady?

example_sentences.japanese: このプレゼントをお父さんにわたしてあげてください。
example_sentences.english: Please hand over this present to your dad. (Give to)

example_sentences.japanese: ユカに消しゴムをかしてあげてください。
example_sentences.english: Please lend your eraser to Yuka. (For Yuka)

example_sentences.japanese: 寂しそうにしているから、ハグしてあげましょう。
example_sentences.english: Because they look lonely let's give them a hug. (For them)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に優しくしてあげましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's be nice (as a favor) to our friends. (For our friends)

example_sentences.japanese: 息子がオモチャを無くしたから、さがしてあげた。
example_sentences.english: Since my son lost his toy, I searched for it. (For my son)

example_sentences.japanese: 今暇だから、晩ご飯をつくってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: Since I'm not busy now, I will make dinner (as a favor) for you.

example_sentences.japanese: エレンさんがミカサさんに美しい花をもってきてあげた。
example_sentences.english: Eren brought beautiful flowers (as a favor) for Mikasa.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が泣いていたから、よしよししてあげた。
example_sentences.english: I gave comfort to my daughter because she was crying. (For my daughter)

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの人の話をよくきいてあげましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's listen to the stories of people around us. (Lend an ear to, for the people)

example_sentences.japanese: 君の漢字の勉強の仕方をトムにおしえてあげてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach Tom your method of studying Kanji. (For Tom)

example_sentences.japanese: 部長、今夜は俺がおごってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: Boss, I'll pay for the food tonight (as a favor). (Natural Japanese, but may be considered rude by the boss)

example_sentences.japanese: 犬に餌をやる。
example_sentences.english: To feed the dog. (To give food to the dog because they need it to live)

example_sentences.japanese: 犬に餌をあげる。
example_sentences.english: To feed the dog. (To give food to the dog because you want it to have the best life)

example_sentences.japanese: お前が食いたいものは何でも作ってやるよ。
example_sentences.english: I will make anything you want to eat for you.

general_translation: To do something for someone (usually you)
formation: Verb［て］+ くれるVerb［ないで］+ くれるPoliteness Levels
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ くれるVerb［ないで］+ くれるPoliteness Levels
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ くれますかVerb［ないで］+ くれますかPoliteness Levels
explanation: A phrase used to highlight that the speaker or someone close to them is having a favor done for them.

example_sentences.japanese: あのグラスをここにもってきてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Would you bring me that glass?

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんはいつも美味しいご飯を作ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: Grandma always makes delicious food for us!

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が旅行から帰ってくるとお土産を持って来てくれる。
example_sentences.english: When my friend comes back from vacation, they bring me souvenirs.

example_sentences.japanese: パパ、電気を消してくれる？
example_sentences.english: Dad, can you turn the lights off for me?

example_sentences.japanese: お願いだから急いでくれ。
example_sentences.english: I'm begging you, could ya hurry it up (for me)?

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字の意味をおしえてくれますか。
example_sentences.english: Would you teach me the meaning of this kanji? (for me)

example_sentences.japanese: 私をあいしてくれますか。
example_sentences.english: Will you love me? (do me the favor of)

example_sentences.japanese: ママが書きやすいペンをかってくれた。
example_sentences.english: My mom bought a pen that is easy to write with. (For me)

example_sentences.japanese: 喋らないでだまっていってくれますか。
example_sentences.english: Could you not talk, shut up and go? (for me)

example_sentences.japanese: ごめん、牛乳もかってきてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Sorry, could you also buy some milk (and come back)? (for me)

example_sentences.japanese: サンタさん、何をもってきてくれたの？
example_sentences.english: Santa, what did you bring? (for me)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が私の切符をかってくれました。
example_sentences.english: My friend bought my ticket. (For me)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の友達はいつも相談をきいてくれる。
example_sentences.english: My friend always does me the favor of listening to my problems.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べる前にテーブルの上を綺麗にしてくれますか。
example_sentences.english: Before we eat, could you clean the table for me?

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが来るので、コーヒーをいれてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Since we are having some guests, won't you make some coffee? (for me)

example_sentences.japanese: 怖いから、そばにいてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Because I'm scared, could you stay by me? (Being there for me)

example_sentences.japanese: 遊園地に連れて行ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: Someone will take me to the amusement park. (They are taking me for my benefit)

example_sentences.japanese: 遊園地に連れて行ってもらう。
example_sentences.english: Someone is taking me to the amusement park. (I am having someone take me)

example_sentences.japanese: 遊園地に連れて行って頂く。
example_sentences.english: Someone is taking me to the amusement park. (I am being bestowed the act of being taken)

general_translation: To get someone to do, To have someone do
formation: Verb［て］+ もらうPoliteness Levels
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ もらうPoliteness Levels
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ もらいますPoliteness Levels
explanation: An expression used when someone is getting another person to do something for them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は母に宿題をしてもらった。
example_sentences.english: I had my mom do my homework (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が話せないから友達に行き方を聞いてもらう。
example_sentences.english: Because I can't speak Japanese, I'm going to have my friend ask for directions on my behalf.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は虫が嫌いなので妻に虫を捕ってもらう。
example_sentences.english: Since I hate bugs, I get my wife to catch them (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は朝から頭が痛かったから医者に見てもらった。
example_sentences.english: Because my head hurt since the morning yesterday, I had a doctor look at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝から頭が痛かったから病院に行って、医者が見てくれた。
example_sentences.english: Because I had a headache since this morning, I went to the doctor and he checked it out for me.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスに犬をかってもらうかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I might have (someone) buy me a dog for Christmas.

example_sentences.japanese: (誰かに)この仕事をてつだってもらう。
example_sentences.english: I will get someone to help with this work.

example_sentences.japanese: ユカは誰かにてつだってもらったかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Yuka might have gotten someone to help her.

example_sentences.japanese: まず掃除をしてもらうと思う。
example_sentences.english: First I think I will have you clean (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: クッキーを焼いている時、彼女にコーヒーをいれてもらった。
example_sentences.english: I had my girlfriend make coffee while I baked cookies. (For me)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は誰にでも何でもしてもらうことが出来る。
example_sentences.english: That person can get anyone to do anything. ( For them)

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降りそうだから、傘をもっていってもらってね。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it might rain, so have them take an umbrella (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: 伝えにくいけど、頑張って説明してもらいましょう。
example_sentences.english: It is difficult to express, but let's have you explain to the best of your ability. (for us)

example_sentences.japanese: このタイヤもうだめです。(誰かに)タイヤ交換をしてもらってください。
example_sentences.english: This tire is no longer any good. Please have it changed (by someone).

example_sentences.japanese: 雑誌にあった漢字の読み方が分からなかったので、ネイティブによんでもらいます。
example_sentences.english: I did not understand the reading of a kanji in a magazine, so I will have a native read it for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は運転が下手だから、私が運転して、彼には後ろにのってもらった。
example_sentences.english: He is terrible at driving, so I drove and had him ride in the back.

formation: Verb［stem］+ なさい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ なさい
explanation: A stern but semi-polite way to request that someone do something.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強しなさい。
example_sentences.english: Study!

example_sentences.japanese: 遊んでいないで勉強しなさい！
example_sentences.english: Stop playing and study!

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強しな。
example_sentences.english: You should study.

example_sentences.japanese: お前も悪いから謝りな。
example_sentences.english: You are also at fault, so you should apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く寝なさい！
example_sentences.english: Hurry up and sleep!

example_sentences.japanese: 早くかえりなさい。
example_sentences.english: Hurry up and go home!

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜をたべなさい。
example_sentences.english: Eat your vegetables!

example_sentences.japanese: これをパパにわたしなさい。
example_sentences.english: Hand this to your dad.

example_sentences.japanese: 注意しなさい。
example_sentences.english: Be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 道路を渡る前に右と左を確認しなさい。
example_sentences.english: Before you cross the road check both your right and your left.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームをやめなさい。
example_sentences.english: Stop playing your video game.

example_sentences.japanese: あっ、泥棒が逃げた！つかまえなさい！
example_sentences.english: Ah! The thief escaped! Seize him!

example_sentences.japanese: 本当の気持ちをつたえなさい。
example_sentences.english: Tell us your true feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 丁寧にはなしなさい。
example_sentences.english: Speak politely.

example_sentences.japanese: 凄い匂い！シャワーあびなさい。
example_sentences.english: What a smell! Take a shower!

example_sentences.japanese: 妹に人形をかえしなさい。
example_sentences.english: Give the doll back to your sister.

example_sentences.japanese: このクッキーを食べな。
example_sentences.english: You should eat this cookie.

example_sentences.japanese: このクッキーを食べるな。
example_sentences.english: Do not eat this cookie.

formation: Verb［て］+ Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ Phrase
explanation: A casual, simple conjunctive form highlighting non-sequence, but contrasting states.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はくもっていて寒かった。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday was cloudy and cold.

example_sentences.japanese: お姉ちゃんは毎晩勉強をして弟は毎晩ゲームをしている。
example_sentences.english: My older sister studies every night, and my younger brother plays games.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は買い物に行って、私はごみを捨てに行った。
example_sentences.english: My wife went shopping, while I went to throw away the trash.

example_sentences.japanese: タケルはご飯を食べてナオミはパンを食べる。
example_sentences.english: Takeru eats rice, and Naomi eats bread.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝は雨が降って夕方は晴れた。
example_sentences.english: It rained this morning, and then it cleared up in the afternoon. (There is no particular emphasis on either event)

example_sentences.japanese: 朝は雨が降ったけど夕方は晴れた。
example_sentences.english: It rained this morning, but then it cleared up in the afternoon. (There is emphasis on that it stopped raining)

example_sentences.japanese: チトゲさんはうたってオノデラさんは踊っている。
example_sentences.english: Chitoge is singing and Onodera is dancing. (but・contrast)

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がふって雷が鳴る。
example_sentences.english: It rains and thunders.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあさんはいつもラジオをきいておじいさんはいつもテレビを観る。
example_sentences.english: My grandma always listens to the radio, and my grandfather always watches tv. (but・contrast)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はピアノをひけてドラムも上手に叩ける。
example_sentences.english: She can play the piano, and also she can play drums well.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの猫はちょっとふとっていて、小さくてとーってもかわいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Our cat is a bit plump and small, it's super cute!

example_sentences.japanese: 妹はカナダにいって、弟はイギリスに行った。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister went to Canada, and my younger brother went to the United Kingdom. (but・contrast)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語がはなせて漢字も書けます。
example_sentences.english: He can speak Japanese, and also write kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: ボブさん：「太陽がかがやいていて天気が良い。」
example_sentences.english: Bob-san: 'The sun is shining, and the weather is nice.'

example_sentences.japanese: この水筒はおりたためて、ポケットやバックパックで持ち運びやすい。
example_sentences.english: This water bottle is foldable, and is easy to carry in a pocket, backpack, etc.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はジャガイモの皮をむいて姉さんは油で魚を焼いた。
example_sentences.english: I peeled the potatoes and my elder sister fried the fish in oil.

example_sentences.japanese: テキストメッセージの打ち合い：「あんたたち、何してるの？」「オレはうんこしてて、トムは洗い物をしてる。」
example_sentences.english: Via text message: 'What are you guys doing?''I am pooping, and Tom is washing dishes.'

example_sentences.japanese: かみねさんは東京にいって京都に行った。京都に行ったのが先だったけど。
example_sentences.english: Kamine went to Tokyo and Kyoto. She went to Kyoto first though.

formation: Verb［ない］+ で。
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ で。
explanation: A casual, simple conjunctive form used as an abbreviated way of saying please don't do (A).

example_sentences.japanese: あそこの公園は危ないので、あそばないで。
example_sentences.english: Since that park is dangerous, (please) don't play there.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「そこの生徒、授業中に寝ないで！」
example_sentences.english: Teacher: 'The student there, please don't sleep during class!'

example_sentences.japanese: 母が娘に：「知らない人についていかないで！約束よ。」
example_sentences.english: Mother to her daughter: 'Please don't go with people you don't know! That's a promise.'

example_sentences.japanese: 妻が夫に：「貯金をしたいから、無駄な物にお金を使わないで。」
example_sentences.english: Wife to her husband: 'I want to save up, so please don't use money recklessly.'

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫にあるケーキはまだたべないでね。
example_sentences.english: (Please) don't eat the cake in the refrigerator yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べてからジェットコースターにのらないで。
example_sentences.english: (Please) don't ride a rollercoaster after eating.

example_sentences.japanese: 「バカにしないでよ！はんだくん。」
example_sentences.english: '(Please) don't make a fool out of me! Handa.'

example_sentences.japanese: ここは病院なので、走ったり、騒いだりしないで。
example_sentences.english: Since this is a hospital, (please) don't do things like run or be boisterous.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が子供に言う：「まだ熱いから、さわらないでね。」
example_sentences.english: Mother speaking to her child: 'It is still hot, so (please) don't touch it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が子供に言う：「いい子だから、なかないでね。」
example_sentences.english: Mother speaking to her child: 'You are a good child, so (please) don't cry, okay? '

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前に携帯を使ったり、おかしを食べたりしないで。
example_sentences.english: Before going to bed, (please) don't do things like use your phone or eat candy.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から旅行に行くから、風邪をひかないでね。
example_sentences.english: Since you are going on a trip tomorrow, (please) don't catch a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉が弟に言う：「頼むから、親には何もいわないで。」
example_sentences.english: Elder sister speaking to her younger brother: 'I am asking you, so (please) don't tell our parents.'

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が子供に言う：「お父さんはまだ寝ているので、大きい声をださないでね。」
example_sentences.english: Mother speaking to her child: 'Since dad is still sleeping, (please) don't talk loudly.'

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が母親に言う：「ママ、すぐに戻ってくるよ。しんぱいしないで。」
example_sentences.english: A child speaking to their mother: 'Mom, I will come back soon. (Please) don't worry.'

formation: Verb［て］ + くれて + ありがとう
casual_structure: Verb［て］ + くれて + ありがとう
polite_structure: Verb［て］ + くれて + ありがとう + ございます
explanation: A polite expression used to thank someone for doing something for you.

example_sentences.japanese: てつだってくれてありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for helping (me).

example_sentences.japanese: いつもゴキブリを捕まえてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for always catching the cockroaches.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキを買って来てくれてありがとう！
example_sentences.english: Thank you for buying the cake for me!

example_sentences.japanese: いつも一緒にいてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for always being with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅までおくってくれてありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for taking me to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩御飯をつくってくれてありがとう！
example_sentences.english: Thanks for making dinner (for me)!

example_sentences.japanese: 遅くなってごめん！まっていてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I am late! Thank you so much for waiting (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことをいってくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for saying those things (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: 看板に載っている漢字の読み方をおしえてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for teaching me the readings of the kanji on that billboard.

example_sentences.japanese: いい匂いがするコーヒーをいれてくれてありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for brewing some lovely-smelling coffee (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: １００円をかしてくれてありがとう。また後で返すね。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for lending me 100 yen. I will pay you back later.

example_sentences.japanese: オモチャを欲しがっていた 子供にかってくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for buying a toy for the child (that wanted the toy) (on my behalf).

example_sentences.japanese: 遅くまで一緒にいてくれてありがとう。助かった。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for being with me until late. It was really helpful.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しそうな料理をつくってくれてありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you so much for making a meal that looks delicious (for me).

example_sentences.japanese: 弁当を袋に入れてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for putting my bento in a bag! (Slightly unnatural Japanese, if just plainly thanking someone for doing their job)

general_translation: Won't you?, Will you?, Could you?, Can you?, Would you?
formation: Verb［て］+ くれない (か) ？Verb［て］+ もらえない (か) ？Could you notVerb［ないで］+ くれない (か) ？Verb［ないで］+ もらえない (か) ？Levels of politeness
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ くれない (か) ？Verb［て］+ もらえない (か) ？Could you notVerb［ないで］+ くれない (か) ？Verb［ないで］+ もらえない (か) ？Levels of politeness
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ くれません (か) ？Verb［て］+ もらえません (か) ？Could you notVerb［ないで］+ くれません (か) ？Verb［ないで］+ もらえません (か) ？Levels of politeness
explanation: A polite way of asking someone if they will do (A) for you. Could I not have you do (A) for me.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホをつかわせてくれないか？
example_sentences.english: Won't you let me use your phone?

example_sentences.japanese: テレビを点けてもらえないか。
example_sentences.english: Could I get you to turn the TV on for me, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 私に漢字を教えてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Would you not teach me kanji? (Would you please teach me kanji?)

example_sentences.japanese: 道を調べてもらえない？
example_sentences.english: Could I get you to look up the way?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日だけ自転車を貸してくれないか？
example_sentences.english: Just for today, would you not let me borrow your bike?

example_sentences.japanese: お茶をいれてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Won't you make some tea for me?

example_sentences.japanese: うちでもはたらいてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Won't you work at my place (for me) too?

example_sentences.japanese: こっちに醤油をとってもらえない？
example_sentences.english: Won't you pass (take) the soy sauce (for me)?

example_sentences.japanese: 米をたいておいてくれない？
example_sentences.english: Won't you cook some rice (in advance) for me?

example_sentences.japanese: ヘアドライヤーをかしてもらえない？朝だけ。
example_sentences.english: Could I get you to lend me your hairdryer? Only for the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親：「ともこ、きーちゃんに周りを案内してあげてくれない？」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'Tomoko, won't you show Ki-chan around (for me)?'

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬を見たら電話してくれないか？
example_sentences.english: If you see my dog, won't you give me a call (for me)?

example_sentences.japanese: ひっき、まずいって知ってるけど、このクッキーをたべてみてくれないか？
example_sentences.english: Hikki, I know that these cookies are not very good, but won't you try (eating) them for me?

example_sentences.japanese: それは僕一人では出来ないよ。たすけてくれない？
example_sentences.english: I can't do that on my own. Won't you help me?

example_sentences.japanese: 夜遅くに電話しないでくれない？
example_sentences.english: Would you not call me late at night (for me)?

example_sentences.japanese: まつさに先生：「みしまさん、ちょっとにったさんを手伝ってあげてくれない？」
example_sentences.english: Matsusani-sensei: 'Mishima-san, won't you help Nitta a bit (on my behalf)?'

formation: Verb +（の(1)）+ だろうか［い］Adjective +（の(1)）+ だろうか［な］Adjective +（な + の(1)）+ だろうかNoun +（な + の(1)）+ だろうか(1) ん
casual_structure: Verb +（の(1)）+ だろうか［い］Adjective +（の(1)）+ だろうか［な］Adjective +（な + の(1)）+ だろうかNoun +（な + の(1)）+ だろうか(1) ん
polite_structure: Verb +（の(1)）+ でしょうか［い］Adjective +（の(1)）+ でしょうか［な］Adjective +（な + の(1)）+ でしょうかNoun +（な + の(1)）+ でしょうか(1) ん
explanation: A somewhat casual phrase to express that the speaker is wondering about (A), because it is uncertain.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の都合が悪いだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it is bad timing for him?

example_sentences.japanese: トムは私を誘うだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if Tom will invite me. (の omitted)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は本当に弁護士だろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that person is actually a lawyer. (なの omitted)

example_sentences.japanese: そんな高い鉛筆をトムが買うのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if Tom will buy a pencil that expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: あの車はキムの車なのでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that car belongs to Kim.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちのチームは勝てるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if our team can win.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は本当に彼氏が欲しいのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if she actually wants a boyfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は大丈夫なのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that person is okay.

example_sentences.japanese: あれは本当に食べ物なのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that is really food.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ時間だろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it is about time.

example_sentences.japanese: 練習したら、うまくなるだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if I will get better at it if I practice.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人が見つかるだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if the criminal will be found.

example_sentences.japanese: この小屋に虫が居るのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if there are any bugs in this storehouse.

example_sentences.japanese: この湖は汚そうだけど、入っていいのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: This lake looks really dirty. I wonder if it is okay to get in.

example_sentences.japanese: 賞味期限が過ぎているけど、食べていいのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: It is past the expiration date. I wonder if it is okay to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: このビルの屋上から何が見えるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what you can see from the roof of this building.

example_sentences.japanese: 後で本当に家に行っていいのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it is really okay to go to his/her house later.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆が言っているけど、僕の性格は本当に変わったのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Everyone is saying it, but I wonder if my personality really changed.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語がもの凄く難しいので、上手になるのだろうかと思った。
example_sentences.english: I thought, since Japanese is extremely difficult, I wonder if I will become proficient.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校生の時納豆を食べてみたけど、凄い不味かった。本当に納豆が好きになるのだろうかと思った。
example_sentences.english: When I was a highschool student I tried natto, but it was gross. I wondered whether I would really come to like it.

example_sentences.japanese: この人が言っていることは本当なのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if what this person is saying is true. (Said while talking to oneself)

example_sentences.japanese: そこに息子を連れて行っていいのだろうか？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if I can take my son there. (Said while talking to oneself)

formation: お + Verb［stem］+ になるご(1) + ［する］Verb + になるいく・くる・いる ￫ おいでになる(1) お, limited to ［する］Verbs like: 電話（でんわ）する、勉強（べんきょう）する、散歩（さんぽ）する
casual_structure: お + Verb［stem］+ になるご(1) + ［する］Verb + になるいく・くる・いる ￫ おいでになる(1) お, limited to ［する］Verbs like: 電話（でんわ）する、勉強（べんきょう）する、散歩（さんぽ）する
polite_structure: お + Verb［stem］+ になりますご(1) + ［する］Verb + になりますいきます・きます・います ￫ おいでになります(1) お, limited to ［する］Verbs like: 電話（でんわ）する、勉強（べんきょう）する、散歩（さんぽ）する
explanation: A polite, modern expression, that respectfully states the action of others.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はおかえりになりました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher has gone home.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様がお見えになるのは３時頃です。
example_sentences.english: The time that the customers will come will be around 3 o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆様、お立ちになってください。
example_sentences.english: We request that everyone stand up.

example_sentences.japanese: この資料がご参考になれば幸いです。
example_sentences.english: It would bring me great happiness if this document could be a useful reference for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長はどういう番組をご覧になるのですか？
example_sentences.english: Boss, what kind of TV shows do you watch?

example_sentences.japanese: ハリーポッターをおよみになりましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you read Harry Potter?

example_sentences.japanese: 父上はもうおかえりになったんですね。
example_sentences.english: Father has already gone home, hasn't he.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯医者がおみえになるのは３時です。
example_sentences.english: The dentist will arrive at 3 o'clock.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは何時頃おかえりになります？
example_sentences.english: Around what time will father return home?

example_sentences.japanese: この雑誌はもうおよみになりましたか。
example_sentences.english: Have you already read this magazine?

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの商品をおもとめになったお客様。
example_sentences.english: The customer who requested this product.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、田中様がおめしあがりになっています。
example_sentences.english: Now, Tanaka-sama is eating.

example_sentences.japanese: おとりになった切符を忘れないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not forget the ticket you took.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生：「あのすみません。まきせ博士はもうおでかけになりましたか？」
example_sentences.english: University student: 'Excuse me. Has Dr. Makise already left?'

example_sentences.japanese: おいでになる時間をお伝えください。
example_sentences.english: Please let me know what time you will arrive (come).

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木さんは学校長とおあいになります。
example_sentences.english: Suzuki-san will meet with the principal.

formation: する ￫ なさる料理（りょうり）する ￫ 料理（りょうり）なさるお + Verb［stem］+ なさるConjugationsVerb［る］ ￫ なさるVerb［ない］ ￫ なさらないVerb［た］ ￫ なさったVerb［なかった］ ￫ なさらなかった
casual_structure: する ￫ なさる料理（りょうり）する ￫ 料理（りょうり）なさるお + Verb［stem］+ なさるConjugationsVerb［る］ ￫ なさるVerb［ない］ ￫ なさらないVerb［た］ ￫ なさったVerb［なかった］ ￫ なさらなかった
polite_structure: する ￫ なさいます料理（りょうり）する ￫ 料理（りょうり）なさいますお + Verb［stem］+ なさいますConjugationsVerb［る］ ￫ なさいますVerb［ない］ ￫ なさいませんVerb［た］ ￫ なさいましたVerb［なかった］ ￫ なさいませんでしたThere are multiple levels of politeness for the て-form of なさる:なさっています ￫ なさってらっしゃいます ￫ なさっていらっしゃいます and なさっておられます
explanation: A polite, somewhat old expression, that states the actions of others respectfully.

example_sentences.japanese: お飲み物はどうなさいますか。
example_sentences.english: What will you have to drink?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は計画を変えることはなさいませんでした。
example_sentences.english: He did not do anything to change the plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末もお仕事をなさるのですか。
example_sentences.english: Are you going to work over the weekend also?

example_sentences.japanese: 勘違いなさらないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't take this the wrong way.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は先週どちらでゴルフをなさったのですか。
example_sentences.english: Boss, where did you go to play golf last week?

example_sentences.japanese: 納得なさらないなら私に言ってください。
example_sentences.english: If you are not with me on this, please let me know.

example_sentences.japanese: お飲み物はどうなさいますか？
example_sentences.english: What would you like to drink?

example_sentences.japanese: 忘れ物はなさいませんか。
example_sentences.english: Did you forget anything?

example_sentences.japanese: お客様、どうなさいましたか。
example_sentences.english: Valued guest, what seems to be the issue?

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝、彼は家を留守になさいました。
example_sentences.english: He was away from home this morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころスポーツをなさっていたんですね。
example_sentences.english: I hear that you played sports when you were younger.

example_sentences.japanese: 今何を勉強なさっていますか。
example_sentences.english: What are you studying now?

example_sentences.japanese: 何をなさろうとするのですか。
example_sentences.english: What will you attempt to do?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人を信用なさっていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you trust that person?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日何時まで仕事をなさったのですか。
example_sentences.english: Until what time did you work yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: 私はそんなに上手じゃないので、期待なさらないでください。
example_sentences.english: I am not that good, so please do not expect much.

example_sentences.japanese: お申し込みなさるのでしたら、このペンでお書きください。
example_sentences.english: If (you will do) an application, please use this pen to write with.

example_sentences.japanese: 平野さんは明日の飲み会に出席なさいますか。
example_sentences.english: Will Hirano-san attend the drinking party tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: 私はコーヒーにします。山田さんは何になさいますか。
example_sentences.english: I will have a coffee. What will you have (do) Yamada-san?

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚記念日にどうなさるつもりですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日より、今日にしたらいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: If/when you do it today instead of tomorrow, I think that would be good. (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行くつもりだったら、パスポートを忘れないで。
example_sentences.english: When you intend to go abroad, don't forget your passport. (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強したら、もっと上手に話せますよ。
example_sentences.english: When you study you are able to speak more skillfully. (from when...)

example_sentences.japanese: 暇だったら、一緒に映画を見に行きませんか。
example_sentences.english: When you are free, won't you go see a movie together (with me)? (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームをしたかったら、友達の家に行ってください。
example_sentences.english: When you want to play videogames, please go to your friend's house. (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の掃除がまだだったら、まずそれをしなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: If you have not cleaned your room yet, first you have to do that. (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: これをしてみたら、きっと楽しいと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: When/if you try this, I think that it will surely be fun. (from when・just when)

example_sentences.japanese: 来週だったら、いけるよ。
example_sentences.english: If it is next week, I can go. (Highlighting a future event)

example_sentences.japanese: 先週だったら行けたのに。
example_sentences.english: If it was last week, I could have gone. (Highlighting a past event)

example_sentences.japanese: 買い物に行ったら、クッキーを買ってきて。
example_sentences.english: When/if you go shopping, please get me some cookies.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたがその本を読まないなら、私が読みます。
example_sentences.english: If you are not going to read that book, I will read it.

general_translation: Other, Another, Any other, Anything else, As well as, Besides, In addition
formation: 他（ほか） + の + Noun（その(1)） + 他（ほか） + にも(2)Noun + の + 他（ほか） + にも(2)Verb + 他（ほか） + にも(2)（その(1)） +  他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］Noun  + の + 他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］Verb  + 他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］(1) この(2) に、も、は、には(3) に、は
casual_structure: 他（ほか） + の + Noun（その(1)） + 他（ほか） + にも(2)Noun + の + 他（ほか） + にも(2)Verb + 他（ほか） + にも(2)（その(1)） +  他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］Noun  + の + 他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］Verb  + 他（ほか） + には(3) + Phrase［ない］(1) この(2) に、も、は、には(3) に、は
explanation: A structure which may either indicate or negate the presence of something other than (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ほかは？
example_sentences.english: Anything else?

example_sentences.japanese: ほかに、欲しいものはある？
example_sentences.english: Is there anything else you want?

example_sentences.japanese: 動物園のほかにもどこかへ行きますか。
example_sentences.english: Is there anywhere else you want to go, other than the zoo?

example_sentences.japanese: ほかにはない物が食べたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat something that isn't anywhere else. (Something unique to this place)

example_sentences.japanese: この電子レンジは壊れているのでほかの電子レンジをお使いになってください。
example_sentences.english: This microwave is broken so please use a different one.

example_sentences.japanese: お金のほかには何が欲しいですか。
example_sentences.english: Other than money, what do you want?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のほかにはフランス語を話せる人はいません。
example_sentences.english: Other than him, there isn't anyone else that can speak French.

example_sentences.japanese: いいえ、ほかはいりません。
example_sentences.english: No, I don't need anything else.

example_sentences.japanese: ほかの国に行ったことがありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever been to any other countries?

example_sentences.japanese: ほかの方法がないかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if there is no other way. (another)

example_sentences.japanese: この箸のほかには使えないんだ。
example_sentences.english: I can't use anything but these chopsticks. (other than)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はスーパーに行くほかは予定がない。
example_sentences.english: Today, I don't have any plans other than going to the store.

example_sentences.japanese: この機械が壊れたので、ほかのを使ってください。
example_sentences.english: This machine is broken, so please use another one.

example_sentences.japanese: 今サッカーをしているけど、ほかのスポーツは出来る？
example_sentences.english: You are playing soccer now, but can you do any other sports?

example_sentences.japanese: この本だけですか。(この/この本の）ほかにもほしいものはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Only this book? Is there anything else (besides this one/this book) you want?

example_sentences.japanese: ほかに、行きたいところはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Are there any other places (in addition to that) you would like to go to?

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあまりジュースを飲まないから、ほかの飲み物がほしいです。
example_sentences.english: Since I do not really drink juice, I want another beverage.

example_sentences.japanese: この大学に田中先生のほかにも日本語の先生がいらっしゃいますか。
example_sentences.english: Are there any other Japanese teachers besides Tanaka-sensei at this college?

example_sentences.japanese: 欲しいものは、その他にもない。
example_sentences.english: There is also nothing else besides what I want. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: その他にも何か質問がありませんか？
example_sentences.english: Besides that, are there no other questions? (Natural Japanese)

formation: Noun + が + 必要（ひつよう） + だVerb + こと + が + 必要（ひつよう） + だ
casual_structure: Noun + が + 必要（ひつよう） + だVerb + こと + が + 必要（ひつよう） + だ
polite_structure: Noun + が + 必要（ひつよう） + ですVerb + こと + が + 必要（ひつよう） + です
explanation: A grammar point that indicates nouns or noun-like phrases as being necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: テストをする時はえんぴつがひつようです。
example_sentences.english: A pencil is necessary when you take a test.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎に住むには車がひつよう。
example_sentences.english: To live in the countryside, a car is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: プールで泳ぐときは水着がひつようだ。
example_sentences.english: When swimming in a pool, a swimsuit is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: バスを運転するには特別な免許がひつようだ。
example_sentences.english: You need a special license to drive a bus.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は車を持っていないから迎えに行くことがひつようだ。
example_sentences.english: Because he doesn't have a car, it is necessary to go pick him up.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは泥棒が多いから出かける前に鍵をかけることがひつようだ。
example_sentences.english: Because there are a lot of burglars here, it is necessary to lock your door before you go out.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は運転するときは眼鏡がひつよう。
example_sentences.english: I need glasses when I drive.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキを作るなら、砂糖がひつようです。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to make a cake, sugar is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎に住んだら、車がひつようです。
example_sentences.english: If you live in the countryside, a car is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: スノーボードに行くなら、手袋がひつようです。
example_sentences.english: If you are going snowboarding, you need gloves.

example_sentences.japanese: 何がひつようかな〜。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what I need...

example_sentences.japanese: 後で部屋を綺麗にしてもらう。ほうきがひつようだと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Later, I will have you clean up your room. I think that you will need a broom.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝はコーヒーがひつようです。なかったら、私は仕事が出来ません。
example_sentences.english: Coffee is necessary in the morning. If I do not have any, I cannot work.

example_sentences.japanese: この話は分かりにくいので、話が終わるまで集中力がひつようです。
example_sentences.english: This story is difficult to understand, so until it is over I need to concentrate.

example_sentences.japanese: 行ったことがない国に行くなら、プランニングがひつようです。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to go to a country you have never been before, planning is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ親の愛がひつようだった。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, the love of my parents was necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生だから、消しゴムがひつようだろう。どうして持って来てないの？
example_sentences.english: Since you are a student, you need an eraser, right? Why haven't you brought one?

example_sentences.japanese: 砂が暑いので、ビーチに行くならサンダルがひつようです。
example_sentences.english: The sand is hot, so if you go to the beach you need (to bring) sandals.

formation: そんなに + Verbそんなに + ［い］Adjectiveそんなに + ［な］Adjective
casual_structure: そんなに + Verbそんなに + ［い］Adjectiveそんなに + ［な］Adjective
explanation: A word that is used to show the surprising extent of something. To that extent.

example_sentences.japanese: このケーキはそんなに甘いんですか。
example_sentences.english: Is this cake really that sweet?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに食べたらお腹を壊 すよ。
example_sentences.english: If you eat that much, you are going to break your stomach. (Natural Japanese for 'stomach ache')

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに暑いと思うならエアコンをつければいい。
example_sentences.english: If you think it's that hot, you should turn on the air conditioner.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに嫌いなら、無理して食べなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: If you dislike it that much, you don't have to force yourself to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなにもらってもいいんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is it okay to receive this much? (Are you really giving me all of this?)

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに食べたのにまだお腹が空いているの？
example_sentences.english: You are still hungry, even after eating that much?

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに頑張っても、私は先輩みたいにはなれないと思う。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard I try, I don't think that I can become like my senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに痛いなら、病院に行ったほうがいいんじゃないですか。
example_sentences.english: If it hurts that much, shouldn't you go to the hospital?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに頑張っても、彼みたいに出来ない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I tried that hard, I couldn't do it like he can. (that much)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに日本に行きたいなら、行って来たら？
example_sentences.english: If you want to go to Japan that much, why don't you?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに水泳が嫌いなら、泳がなくていいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: If you hate swimming so much, why don't you just not swim? (that much)

example_sentences.japanese: もうお金がそんなにないから、買うのをやめましょう。
example_sentences.english: Because I don't have that much money, I won't buy it. (I will stop myself from buying it)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに宿題が多かったら、今すぐ始めた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: If you have that much homework, it would be better to start now.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに頭が痛いなら、お医者さんに見てもらってください。
example_sentences.english: If your head hurts that much, please go to a doctor. (Please get an examination by a doctor)

example_sentences.japanese: 君がこの写真そんなに好きだったら、あげる。
example_sentences.english: If you like this picture that much, I will give it to you.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに迷惑をかけたと思っていなかったです。すみませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't think that I was causing that much trouble. I'm sorry (for what I did).

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにアイスクリームが好きなら、後で買ってあげる。
example_sentences.english: If you like ice cream that much, I will buy you some later.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに妻と喧嘩するならカウンセリングに行ってみ。
example_sentences.english: If you fight that much with your wife, try going to counseling.

formation: Verb + 必要（ひつよう） + が + ある
casual_structure: Verb + 必要（ひつよう） + が + ある
polite_structure: Verb + 必要（ひつよう） + が + あります
explanation: A phrase that highlights a specific action as being required.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べるひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to eat breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はテストがあるから、勉強をするひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: Because I have a test tomorrow, it is necessary to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はまだ小さいので、いつも一緒にいるひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: Since my son is still little, it is necessary for me to be with him at all times.

example_sentences.japanese: カイルは日本語が分かるので、書類を英語に訳すひつようがない。
example_sentences.english: Since Kyle understands Japanese, there is no need to translate the documents into English.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は元気になったので、病院に行くひつようがありません。
example_sentences.english: Since my daughter got well, there is no need to go to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: それを明日までに終えるひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to finish that by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: この板が厚すぎて、切るひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: This board is too thick, so it is necessary that it is cut.

example_sentences.japanese: 痩せたいなら、運動するひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: If you want to lose weight, then it is necessary to exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルに泊まるならカミソリを持って行くひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to stay at a hotel, it is necessary to bring a razor.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳があまりないからスーパーに行くひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: There isn't much milk left, so it is necessary to go to the store.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一回説明してもらうひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to have it explained once more.

example_sentences.japanese: また寝坊したの？早く寝るひつようがあると思う。
example_sentences.english: You slept in again? I think that it is necessary to sleep early.

example_sentences.japanese: 変な匂いがするね。スプレーするひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: It smells weird, doesn't it. It is necessary to spray air freshener.

example_sentences.japanese: テストに合格したかったら、先生の話を聞くひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: If you want to pass the test, it is necessary to listen to the teacher's instruction.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんがもう来ているから、早めに店を開くひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: There are already customers, so it is necessary to open the store early.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外旅行に行きたいなら、パスポートを持っていくひつようがある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to take a passport with you if you want to go overseas.

formation: たとえば + Phrase
casual_structure: たとえば + Phrase
explanation: A hypothetical phrase which presents the example of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、「英語が好きですか。」と聞いてみたら？
example_sentences.english: For example, why don't you ask 'Do you like English?'

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、ドイツとかは？
example_sentences.english: For example, how about Germany, or something?

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、冷たい物を食べたときに歯が痛いです。
example_sentences.english: For example, my teeth hurt when I eat cold things.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、翻訳者になったら日本に住むことが出来る。
example_sentences.english: For example, if you become a translator, you will be able to live in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を覚えるサイトがたくさんあります。たとえば、ワニカニだ。
example_sentences.english: There are a number of sites you can use to learn kanji. For example, Wanikani.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば毎日日本語を話すなら、日本語のレベルが上がる。
example_sentences.english: For example, if you speak Japanese every day, your Japanese level will rise.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、たとえばあそこにあるイタリアンレストランのような店を作りたい。
example_sentences.english: For example, I want to make a restaurant like that Italian restaurant over there.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々な国に行って見たい。たとえば、ベトナム。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to a variety of countries. Vietnam for example.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ何でも食べることが出来た。たとえば、納豆が好きだった。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, I could eat anything. I liked natto for example.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、毎日日本語を話したら、だんだん上手になってくるよ。
example_sentences.english: For example, if you speak Japanese every day, you will gradually get better.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、違う国の歴史を勉強したら文化の違いが分かってくる。
example_sentences.english: For example, if you study the history of other countries, you will come to realize differences in culture.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも丁寧に話す方がいいよ。たとえば、「ありがとう」と「すみません」は必要な言葉。
example_sentences.english: It is better to always speak politely. For example, 'thank you' and 'excuse me' are necessary phrases.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえば、「私はお金持ち」って子供に言ったら、子供たちが色々なものを買ってもらいたくなるだろう。
example_sentences.english: For example, if you say that you are rich, your children will want to have you buy them various things.

example_sentences.japanese: この授業は本当に大変だ。たとえば、明日までにこの文章を書き終わらなかったら、点数がゼロになる。
example_sentences.english: This class is really giving me trouble. For example, if I don't finish writing this essay by tomorrow, I'll get zero points.

example_sentences.japanese: 詳しく言うと、トマトのように種がいっぱいある食べ物が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: More specifically, I don't like foods that have a lot of seeds, like tomatoes.
