explanation: A construction that expresses the ability to do (A), but is also often shortened in modern Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: あの山がみられますか。
example_sentences.english: Can you see that mountain over there?

example_sentences.japanese: サリーはほとんどの漢字を書くことができる。
example_sentences.english: Sally is able to write most kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: この歌は弾けますか？
example_sentences.english: Are you able to play this song?

example_sentences.japanese: この池では色々な魚が釣れます。
example_sentences.english: You can catch many kinds of fish in this lake.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに届けられる？
example_sentences.english: Can you deliver it by tomorrow? (Natural Japanese, and may express 'potential', 'passivity', 'respect', or 'spontaneous occurrence')

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で全部食べられる？
example_sentences.english: Can you eat all of this on your own? (Natural Japanese, and may express 'potential', 'passivity', 'respect', or 'spontaneous occurrence')

example_sentences.japanese: トムはすぐに新しい文法を覚えれる。
example_sentences.english: Tom is able to remember new grammar immediately. (Natural Japanese only when expressing 'potential', not 'passivity', 'respect', or 'spontaneous occurrence')

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなんでも食べれる。
example_sentences.english: He can eat anything. (Natural Japanese only when expressing 'potential', not 'passivity', 'respect', or 'spontaneous occurrence')

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の話はしんじられない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot believe her story.

example_sentences.japanese: 十分まてますか。
example_sentences.english: Can you wait 10 minutes?

example_sentences.japanese: 私の好きな映画がみられたらいいね。
example_sentences.english: I hope that you can see the movie I like.

example_sentences.japanese: みつけられなくてすみませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I was unable to find it.

example_sentences.japanese: ほしいけど、お金がないからかえないですよ。
example_sentences.english: I want it, but I don't have any money so I am unable to buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: ＣＤを持ってくるのを忘れたから、車で音楽がきけません。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to bring my CDs, so I cannot listen to music in the car.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は力が強いからあの重いテレビ台を一人でもてます。
example_sentences.english: He is strong, so he can pick up that heavy TV stand by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹は１００字の漢字がかける。
example_sentences.english: My little sister is able to write 100 kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: この服がきつすぎるから、きられないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: These clothes are so tight that I may be unable to wear them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は夏休みごろ、旅行にいける。
example_sentences.english: I can take a trip around summer vacation.

example_sentences.japanese: この公園ではあそべるけど、あそこの公園では遊べないよ。
example_sentences.english: You can play in this park, but you cannot play in that one.

example_sentences.japanese: やっとシャワーを浴びられる！
example_sentences.english: I can finally take a shower!

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは何が食べられるの？
example_sentences.english: What can you eat?

example_sentences.japanese: トムは日本語とフランス語と英語を話すことができる。
example_sentences.english: Tom is able to speak Japanese, French, and English.

formation: Phrase (A) + のだ(1) + が(2) + Phrase (B)  (1) んだ  (2) けれども、けれど、けども、けど
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + のだ(1) + が(2) + Phrase (B)  (1) んだ  (2) けれども、けれど、けども、けど
polite_structure: Phrase (A) + のです(1) + が(2) + Phrase (B)  (1) んです  (2) けれども、けれど、けども、けど
explanation: A casual way of expressing but, with the focus on giving reasons, elongating a pause, or leaving something unsaid due to awkwardness.

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨日の告白はどうなったの？」「こくはくしたんだけど 。」
example_sentences.english: 'How did yesterday's confession go?''I confessed but… (I was rejected).'

example_sentences.japanese: 助かるんだけど一人でできるから帰ってもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: I feel like you are being helpful, but I can handle it by myself, so you can go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は明日釣りに行くのですが先輩も行きませんか？
example_sentences.english: I am going to go fishing tomorrow, but senpai, do you also want to go?

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいパソコンを買いたいのだけど...どれを買えばいいか分からない。
example_sentences.english: I want to buy a new computer, but… I don't know which one to buy.

example_sentences.japanese: これほしいんだけど 。
example_sentences.english: I want this, but… (it is expensive).

example_sentences.japanese: やせられたらいいんだけど (難しいね)。
example_sentences.english: It would be great if I could lose some weight, but… (it is hard).

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい時計を買いたいのですが 。
example_sentences.english: I would like to buy a new watch (and…) (which one would be good?)

example_sentences.japanese: 窓が開いているからちょっと寒いんですが (どうか窓を閉めていただけませんか？)。
example_sentences.english: Since the window is open, it is a bit cold (and…) (I wonder if you wouldn't mind closing it?).

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの男、顔がいいね。」「顔はいいんだけど (なんか性格がわるそう)。」
example_sentences.english: 'That guy, he has nice features, don't you think?''He has nice features, but… (It seems that he has a bad personality).'

example_sentences.japanese: 「はるこさんはこれを食べたことがありますか？」「たべてみたことがあるのですが 。」
example_sentences.english: 'Haruko-san, have you tried this before?''I tried it, but… (it was not very tasty).'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あしたカフェに行くんだけど (一緒に行かない？)」「行きたいんだけど (仕事がある）ごめん。」
example_sentences.english: 'I am going to a cafe tomorrow, (won't you go with me?)''I want to go, but… (I have work) Sorry. '

example_sentences.japanese: 「明日映画館に行かない？」「行きたいんだけど (明日試験があるから、行けない)。」
example_sentences.english: 'Won't you go to the cinema tomorrow?''I'd like to go, but… (I have an exam tomorrow, so I can't).'

example_sentences.japanese: この自転車のモデルを買おうと思っているのですが (どう思いますか？)。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking about buying this bicycle model, but… (what do you think?).

example_sentences.japanese: オニズカ先生、質問があるのですが (聞いてもよろしいのでしょうか)。
example_sentences.english: Onizuka-sensei, I have a question and… (may I ask it?).

example_sentences.japanese: 誕生日パーティーをやるんだけど、(来ないの？)
example_sentences.english: I am having a birthday party and… (won't you come?)

example_sentences.japanese: 顔はいいのだけど...性格は悪い。
example_sentences.english: He has a good looking face, but… his personality is bad.

general_translation: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)
formation: Verb + はず + だ［い］Adjective + はず + だ［な］Adjective + な + はず + だNoun + の + はず + だ
casual_structure: Verb + はず + だ［い］Adjective + はず + だ［な］Adjective + な + はず + だNoun + の + はず + だ
polite_structure: Verb + はず + です［い］Adjective + はず + です［な］Adjective + な + はず + ですNoun + の + はず + です
explanation: A phrase that expresses when the speaker thinks that (A) is bound to be true.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は借りたペンを返すはずだ。
example_sentences.english: He is bound to return the pen he borrowed. (expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降るはずだ。
example_sentences.english: It is supposed to rain today. (But I am not 100% sure if it will)

example_sentences.japanese: 新幹線で行った方が速いはずだ。
example_sentences.english: It is bound to be faster if we go by shinkansen. (But I am not 100% sure if it will)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は魚が嫌いだから寿司は嫌いなはずだ。
example_sentences.english: He does not like fish, so he is sure to dislike sushi. (But I am not 100% sure if he will)

example_sentences.japanese: 頼んだのはコーヒーのはずだったけどお茶が来た。
example_sentences.english: I was sure that I ordered coffee, but tea came. (But I am not 100% sure if I did)

example_sentences.japanese: 夏だから、暑いはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Because it is summer, it is expected to be hot. (bound to be)

example_sentences.japanese: ここから富士山が見えるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: One should be able to see Mt. Fuji from here. (bound to)

example_sentences.japanese: この港には船があるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: There are bound to be boats in this harbor. (expected to be)

example_sentences.japanese: 脱出した犯人が見つかるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: The escaped convict is bound to be found. (expected to be)

example_sentences.japanese: 降りるのは次の駅のはずです。
example_sentences.english: The next station is bound to be the one we get off at. (expected to be)

example_sentences.japanese: お兄ちゃんはこのプレゼントが好きなはずだ。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is bound to like this present. (expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: 約束のはずだったのに、破ったの？
example_sentences.english: It was supposed to be a promise, but you broke it? (expected to be)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな薄い氷の上では歩けないはずだ。
example_sentences.english: You should not be able to walk on this thin ice. (bound to・expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は夜七時までに、帰ってくるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: My wife is expected to return home by seven o'clock. (bound to)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日お母さんが家に居るから、迎えに来てくれるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: My mom is home today, so she should be able to come pick us up. (bound to・expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと用意したはずだったのに、歯ブラシ持って来るのを忘れた。
example_sentences.english: I should have been fully prepared, but I forgot to bring a toothbrush. (expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: ハリーも今日のパーティーに行く…はず。
example_sentences.english: Harry will go to the party today… Probably.

example_sentences.japanese: 出かける前に家の中の電気は全部消した… はず。
example_sentences.english: I turned off all the lights in my house before I left… I'm pretty sure.

formation: Verb + か + どう + か + Phrase［い］Adjective + か + どう + か + Phrase［な］Adjective + か + どう + か + PhraseNoun + か + どう + か + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + か + どう + か + Phrase［い］Adjective + か + どう + か + Phrase［な］Adjective + か + どう + か + PhraseNoun + か + どう + か + Phrase
explanation: A phrase that expresses the speaker's uncertainty about whether (A) is true, or something else is.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行けるかどうかわからない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether or not I can go on a trip.

example_sentences.japanese: サチコと付き合うかどうか分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether or not I will go out with Sachiko.

example_sentences.japanese: 水が汚いからこの川が深いかどうか分からない。
example_sentences.english: Since the water is dirty, I don't know whether or not this river is deep.

example_sentences.japanese: この携帯が便利かどうか分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether or not this cell phone is useful.

example_sentences.japanese: 目が悪いからあそこにいるのが父親かどうかわからない。
example_sentences.english: Because I have bad eyes, I don't know whether or not the person over there is my father.

example_sentences.japanese: サンタさんがいるかどうか探しています。
example_sentences.english: We're searching for clues as to whether or not Santa's here.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ日本に行けるかどうか、分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether or not I still can go to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチがうまくできるかどうか心配している。
example_sentences.english: I am worried whether or not my speech will go well.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の動物は犬かどうか分からないけど、怖かった。
example_sentences.english: I don't know whether or not the animal I just saw was a dog, but it was frightening.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに宿題が出来るかどうかあまり自信がないですね。
example_sentences.english: I am unsure if I can get my homework done by tomorrow or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の姿がトムかどうか分からないけど、多分トムだったと思う。
example_sentences.english: I am not sure whether that (figure) was Tom or not, but it was probably Tom.

example_sentences.japanese: この食べ物は美味しいかどうかわからないので、食べてみたい。
example_sentences.english: Because I don't know whether or not it is delicious, I want to try eating this food.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが必要だが、買えるかどうかはお金の問題だ。
example_sentences.english: I need a computer, but the problem is whether or not I will be able to buy it. (It's a money issue)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかどうか分からないから、傘を持って行った方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: I am not sure whether or not it will rain today, so you had better bring an umbrella.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の月食が僕が死ぬ前にあるかどうか知りたいんだ。
example_sentences.english: I want to know whether or not the next lunar eclipse will happen before I die.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランの料理が美味しくなるかどうか分からないけど、もう二度と行かない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know if this restaurant will get better or not, but I will never go there again.

formation: Verb + と［い］Adjective + と［な］Adjective + だ  +  とNoun + だ + と
casual_structure: Verb + と［い］Adjective + と［な］Adjective + だ  +  とNoun + だ + と
explanation: A conditional that expresses known or certain outcomes.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をすると、テストは簡単になる。
example_sentences.english: If you study, tests become easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 甘いものをいっぱい食べると、太る。
example_sentences.english: If you eat a lot of sweet things, you will gain weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が汚いと、お母さんに怒られる。
example_sentences.english: If my room is messy, my mother will yell at me.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が静かだと、眠れない。
example_sentences.english: If my room is quiet, I can't sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 地下鉄だと、五分早く着く。
example_sentences.english: If it's the subway, you will arrive 5 minutes faster.

example_sentences.japanese: 走るとけがをする。
example_sentences.english: If I run, I will injure myself. (Unnatural Japanese, unless this person always injures themselves while running for some reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 目を閉じると、何も見えない。
example_sentences.english: I close my eyes, and I can't see.

example_sentences.japanese: この石を磨くと、綺麗になる。
example_sentences.english: If you polish this rock, it will become beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: そうすると絶対に失敗するよ。
example_sentences.english: If you do it that way, you will definitely make a mistake.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから見ると、富士山が全然見えない。
example_sentences.english: If you look from here, you can't see Mt. Fuji at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 週に３回トレーニングをするとだんだん強くなる。
example_sentences.english: Whenever you workout three times a week, you gradually get stronger. (if...)

example_sentences.japanese: この辺でスピードを出し過ぎるとスピード違反になるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you speed in this area, you will get a speeding violation.

example_sentences.japanese: ガスの匂いがしているときに火を点けると、危ないです。
example_sentences.english: It is dangerous to light a fire, if you smell gas. (whenever...)

example_sentences.japanese: 今行くと危険なので、行かない方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: If you go now it is dangerous, so I think that it is better not to go.

example_sentences.japanese: 水着を持って来るのを忘れると海に入れないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you forget to bring your swimsuit, you won't be able to swim in the ocean.

example_sentences.japanese: ロッククライミングをすると使ったことのない筋肉を使う。
example_sentences.english: If you go rock-climbing you use muscles that you have never used before.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の人口が減ると大変になる。
example_sentences.english: If the Japanese population diminishes then it will become a serious situation.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語で喋ってみると日本人が喜ぶよ。
example_sentences.english: If you speak Japanese, Japanese people will be happy.

formation: Verb［ない］+ と + （いけない(1)）(1) だめ
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ と + （いけない(1)）(1) だめ
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ と + （いけません(1)）(1) だめです
explanation: A casual, hypothetical structure showing that one must do (A). Often with the nuance of if (A) is not done, something bad may happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 「約束をまもらないといけません！」
example_sentences.english: 'You have to keep your promise!' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: ライト君が悪いんだから、リュウ君に謝らないといけないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Raito-kun, you are in the wrong, so you have to apologize to Ryu-kun, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は勉強しないとだめだから、明日は？
example_sentences.english: I have to study today, so how about tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はテストがあるの？！勉強しないと。
example_sentences.english: There is a test tomorrow!? I have to study.

example_sentences.japanese: もう７時じゃん？準備しないと。
example_sentences.english: Oh, it's already 7? I need to get ready.

example_sentences.japanese: 「なぜ、税金をはらわないといけないのですか？」
example_sentences.english: 'Why do I have to pay taxes?' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「子沢山だから、一週間に三十回は洗濯しないとだめ。」
example_sentences.english: 'There are lots of children, so I have to do laundry thirty times a week.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「合格したらまず両親や先生につたえないと。」
example_sentences.english: 'If I pass, I have to tell my parents and teacher first!' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ピーナッツにアレルギーがあるといっておかないといけないんだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I have to tell (you) in advance that I am allergic to peanuts.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 母親：「どうしたの？」息子：「また床にカップを落としちゃったんだ。かたづけないと…」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'What happened?'Son: 'I dropped a cup on the floor again! I have to clean it up...' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「日本では家へ上がるとき、靴をぬがないといけません。」
example_sentences.english: 'When you enter a home in Japan, you have to take off your shoes.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 配偶者：「疲れてるみたいね。何かたべないといけないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Spouse: 'You look tired. You have to eat something!' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「明日、目覚めたらまず病院に電話しないといけないよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Tomorrow, the first thing you must do after you wake up is call the hospital.' (have to)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ほたるちゃん、うちに遊びにきてくれるの？」「すみません。明日までに宿題をすませないといけないのです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Hotaru, will you come and hang out at my house?''I am sorry. I have to finish doing my homework by tomorrow.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「君はまだ小さい子供だから大人と一緒にこないといけません。」
example_sentences.english: 'You are still a small child, so you have to come with an adult.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 「すみません、どこに署名しないといけませんか？」「ここに名前を書いてください。」
example_sentences.english: 'Excuse me, where do I have to sign?''Write down your name here, please.' (must)

example_sentences.japanese: 歩行者も信号機を守らないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Even pedestrians have to obey traffic lights.

general_translation: Hardly possible, Cannot be, Highly unlikely, Improbable
formation: Verb + はず + が + ない［い］Adjective + はず + が + ない［な］Adjective + な + はず + が + ないNoun + の + はず + が + ない
casual_structure: Verb + はず + が + ない［い］Adjective + はず + が + ない［な］Adjective + な + はず + が + ないNoun + の + はず + が + ない
polite_structure: Verb + はず + が + ありません［い］Adjective + はず + が + ありません［な］Adjective + な + はず + が + ありませんNoun + の + はず + が + ありません
explanation: An expression that shows that (A) is not bound to be the case, or is unlikely.

example_sentences.japanese: これだけのはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is highly unlikely that it is just this.

example_sentences.japanese: 一時間も早く家を出たから遅れるはずがない。
example_sentences.english: Because I left the house an hour early, it is improbable that I will be late. (That I am bound to be late is not true)

example_sentences.japanese: この箱は重いはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is hardly possible that this box is heavy. (It is not the case that this box is bound to be heavy)

example_sentences.japanese: サリーの家は立派なはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is highly unlikely that Sally's house is splendid. (That Sally's house is sure to be splendid is not the case)

example_sentences.japanese: あそこにいる人はトムのはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is highly unlikely that the person over there is Tom.

example_sentences.japanese: それはあなたのカバンのはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is highly unlikely that that is your bag.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏に雪が降るはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is hardly possible for it to snow in the summer.

example_sentences.japanese: あのビルは古すぎなので、病院のはずがない。
example_sentences.english: Because that building is so old, it is hardly possible that it is a hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな量を一気に食べられるはずがないよ。
example_sentences.english: It is hardly possible to eat this amount of food at once.

example_sentences.japanese: この安い給料の仕事で、家を建てられるはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is improbable to think that one could build a house on such a low salary.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名人は人気だから、寂しいはずがない。
example_sentences.english: Famous people are popular so it seems hardly possible for them to be lonely.

example_sentences.japanese: 少年の部屋だから、綺麗なはずがない。
example_sentences.english: Since it's a boy's room, it is highly unlikely that it is clean.

example_sentences.japanese: ＮＨＫを見るだけで日本語が上手になるはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is hardly possible to get proficient at Japanese just by watching NHK.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は強いけど、車を持ち上げられるはずがない。
example_sentences.english: He is strong, but it is improbable that he could lift a car.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビを見ながら、ちゃんと勉強出来るはずがない。
example_sentences.english: One cannot study properly while watching TV. (Hardly possible)

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が綺麗じゃなかったので、彼女も綺麗なはずがなかった。
example_sentences.english: Her mother was not pretty, so it was highly unlikely that she was pretty.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は毎日４時間以上勉強したから、テストが不合格のはずがない。
example_sentences.english: I studied over 4 hours a day, so it is highly unlikely that I will fail the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の車は高くないはずだ。
example_sentences.english: His car would not be expensive. (His car is bound to not be that expensive)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の車は高いはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It is hardly possible that his car is expensive. (That his car is bound to be expensive is not true)

formation: Noun + しか + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Noun + しか + Verb［ない］
explanation: A phrase that highlights that one specific thing is all that exists.

example_sentences.japanese: 座るところがここしかありません。
example_sentences.english: There is nowhere else to sit but here.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人はまだ３人しか捕まっていない。
example_sentences.english: Only 3 of the criminals have been caught so far.

example_sentences.japanese: この店は牛丼しか置いていない。
example_sentences.english: This store only has gyudon.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣りに行って、一匹しか釣れないと悲しくなる。
example_sentences.english: I get sad when I go fishing and only catch one fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠いので、車で行くことしかできない。
example_sentences.english: Because it is far away, you can only go by car.

example_sentences.japanese: 「はい」と「いいえ」しかいわない人とは話しにくい。
example_sentences.english: It is difficult to talk to people who only respond with 'yes' and 'no'.

example_sentences.japanese: すみませんが、午後しかあいていないみたいです。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry, but it looks like only the afternoon is open.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫に牛乳しか残っていない。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing but milk in the fridge.

example_sentences.japanese: 手袋を一枚しか見つけられない。
example_sentences.english: I can only find one glove.

example_sentences.japanese: 多く見えるけど、ちょっとしかない。
example_sentences.english: It looks like there is a lot, but there's only a few. (nothing but)

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をするなら、今しかできない！
example_sentences.english: If you are going to study, it is now or never! (nothing but)

example_sentences.japanese: お茶しかないけど、よかったらどうぞ。
example_sentences.english: We have nothing but tea, but, if you like, please help yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: 空気が綺麗だし、皆が優しいから、ここにしかすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Not only is the air clear, everyone is so nice. There is no other place to live but here.

example_sentences.japanese: 泥棒がロウソクしかとらなかったので、警察に電話していない。
example_sentences.english: The thief took nothing but the candles, so I didn't call the police.

example_sentences.japanese: このテレビはチャネルが二つしかないけど、テレビをあまり見ないからいい。
example_sentences.english: This TV only has two channels, but I don't really watch TV so it's okay.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から雨が降るから、今日行くしかない。
example_sentences.english: Since it will start raining tomorrow, we have no choice but to go today.

formation: Verb + だけ + でなく(1)［い］Adjective + だけ + でなく(1)［な］Adjective + な + だけ + でなく(1)Noun + だけ + でなく(1)(1) ではなく（て）、じゃなく（て）
casual_structure: Verb + だけ + でなく(1)［い］Adjective + だけ + でなく(1)［な］Adjective + な + だけ + でなく(1)Noun + だけ + でなく(1)(1) ではなく（て）、じゃなく（て）
explanation: A somewhat casual expression used to show that something is not just (A), but also (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ぶどうは甘いだけでなく、みずみずしい。
example_sentences.english: Grapes are not only sweet, but also juicy.

example_sentences.japanese: 痩せるためには運動をするだけでなく、食べるものにも気を付けなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: To lose weight, not only should you exercise, but you must also be careful of what you eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 名古屋の夏は暑いだけでなく、湿気もひどい。
example_sentences.english: Summer in Nagoya is not only hot, but the humidity is terrible too.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎は静かなだけでなく、空気もきれいだ。
example_sentences.english: The countryside is not only quiet, but the air is also clean.

example_sentences.japanese: トーマスは車だけでなく、バイクとボートも持っている。
example_sentences.english: Not only does Thomas own a car, but he also has a bike, and a boat.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは日本語だけでなくて、中国語も話せる。
example_sentences.english: Not only can Tom speak Japanese, but also Chinese.

example_sentences.japanese: 私だけでなく、私の友達も日本語が喋れる。
example_sentences.english: Not only me, but also my friends can speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は日本語だけでなく、韓国語、中国語とタイ語も話せる。
example_sentences.english: That person can speak not only Japanese, but also Korean, Chinese, and Thai.

example_sentences.japanese: ジョニー・デップはカナダだけでなく、日本も訪れたことがある。
example_sentences.english: Johnny Depp has not only visited Canada, but has visited Japan as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女だけでなく、私もこの映画が好きだよ。
example_sentences.english: Not only does she like this movie but I do too.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏が料理だけでなく、家事も出来るから、凄い助かる。
example_sentences.english: Not only can my boyfriend cook, but he can also do housework, so it is really helpful.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は約束を破るだけでなく、嘘もつく。
example_sentences.english: Not only does that person break promises but they also tell lies.

example_sentences.japanese: 海は綺麗なだけでなく、温かい。
example_sentences.english: The ocean is not only beautiful, but also warm.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手は怪我しただけでなく、次の試合に出られない。
example_sentences.english: That athlete not only got hurt, but also can't play in the next game.

example_sentences.japanese: このバスは臭いだけでなく、遅いし、運転が下手。
example_sentences.english: The bus is not only stinky, but it is slow and the driving is bad too.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の人口が減るだけでなく、高齢者も増える。
example_sentences.english: Not only will the population of Japan decline, but also the number of elderly will increase.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は太っているだけでなく、ニキビもいっぱいできている。大丈夫かな。
example_sentences.english: My older sister is not only gaining weight, but also has bad acne. I wonder if she is okay.

example_sentences.japanese: タケルはピアノだけじゃなく、ギターも弾けると聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Takeru can not only play the piano, but also the guitar.

example_sentences.japanese: 角にあるラーメン屋はおいしいだけでなくて量も多い。
example_sentences.english: The ramen shop on the corner is not only delicious, but the portions are large too.

formation: Verb + こと + が + できるNoun + が + できる
casual_structure: Verb + こと + が + できるNoun + が + できる
polite_structure: Verb + こと + が + できますNoun + が + できます
explanation: A grammar point that can highlight an entire phrase as being possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 馬に乗ることができる。
example_sentences.english: I can ride a horse.

example_sentences.japanese: 力仕事ができる人を探しています。
example_sentences.english: We are looking for a person that is able to do physical labor.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転ができる彼氏が欲しい。
example_sentences.english: I want a boyfriend that can drive.

example_sentences.japanese: 魚のように泳ぐことができるように毎日練習する。
example_sentences.english: I practice everyday so that I will be able to swim like a fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は料理をすることができる。
example_sentences.english: He is able to cook.

example_sentences.japanese: 泳ぐことができますか？
example_sentences.english: Can you swim?

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて、漢字を書くことができた。
example_sentences.english: I was able to write kanji for the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の姉は歌うことができる。
example_sentences.english: My older sister can sing.

example_sentences.japanese: 約束を守ることができなくてすみません。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that I am unable to keep my promise.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌うことができるでしょう？やりなさい。
example_sentences.english: You are able to sing, right? Do it!

example_sentences.japanese: やらなくてはいけないことができない。
example_sentences.english: I am unable to do the things I have to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の子供は一人で買い物ができる。
example_sentences.english: My kid can go shopping by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに提出することができると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that I will be able to submit it by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 私より君の方がピアノをうまく弾くことができる。
example_sentences.english: You can play the piano better than me.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を読むことができるだけで、凄いと思います。
example_sentences.english: Just from the fact that you are able to read Japanese, I think you are amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日日本語を勉強するだけで、将来日本語を話すことができる。
example_sentences.english: Just by studying Japanese every day, you will be able to speak Japanese in the future.

formation: Verb + （の） + かい ［い］Adjective + （の） + かい Noun + （なの） + かい ［な］Adjective + （なの） + かい
casual_structure: Verb + （の） + かい ［い］Adjective + （の） + かい Noun + （なの） + かい ［な］Adjective + （なの） + かい
explanation: A very casual, blunt way to ask questions, that is usually only used by men.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当に行きたいのかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you really want to go?

example_sentences.japanese: このドーナッツを食べたいのかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you want to eat this donut?

example_sentences.japanese: このおもちゃが欲しいのかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you want this toy?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は綺麗なのかい？
example_sentences.english: Is your girlfriend pretty?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいい人なのかい?
example_sentences.english: Is he a good person?

example_sentences.japanese: お前も一緒に行きたいんかい？
example_sentences.english: Do you also want to come with me?

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生なんかい。中学生だと思った。
example_sentences.english: You are a college student? I thought you were a middle schooler.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強してるのかい？
example_sentences.english: Are you studying?

example_sentences.japanese: これだけで十分なのかい？
example_sentences.english: Is just this enough?

example_sentences.japanese: その帽子を被って行くのかい？
example_sentences.english: Are you really going to go wearing that hat?

example_sentences.japanese: どうしたの？恥ずかしいのかい？
example_sentences.english: What's wrong? Are you embarrassed?

example_sentences.japanese: この番組を見たくないのかい？
example_sentences.english: You don't want to watch this TV program?

example_sentences.japanese: もう酔っている？久しぶりに飲んだのかい？
example_sentences.english: You are already drunk? Has it been a while since you've drank?

example_sentences.japanese: 明日テストがあるって言ってただろう。復習しないのかい？
example_sentences.english: I said that we have a test tomorrow, right? You aren't going to review?

example_sentences.japanese: 何その顔？僕が翻訳した文章が変なのかい？
example_sentences.english: What's with that face? Is the sentence I translated weird?

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談で言っていたと思った。本気なのかい？
example_sentences.english: I thought you were joking. Are you being serious?

example_sentences.japanese: 高いレストランに行こうと言ったのは彼なのに、払わないのかい？
example_sentences.english: He is the one that suggested that we go to an expensive restaurant, but he isn't going to pay?

example_sentences.japanese: 君の口すごい匂いがするよ。歯医者に行かなくていいのかい？
example_sentences.english: Your breath really stinks. You don't need to go to the dentist?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が知らないのに、そんなことを言っていいのかい？
example_sentences.english: That person isn't in the know, so is it really okay to say something like that?

example_sentences.japanese: また鍵をなくしたんかい。
example_sentences.english: You lost your keys again, didn't you?

formation: もし + Phrase［たら］(1)(1) Phrase［ば］、Phrase［と］、Phrase［ても］
casual_structure: もし + Phrase［たら］(1)(1) Phrase［ば］、Phrase［と］、Phrase［ても］
explanation: A short word which emphasizes hypothetical sentences even further.

example_sentences.japanese: もし雨が降ったら、車で行く。
example_sentences.english: If it rains, I will go by car.

example_sentences.japanese: もし彼を動物に例えると、猫に似ています。
example_sentences.english: If we were to compare him to an animal, he resembles a cat. (Even if you only slightly compared him)

example_sentences.japanese: もし今日来れれば来てね。
example_sentences.english: If you can come today, please do. (If, on the slight chance you can come)

example_sentences.japanese: もしまだ頭が痛いなら、医者に行った方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: If your head still hurts, you should go to the doctors. (If, on the slight chance it does hurt)

example_sentences.japanese: もし買い物に行ったら、お菓子を買って来て。
example_sentences.english: If you go shopping, can you buy some snacks? (If, on the slight chance you do go)

example_sentences.japanese: もし雨が降っても遊園地に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Even if it rains, we will still go to the amusement park. (If, on the slight chance it does rain)

example_sentences.japanese: もし辛いものだったら、食べられない。
example_sentences.english: If it is spicy, I can't eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: もしコーヒーを買ってくれたら、嬉しい。
example_sentences.english: If you bought coffee for me, I would be happy.

example_sentences.japanese: もしこのパソコンを彼女にあげるなら、説明書も渡してね。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to give this computer to her, (make sure to) give her the manual too.

example_sentences.japanese: もし君が文法を勉強したら、日本語を喋れるようになるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you study grammar, you will become able to speak Japanese, right?

example_sentences.japanese: もし鉛筆を持って来るのを忘れたらテストを受けられなくなる。
example_sentences.english: If you forget to bring a pencil you will not be able to take the test.

example_sentences.japanese: もしうまくなったら、皆ご飯に連れて行くよ。
example_sentences.english: If it goes well, I will take everyone out to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: もしピザを食べたかったら、自分のお金で買ってね。
example_sentences.english: If you want to eat pizza, buy it with your own money.

example_sentences.japanese: もしゲームを欲しがっても、買わない。
example_sentences.english: Even if (he) wanted a game, I won't buy one (for him).

example_sentences.japanese: もし風邪だったら、明日仕事を休んでください。
example_sentences.english: If you have caught a cold, please take tomorrow off work.

example_sentences.japanese: もし子供が好きではなかったら、学校の先生にならないと思う。
example_sentences.english: If you don't like children, I don't think that you will become a school teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: もし醤油がなくなったら、買いに行かなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: If we run out of soy sauce, I have to go buy some.

formation: Verb (A) + し + （Verb (B) + し）［い］Adjective (A) + し + （［い］Adjective (B) + し）［な］Adjective (A) + だ + し + （［な］Adjective (B) + だ + し）Noun (A) + だ + し + （Noun (B) + だ + し）
casual_structure: Verb (A) + し + （Verb (B) + し）［い］Adjective (A) + し + （［い］Adjective (B) + し）［な］Adjective (A) + だ + し + （［な］Adjective (B) + だ + し）Noun (A) + だ + し + （Noun (B) + だ + し）
explanation: A very short, casual expression that is frequently used for listing reasons.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は掃除ができるし、料理も作れるし、結婚してよかった。
example_sentences.english: He can clean and cook (among other things). I am glad that I married him.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はピアノが弾けるし、スポーツができるし、彼女に出来ないことはないと思う。
example_sentences.english: She can play the piano and she can do sports. I think there isn't anything she can't do.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランは高いし、まずいし、何もいいところがない。
example_sentences.english: This restaurant is expensive and doesn't taste good. There are no good parts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は真面目だし、親切だし、彼と友達でよかった。
example_sentences.english: He is serious and nice. I am glad that he is my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は休みだし、晴れだし、今日は公園に行こう。
example_sentences.english: Today is my day off, and it's sunny, so let's go to the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は雨が降ってたし、おばあちゃんも亡くなったし、悲しいな。
example_sentences.english: It was raining yesterday and my grandmother also passed away, so I'm sad. (Unnatural Japanese, as the level of sadness between losing your grandmother, and it being a rainy day would be completely different)

example_sentences.japanese: この赤が可愛いし、デザインがいいし、この帽子を買いたい。
example_sentences.english: This red is cute and the design is good (among other things). I want to buy this hat!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は親切だし、綺麗だし、本当に大好き。
example_sentences.english: She is kind and beautiful (among other things). I really love her.

example_sentences.japanese: この近所は治安がいいし、スーパーが近いし、人が優しいからここに住んでみたい。
example_sentences.english: This neighborhood is safe and the store is close and the people are nice, so I wouldn't mind living here.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は全然やりたくないし、やることが多すぎるし、諦めようと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I have absolutely no desire to do it and there are too many things to do (among other things), (so) I am thinking about giving up.

example_sentences.japanese: でもやったら上手になるし、将来日本に行けるかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: But if you do it, you will become proficient (among other things) and in the future you might be able to go to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミも捨てたし、洗い物もしたし、宿題もしたからゲームをしてもいい？
example_sentences.english: I threw away the garbage and I did the dishes and I did my homework. So can I play videogames (now)?

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと曇って来たし、傘持って来なかったからタクシー乗ろうと思う。
example_sentences.english: It is starting to get cloudy and I didn't bring an umbrella, so I am thinking about taking a taxi.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪の毛抜けて来たし、目も悪くなって来た。もう若くないね。
example_sentences.english: I am starting to lose my hair and my eyes are getting bad (among other things). I'm not as young as I used to be.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は家事を手伝ってくれないし、よく喧嘩するので、別れようと思っています。
example_sentences.english: My girlfriend doesn't help with the house work and we fight a lot, so I am thinking about breaking up with her.

example_sentences.japanese: このツアーで行ったら、バスの乗り放題が付いているし、見物もいっぱいできる。
example_sentences.english: If you go on this tour, an unlimited bus ride is included and you can also do a lot of sightseeing (among other things).

example_sentences.japanese: この高校の生徒たちは全員賢いし、成績がいい。
example_sentences.english: This highschool's students are all smart and they get good grades (among other things).

general_translation: Made of, Made from, Produced from, Come from
formation: Noun + で(1) + できる(1) から
casual_structure: Noun + で(1) + できる(1) から
polite_structure: Noun + で(1) + できます(1) から
explanation: A grammar point which shows what something is made from, or made with. Brought about with (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 裏面がガラスでできているスマホは最近売れ行きがいい。
example_sentences.english: Smartphones with the back made of glass have been selling well recently.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は卵と鶏肉でできる料理を紹介します。
example_sentences.english: Today we will introduce a food that is made from eggs and chicken.

example_sentences.japanese: 味噌は大豆からできると職人さんが教えてくれた。
example_sentences.english: A craftsman told me that miso is made from soybeans.

example_sentences.japanese: このワインはトップクラスのブドウからできています。どうぞ飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: This wine is made from top-class grapes. Please, try it.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーは木曜日にミルクからできている製品のセールをするよ！
example_sentences.english: The supermarket is having a sale of products made from milk on Thursday! (come from)

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機は軽い素材でできている。
example_sentences.english: Airplanes are made with light materials.

example_sentences.japanese: プラスチックやアスファルトは石油からできます。
example_sentences.english: Things like plastic and asphalt are made from oil. (come from)

example_sentences.japanese: アレルギーがあるから、ナッツとかナッツからできているものとか食べてはだめよ。
example_sentences.english: I have a nut allergy so I cannot eat things like nuts or things made from nuts.

example_sentences.japanese: 重金属は超新星爆発からできる。
example_sentences.english: Heavy metals come from supernova explosions. (made from)

example_sentences.japanese: やっと木でできている茶碗が買えて、よかった。
example_sentences.english: I am glad that I was finally able to buy a teacup made of wood.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本には木でできている家がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: There are many houses in Japan that are made of wood.

example_sentences.japanese: それはプラスチックからできているとわかっているのに、信じられない。
example_sentences.english: Although I know it is made from plastic, I just can't believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の爪はこれでできている。アダマンティウム。非常に硬いもの。
example_sentences.english: His claws are made of this. Adamantium. Incredibly tough stuff.

example_sentences.japanese: このスマホの裏面はプラスチックでできているみたいだけど、実は塗装したメタルです。
example_sentences.english: The back of this smartphone seems to be made of plastic, but in reality, it is made from painted metal.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はコンクリートでできる家が人気だ。
example_sentences.english: Recently, houses made of concrete are popular. (Houses in general)

example_sentences.japanese: この箸は竹でできている。
example_sentences.english: These chopsticks are made from bamboo. (This specific pair of chopsticks)

formation: Verb［stem］+ ながら
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ ながら
explanation: A word used to show that (B) happens during (A), with (B) being more important.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: シャワーをあびながらいいアイディアを思いついた。
example_sentences.english: While showering, I thought of a good idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日、音楽を聴きながら走ります。
example_sentences.english: I run every day, while listening to music.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転しながら携帯を使っていたら、前の車にぶつかった。
example_sentences.english: When I was using my phone while driving, I crashed into the car in front of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんがねながら、おならをした。
example_sentences.english: The baby farted while sleeping.

example_sentences.japanese: バスにのりながら、スマホでゲームをしている。
example_sentences.english: I am playing games on my phone, while riding the bus.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達をまちながら、コーヒーを飲もう。
example_sentences.english: Let's get coffee while waiting for our friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転しながら携帯を使ってはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You must not use a cellphone while driving.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と散歩をしながら、本を読んでいた。
example_sentences.english: While I was walking my dog, I was reading a book.

example_sentences.japanese: 桜をみながらパーティーをしようと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that I will have a party while viewing cherry blossoms.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はスマートフォンをつかいながら歩いていて、女の人とぶつかった。
example_sentences.english: That person was walking while using a smartphone and bumped into a woman.

example_sentences.japanese: 森の中をあるきながら、鳥の鳴き声を聞いた。
example_sentences.english: While I was walking through the forest, I listened to the birds singing.

example_sentences.japanese: シャドーイングとは日本語をききながら、繰り返すことだ。
example_sentences.english: Shadowing is repeating what you hear while listening to Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強をしながら、音楽を聞くのが好き。
example_sentences.english: I like to listen to music while doing my Japanese studies.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は晩ご飯をたべながら、一番好きな番組を見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch my favorite TV show while eating dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校の頃はサッカーの練習をしながら漢字の勉強もした。
example_sentences.english: When I was in high school, I studied kanji while also practicing soccer. (Natural Japanese, as the overall timeline of the sentence is 'while in high school')

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字の勉強をしながらアニメを見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch anime while studying kanji. (Natural Japanese, as the speaker is doing both things at the same time)

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に通いながら、トランプ氏がアメリカの大統領だった。
example_sentences.english: Trump was the president of America while I was going to university. (Unnatural Japanese. Although the events happen at the same time, they share no common subject/place)

example_sentences.japanese: あそこの病院は古いながらも中は綺麗だと聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that hospital looks nice inside, even though it is old.

general_translation: Just finished doing, Was just doing
formation: Verb［た］(1) + ところ + だ(1) Verb［ていた］
casual_structure: Verb［た］(1) + ところ + だ(1) Verb［ていた］
polite_structure: Verb［た］(1) + ところ + です(1) Verb［ていた］
explanation: A phrase that expresses the situation or place when an action has just been, or is just about to be completed.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 今食べおわったところです。
example_sentences.english: I just (now) finished eating.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は今終わったところ。もうすぐ帰る。
example_sentences.english: I just finished work. So I'll head home soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、先生に聞いたところ。
example_sentences.english: I just asked the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みを楽しんでいたところで上司から電話が来た。
example_sentences.english: I got a call from my boss just as I was enjoying my day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 服をぬいでいたところに、母が部屋に入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: My mom came into the room  just as I was taking my clothes off.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいおもちゃをわたしたところで壊れた。
example_sentences.english: Just after I gave the new toy (to someone), it broke.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達はたまたま友達に会う：「君に会いたいと今おもっていたところだわ！」
example_sentences.english: Friend meets a friend by accident: 'I was just thinking that I want to see you!'

example_sentences.japanese: 改札にはいったところで電車の扉が閉まった。
example_sentences.english: Just as I (had) entered the ticket gate, the train doors closed.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも勉強しはじめたところで何かが邪魔してくる。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I have just started studying, something gets in the way.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳を全部のんだところで子供が牛乳ほしいって言った。
example_sentences.english: Just when I had drunk all the milk, my kid said that he wanted some milk.

example_sentences.japanese: 今時計をみたところだがもう何時か忘れた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I just looked at the clock, I already forgot what time it was.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は電話で話している。みなみ：「何してるの？」 つばさ：「ちょっと前に宿題をおえたところなんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Friends are talking over the phone, Minami: 'What are you doing?' Tsubasa: 'Just finished doing the homework.'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社でご飯をたべたところ、同僚にご飯行こうと誘われた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I had eaten my lunch at work, a co-worker invited me to go out to eat. (just ate)

example_sentences.japanese: 母親は子供と話している、ともこ：「きーちゃんはもう来たの？」 母親：「今きたところですよ。」
example_sentences.english: Mother and child are speaking, Tomoko: 'Has Kii-chan already come?' Mother: 'She just came.'

example_sentences.japanese: アイスクリームをたべたところでケーキを出された。
example_sentences.english: Just when I had eaten ice cream, cake was brought out. (just ate)

general_translation: In the process of doing ~ right now/at this moment
formation: Verb［ている］+ ところ + だ
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ ところ + だ
polite_structure: Verb［ている］+ ところ + です
explanation: A phrase that highlights the situation or place in which another action is in the middle of occuring.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 今、映画をみているところです。
example_sentences.english: I am in the process of watching a movie right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をしているところだから後で電話するね。
example_sentences.english: I am in the middle of work right now, so I will call you later, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は近所で泥棒が警察から逃げているところを見た。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I saw a burglar running away from the police in my neighborhood.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、お父さんは富士山をのぼっているところです。
example_sentences.english: My dad is in the process of climbing Mt. Fuji right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官がパトロールをしているところです。
example_sentences.english: The police officer is in the process of doing her patrol at this moment.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、先生にきいているところです。
example_sentences.english: I am in the process of asking the teacher right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は今日本語を勉強しているところだけど。
example_sentences.english: I am in the process of studying Japanese right now. (Annoyed that he is being interrupted)

example_sentences.japanese: 海に行った時ライフセーバーが訓練をしているところだった。
example_sentences.english: When I went to the beach, the lifeguards were in the process of a training exercise (at that moment).

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど今晩ご飯をつくっているところなので、早く帰って来て。
example_sentences.english: Just now, I am in the process of making dinner, so hurry home.

example_sentences.japanese: レジでお金をはらっているところで、泥棒が入って来ました。
example_sentences.english: When I was in the process of paying at the register, a robber came (into the store) (at that moment).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がスターバックスに入って来た時、私はコーヒーをのんでいるところだった。
example_sentences.english: When he came into Starbucks, I was in the process of drinking coffee (at that moment).

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐドラマを見るから、今ポップコーンをつくっているところです。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to watch a drama soon, so I am in the middle of making popcorn right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 今漫画の中で一番好きな漫画をよんでいるところです。
example_sentences.english: I am in the process of reading my favorite manga of all mangas at this moment.

example_sentences.japanese: 今水道管を直してもらっているところだから、まだシャワーを浴びられない。
example_sentences.english: I am in the process of having my water pipes fixed right now, so I am unable to take a shower.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画を見ているところだったから電話に出れなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was in the middle of watching a movie, so I couldn't answer the phone.

example_sentences.japanese: ギターを弾いているところだったからメッセージに気付かなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was in the middle of playing my guitar, so I didn't notice your message.

formation: Noun (A) + と + Noun (B) + （と） + どちら(1) + がVerb1 + こと(2) + と + Verb2 + こと(2) + （と） + どちら(1) + が(1) どちらのほう、どっち、どっちのほう(2) の
casual_structure: Noun (A) + と + Noun (B) + （と） + どちら(1) + がVerb1 + こと(2) + と + Verb2 + こと(2) + （と） + どちら(1) + が(1) どちらのほう、どっち、どっちのほう(2) の
explanation: An expression that presents two choices, and then asks the speaker to choose one.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーとお茶とどちらがほしいですか。
example_sentences.english: Between coffee and tea, which do you want?

example_sentences.japanese: 私と彼女どっちが好き？
example_sentences.english: Between me and her, who do you like?

example_sentences.japanese: ピザとラーメンとどちらが好きですか。
example_sentences.english: Between pizza and ramen, which do you prefer?

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を書くことと漢字を読むこととどちらが得意ですか。
example_sentences.english: Between writing and reading kanji, which are you more confident with?

example_sentences.japanese: 遊園地に行くのと動物園に行くのとどちらがいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Between going to the amusement park, and going to the zoo, which is better?

example_sentences.japanese: 辛い物と甘い物とどっちが好き？
example_sentences.english: Between something spicy and something sweet, which do you like more?

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツすることと、ゲームすること、どちらが上手ですか。
example_sentences.english: Between playing sports and playing video games, which are you better at?

example_sentences.japanese: ひらがなとカタカナとどちらが覚えにくいですか。
example_sentences.english: Between hiragana and katakana, which one is more difficult to remember?

example_sentences.japanese: エベレストとＫ２とどちらが高い？
example_sentences.english: Between Everest and K2, which one is taller?

example_sentences.japanese: 電車で行くのと車で行くのとどちらが早いんですか。
example_sentences.english: Between going by train and going by car, which one is faster?

example_sentences.japanese: テニスとバスケとどちらが楽しいと思う？
example_sentences.english: Between tennis and basketball, which do you think is more enjoyable?

example_sentences.japanese: マンガを読むことと、新聞を読むこと、どちらが好きですか。
example_sentences.english: Between reading manga and reading the newspaper, which do you like?

example_sentences.japanese: 猫と犬とどちらが可愛いと聞かれたら、犬の方が可愛いと思う。
example_sentences.english: If I was asked which is cuter, between dogs or cats, I think I would say dogs are (cuter).

example_sentences.japanese: 二階建てのマンションと普通の家とどちらに住んでみたい？
example_sentences.english: Which one would you rather live in, between a two-story apartment and a house?

example_sentences.japanese: 苦いコーヒーと甘いコーヒーとどちらが好みですか。
example_sentences.english: Between bitter coffee and sweet coffee, which one do you prefer?

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人は逃げるのと、警察に行くのとどちらを選ぶでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I wonder which (one) the criminal will choose, between running and going to the police.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーで売っている林檎とコンビニで売っている林檎とどちらが安い？
example_sentences.english: Between apples sold at the store and apples sold at a convenience store, which one is cheaper?

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、どちら様ですか？
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry, who are you?

example_sentences.japanese: ワインとビールとどちらの方が飲みたいですか？
example_sentences.english: Between wine and beer, which would you want to drink more?

general_translation: To try to, To make sure to, To endeavor to
formation: Verb［る］(1) + ように + する(1) Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + ように + する(1) Verb［ない］
polite_structure: Verb［る］(1) + ように + します(1) Verb［ない］
explanation: A phrase that expresses attempting to do something in the manner of (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 妻にばれないようにしてくれ！
example_sentences.english: Try not to let my wife find out about it!

example_sentences.japanese: 最近太ってきたので、毎日走るようにしています。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I have been gaining weight, so I try to run every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の試合で勝てるようにする。
example_sentences.english: I will try to be able to win the next tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: 「空気が汚れるので乗り物に乗らないようにする」と弟が言いました。
example_sentences.english: My brother said 'I try not to ride vehicles, because it pollutes the air'.

example_sentences.japanese: 成績が悪いから学校を休まないようにする。
example_sentences.english: Because my grades are bad, I will try not to miss school.

example_sentences.japanese: 予約に間に合うようにしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's try to be on time for the reservation.

example_sentences.japanese: そのコップを落とさないようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try not to drop that cup.

example_sentences.japanese: あまり音が出ないようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please try not to make much noise.

example_sentences.japanese: 綺麗に包むようにします。
example_sentences.english: I will try to wrap it beautifully.

example_sentences.japanese: 途中迷わないようにしてね。
example_sentences.english: Try not to get lost en route.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月までに家を建てるようにする。
example_sentences.english: We will try to build the house by next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、日本語の文法を勉強するようにしている。
example_sentences.english: I am always making sure to study Japanese grammar every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の前で駄目とか、無理とか言わないようにしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's try not to say things like 'no' or 'that's impossible' in front of children.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者：「Ｂさんは高血圧なので、お菓子を避けるようにした方がいいですよ。」
example_sentences.english: Doctor: 'Mr. B, because you have high blood pressure you should make sure to avoid sweets.'

example_sentences.japanese: 悪役：「彼を誰とも話せないようにした。」
example_sentences.english: Villain: 'I made sure that he won't talk with anyone.'

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日野菜を食べるようにしないといけない。
example_sentences.english: You have to try to eat vegetables every day.

formation: Verb［ない］ + なければ + いけないVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + いけない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］ + なければ + いけないVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + いけない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］ + なければ + いけませんVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + いけません
explanation: A formal, hypothetical way to say that something must be done.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事にいかなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to go to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月に友達の結婚式に行かなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Next month, I have to go to my friend's wedding. (Not going to the wedding is not going to work)

example_sentences.japanese: 車は駐車場に止めなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Cars have to be parked in parking lots. (Not being parked in a parking lot is unacceptable)

example_sentences.japanese: ここで話している場合じゃない。息子を迎えに行かなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: This is not the time to talk here, I have to go pick up my son.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題で、調べなきゃいけない事があるから、パソコン貸して。
example_sentences.english: Since I need to look up something for my homework, would you please lend me your computer?

example_sentences.japanese: 冬になったら、暖房をつけなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: When winter comes, I will have to turn on the heater.

example_sentences.japanese: 覚えにくいけど、おぼえなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: It is difficult to remember, but I must remember.

example_sentences.japanese: すごく汚れたからあらわなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Because it is very dirty, I must wash it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に会いたくないけど、あわなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to see him, but I must (meet him).

example_sentences.japanese: 緑を全部青にしなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to change all the green (ones) to blue.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄みたいに大学にいかなければいけないと言われました。
example_sentences.english: I was told that I have to go to college like my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 頭が痛すぎて、薬をのまなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: My head hurts so much that I must take (drink) medicine.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週までにカタカナとひらがなを書けるようにしなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to be able to write hiragana and katakana by next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近食べすぎて太ったからやせなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I have been eating too much and gained weight, so I must lose weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が色々なことをやってみるから、ずっとみていなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Children will try all sorts of things, so you must always keep watch.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れてすみませんでした。電車が止まっていたから、バスにのらなければいけなかった。
example_sentences.english: I apologize for being late. The trains were stopped, so I had to take (ride) a bus.

formation: Verb［ない］ + なければ + ならないVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + ならない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］ + なければ + ならないVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + ならない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］ + なければ + なりませんVerb［ない］ + なきゃ + なりません
explanation: A very formal, hypothetical way to say that something must be done, that is usually only written.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の話をきかなければならないよ。
example_sentences.english: You have to listen to the teacher (talk).

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をしなければならない。
example_sentences.english: I must do my work.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が部屋に入って来たら立って挨拶をしなければならない。
example_sentences.english: If your senpai comes into the room, you must stand and greet them.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も帰りが遅くなったら妻に怒られるから、もうすぐ帰らなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: My wife is going to scold me if I come home late today too, so I have to go home soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は家事をやらなきゃならないから出かけられない。
example_sentences.english: I have to do some chores today, so I can't go out.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪の毛が長いから、きらなければならない。
example_sentences.english: My hair is long, so I have to cut it.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機に乗りたいなら、空港にいかなければならない。
example_sentences.english: If you want to ride an airplane, you have to go to the airport.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいノートをかわなければならないかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: I might have to buy a new notebook.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手になりたいから、勉強をしなければならない。
example_sentences.english: I want to become proficient in Japanese, so I have to study.

example_sentences.japanese: したくない時でも、宿題をしなければならない。
example_sentences.english: Even when you don't want to, you have to do your homework.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が何になるか、自分できめなければならない。
example_sentences.english: You must choose what you want to be.

example_sentences.japanese: しまった！今日図書館に本をかえさなければならなかった。
example_sentences.english: Oh, no! I had to return the book I borrowed from the library today.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月私の会社は３０００本以上の鉛筆をうらなければならない。
example_sentences.english: My company must sell over 3000 pencils a month.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋変な匂いがするから、掃除をしなければならない。
example_sentences.english: This room smells strange, so I must clean it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を上手に話せるようにならなければならない。
example_sentences.english: I must reach the point (become) where I am able to speak Japanese fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も駅まで送ってくれなかったから、あるかなければならなかった。
example_sentences.english: No one would take me to the station, so I had to walk.

formation: Verb［stem］+ 続ける
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 続ける
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 続けます
explanation: A phrase that highlights (A) as an action that is being continued, or occuring over and over.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: テレビをみつづけるつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: Do you plan to continue to watch TV?

example_sentences.japanese: サリーは暗くなるまで走りつづける。
example_sentences.english: Sally will continue to run until it gets dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は漢字を覚えるまで、同じ漢字を書きつづける。
example_sentences.english: I will continue to write the same kanji until I memorize it.

example_sentences.japanese: まっすぐ見て、あるきつづけなさい！
example_sentences.english: Look straight, and continue walking!

example_sentences.japanese: 文法の間違えをなおしつづけてみたらどうだ？
example_sentences.english: Why don't you try continuing to fix your grammar mistakes?

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい魚を釣るまでつりつづけます。
example_sentences.english: I will continue to fish until I catch a big fish.

example_sentences.japanese: あの警察官は一時間以上みまわりつづけた。
example_sentences.english: That police officer continued to patrol around for over one hour.

example_sentences.japanese: 餌をあげても、その犬はなきつづけるよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you give that dog a treat, it will continue to bark.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯が鳴っていたが、彼は無視して、はなしつづけた。
example_sentences.english: His phone was ringing, but he ignored it and continued talking.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法の勉強を毎日しつづけたら、すぐ上手になるだろう。
example_sentences.english: If you continue to study grammar everyday, you will become more proficient.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんにテレビを消しなさいと言われているのに、まだみつづけるの？
example_sentences.english: Even though mom told you to turn off the TV, you still continue to watch it?

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我をしたし、水ももうなくなったが彼がマラソンをはしりつづけるって。
example_sentences.english: I heard that even though he got injured and is out of water, he will continue to run the marathon.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業したので、どうやってこれから日本語の勉強をしつづけたらいいのだろう？
example_sentences.english: Since I graduated university, how am I supposed to continue my Japanese studies?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の天気は晴れのはずだったのに、雨がふりつづけていますね。
example_sentences.english: It was supposed to be a clear day today, but it is continuing to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は難しいけど、勉強を頑張って続ける。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is difficult, but I will give it my best and continue with study. (Emphasis on the continuation of studying)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は難しいけど、勉強を頑張り続ける。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is difficult, but I will continue giving it my best with study. (Emphasis on the continuation of giving it one's best)

general_translation: To tell, request, or order to do (in such a way)
formation: Verb + ように + 言（い）う(1)(1) 頼たのむ、命めいじる
casual_structure: Verb + ように + 言（い）う(1)(1) 頼たのむ、命めいじる
polite_structure: Verb + ように + 言（い）います(1) 頼たのみます、命めいじます
explanation: A slightly formal way to state that something is said, requested, or ordered in the manner of (A).
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: トムに手伝いをするようにたのんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I requested (in such a way) that Tom help out.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供に水をこぼさないようにいう。
example_sentences.english: I tell my child not to spill his water. (To tell them in a way that 'not spilling the water' is the focus)

example_sentences.japanese: 弁護士が犯人に警察に話さないようにいう。
example_sentences.english: A lawyer will tell a criminal not to talk to the police. (To tell them in a way that 'not talking to the police' is the focus)

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の漫画を借りてもいいけど、破らないようにたのむよ。
example_sentences.english: It is okay for me to let you borrow my manga, but I request that you not rip it.

example_sentences.japanese: 総理は国民に海外旅行に行かないようにめいじる。
example_sentences.english: The prime minister will order citizens to not travel abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供らが怖がらないようにたのむよ。
example_sentences.english: I request that you not scare the kids. (in such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 卵を買うようにいったはずだ。
example_sentences.english: I'm almost positive I told you to pick up eggs. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日試合があるので、今夜よく眠るようにいった。
example_sentences.english: Since we have a game tomorrow, I told them to get a good night's sleep tonight. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 息子に本を月に１冊読むようにいった。
example_sentences.english: I told my son to read a book a month. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: お弁当を持って行くことを忘れないようにいった。
example_sentences.english: I told you (in such a way as) not to forget to take your lunchbox with you.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にパーティーにプラスチックカップを持って来るようにたのんだ。
example_sentences.english: I requested that he bring plastic cups to the party. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: みんなにママに何も言わないようにたのんだがバレてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I requested that no one tell mom anything, but she found out. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生に宿題を持って来るのを忘れないようにいわれた。
example_sentences.english: We were told by the teacher not to forget to bring our homework. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: この駅に来るようにいったけどまだ来ないね。
example_sentences.english: I told them to come to the station, but they still haven't come yet. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 掃除が終わったばかりなのに洗い物もするようにたのまれた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I had just finished cleaning the house, I was requested to do the dishes. (In such a way)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のスマホを貸してあげるけど、濡れないようにたのむぞ。
example_sentences.english: I'll let you borrow my smartphone, but I request that you use it in a way that it doesn't get wet.

formation: Verb + 予定 + だNoun + の + 予定 + だ
casual_structure: Verb + 予定 + だNoun + の + 予定 + だ
polite_structure: Verb + 予定 + ですNoun + の + 予定 + です
explanation: An expression that highlights a specific plan that someone has made.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 会議は月曜日のよていです。
example_sentences.english: The meeting is planned for Monday.

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜は先輩たちと飲みに行くよていだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to go drink with some of the senior staff tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みは来週からのよていだ。
example_sentences.english: My break is planned to start from next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校で研究をするよていです。
example_sentences.english: I plan to do research at school.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業してから、仕事を探すよていです。
example_sentences.english: After graduating, I plan to look for a job.

example_sentences.japanese: 電気代が高くなるけど、エアコンを点けておくよていだ。
example_sentences.english: The electric bill might be high, but I plan to leave the air conditioner on.

example_sentences.japanese: いつ日本語を勉強し始めるよていですか。
example_sentences.english: When do you plan to start studying Japanese?

example_sentences.japanese: なるべく早く日本語を喋れるようになるよていだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to be able to speak Japanese as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつらが銀行のお金を盗むよていだったみたいです。
example_sentences.english: It appears that they planned to steal the money from the bank.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が止んだから、三時から試合が始まるよていです。
example_sentences.english: Since it stopped raining, they plan to start the match at 3.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りまでに家賃を全部払うよていだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to pay the rent, in full, by the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: セミナーが来週の金曜日に開かれるよていだ。
example_sentences.english: The seminar is planned for Friday, next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学で２年間勉強して、日本に留学するよていだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to study two years at university, then study abroad in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は晩ご飯を作るよていだったが、彼がご飯を食べて帰って来た。
example_sentences.english: I had planned to make dinner, but he ate before coming home.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は友達とステーキを食べる予定だ。
example_sentences.english: I have plans to eat a steak with a friend tomorrow. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は友達とステーキを食べる予定。
example_sentences.english: I have an 'eating a steak with a friend' plan tomorrow. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Pray that/for, Hope that/for, Keep fingers crossed that
formation: Verb［る］ + ように + 祈（いの）るVerb［ない］ + ように + 祈（いの）る
casual_structure: Verb［る］ + ように + 祈（いの）るVerb［ない］ + ように + 祈（いの）る
polite_structure: Verb［る］ + ように + 祈（いの）りますVerb［ない］ + ように + 祈（いの）ります
explanation: A structure indicating that one hopes that (A) will happen, so is praying in that manner.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 生きてここを出られるようにいのっているんだ。
example_sentences.english: I am praying that I can leave this place alive.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日雪が降って学校が休みになるようにいのる。
example_sentences.english: I hope that it snows tomorrow and school gets canceled.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界が平和になるようにいのる。
example_sentences.english: I hope that the world becomes a peaceful place.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業中に先生に呼ばれないようにいのる。
example_sentences.english: I hope that the teacher doesn't call on me during class.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の車に乗る前に死なないようにいのる。
example_sentences.english: Before I get in my friend's car, I pray that I don't die.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が安全に帰れるようにいのろう！
example_sentences.english: Let's pray that he can come home safely.

example_sentences.japanese: うまく行くようにいのってね。
example_sentences.english: Please pray that it will go well.

example_sentences.japanese: このノートパソコンに税金がかからないようにいのっている。
example_sentences.english: I am praying that this laptop is not subject to taxation!

example_sentences.japanese: うちの娘が事故に遭わないようにいのっているわ。
example_sentences.english: I am praying that our daughter won't have an accident.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風で大きな被害がないようにいのりましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's pray that there will be no bad damage due to the typhoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 留守のときに車が盗まれないようにいのっているんだ。
example_sentences.english: I am praying that my car won't be stolen when I am away.

example_sentences.japanese: トモちゃんとジュンイチロウくんが結婚するように(祈る)。
example_sentences.english: I pray that Tomo-chan and Junichirou-kun get married.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に合格できるように毎日いのっているわよ。
example_sentences.english: I am praying every day for the ability to pass the JLPT.

example_sentences.japanese: きみはスマホに水をこぼしちゃったあとでまだ使えるようにいのったほうがいいよ！
example_sentences.english: You'd better pray that phone is still usable after you spilled water on it!

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに最初のデートの日に雨が降らないようにいのったのに。
example_sentences.english: Even though I did all of that praying for no rain on our first date (it still rained).

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「マルちゃんは何を祈っているの？」娘のマルちゃん：「ワシみたいに飛べるようにいのっているのだ！」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'What are you praying for, Maru-chan?'Daughter, Maru-chan: 'I am praying for the ability to fly like an eagle!'

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は国に帰れますように。
example_sentences.english: I pray that you can go back to your country this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日のテストで合格できますように。
example_sentences.english: I pray that I can pass tomorrow's test.

example_sentences.japanese: 行きたい大学に行けるといいね。
example_sentences.english: I hope that you get into the college that you want to get into. (Hope for your sake)

example_sentences.japanese: 来年は海外旅行に行けるといいな。
example_sentences.english: I hope I can travel abroad next year. (Hope for my own sake)

formation: Verb［た］+ ばかり
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ ばかり
explanation: A semi-formal construction that subjectively expresses when something has just happened.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: 今、家をでたばかりです。
example_sentences.english: I just left home.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたばかりの時に友達から「やっぱり今日は遊べない」とメッセージが来た。
example_sentences.english: Just as I got to the station, I got a message from my friend saying, 'Actually, I can't hang out today'.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホが壊れた。昨日買ったばかりなのに…。
example_sentences.english: My smartphone broke. Even though I just bought it yesterday...

example_sentences.japanese: さっき食べたばかりだから、お腹はまだ空いていない。
example_sentences.english: I just ate earlier, so I am still not hungry.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車にのったばかりの時に携帯を落とした。
example_sentences.english: Just when I got on the train, I dropped my phone.

example_sentences.japanese: ユミに彼氏が出来たときいたばかり。
example_sentences.english: I just heard that Yumi got a boyfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: その漢字をならったばかりなのに、もう忘れた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I just learned that kanji, I already forgot it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の赤ちゃんはうまれたばかりでしょう。
example_sentences.english: The baby we just saw was just born, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 一昨日かったばかりの服が破れた。
example_sentences.english: The clothes that I just bought the day before yesterday are already ripped.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯をもう無くしたの？先月かったばかりだろう！
example_sentences.english: You already lost your phone? You just bought it last month, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 運転免許をもらったばかりで事故にあった。
example_sentences.english: Just after I got my driver's license I got into an accident.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強をはじめたばかりなのに携帯が鳴った。
example_sentences.english: I  had just started to study Japanese, but my phone rang.

example_sentences.japanese: 今くもってきたばかりなので、雨が降っているはずがない。
example_sentences.english: It just now started getting cloudy, there's no way that it is raining.

example_sentences.japanese: また海外行くの？先週台湾にいったばかりじゃない？
example_sentences.english: You are going abroad again? You just went to Taiwan last week, didn't you?

example_sentences.japanese: かえってきたばかりなのに母にコンビニに行かされた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I just got home, my mom made me go to the convenience store.

general_translation: -ification, -ization, To make something, To change, To become, Transform into
formation: Noun + 化（か）(する)Noun + 化（か） + する(1) + Noun(1) した、の
casual_structure: Noun + 化（か）(する)Noun + 化（か） + する(1) + Noun(1) した、の
explanation: A suffix showing that something will change or transform into (A). Similar to (A)ification, or (A)ization in English.
lesson_topic: Do it Like this, Did it Like that - Advanced

example_sentences.japanese: それは単純かした英語のように見える。
example_sentences.english: It appears to be simplified English.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: あと数年で運転は自動かする。
example_sentences.english: In a few years driving will become automated.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は仕事で書類をデータかする。
example_sentences.english: At work, I digitize documents.

example_sentences.japanese: 劣かした家を立て直す仕事をしたい。
example_sentences.english: I want a job rebuilding deteriorated homes.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は紙社会なので仕事をオンラインかするのは厳しい。
example_sentences.english: Since Japan is a paper society, digitalization of work is difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では高齢かが進んでいる。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, the population is aging progressively.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０世紀には経済成長の原因の一つは自動かだと考えられている。
example_sentences.english: It is considered that automation is one of the sources of economic growth in the 20th century.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、アプリはこうやって最小かするの。
example_sentences.english: Dad, you minimize apps like this.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: その新たなタイプの電池が商品かする計画があると言われている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that there are already plans to commercialize that new type of battery.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: プラスチックを液かする方法はエネルギ産業を一変させるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: The plastic liquefaction method might revolutionize the energy industry.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 助詞「の」を付けることは名詞かの方法の一つだ。
example_sentences.english: Adding the particle 'の' is one of the methods of nominalization.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 政府の努力で通貨は安定かされ始めてきました。
example_sentences.english: The currency has started to become stable due to the effort of the government. (Change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 家電製品のコンピューターかが続く。例えば最近では歯ブラシまでもＢｌｕｅｔｏｏｔｈなどを備えている。
example_sentences.english: The computerization of household appliances continues. For example, recently even toothbrushes are equipped with things like Bluetooth.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 人口の高齢かの進行は日本の最大の問題だと考えられています。
example_sentences.english: The transformation to an ever increasing elderly population is considered Japan's biggest problem.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 有名なライトノベルの漫画かが５月に始まります！
example_sentences.english: The manga adaptation of the famous light novel starts in May!(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: 「指輪物語」の映画かは、最も撮影技術の優れた作品の一つと言われている。
example_sentences.english: The movie adaptation of The Lord of the Rings is said to be one of cinematography's greatest works.(change/transform into)

example_sentences.japanese: デジタイザと画面を一体かすることで消費電力を２０％低減させることができた。
example_sentences.english: The integration of the screen and digitizer made it possible to reduce power consumption by 20%.(change/transform into)
