example_sentences.japanese: 私の携帯をかえせ！
example_sentences.english: Give back my cellphone!

example_sentences.japanese: 道路標識：「とまれ！」
example_sentences.english: Road sign: 'Stop!'

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官：「手をあげろ。」
example_sentences.english: Policeman: Raise your hands!

example_sentences.japanese: 元気だせよ。
example_sentences.english: Cheer up!

example_sentences.japanese: がんばれよ。
example_sentences.english: Just give it your all!

example_sentences.japanese: もっとのめ！
example_sentences.english: Drink more!

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミはゴミ箱にすてろ！
example_sentences.english: Throw away your trash in the trash can!

example_sentences.japanese: 早くねろ！
example_sentences.english: Sleep already!

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が「皆静かにしろ！」と言った。
example_sentences.english: The teacher said, 'Everyone, be quiet!'

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯は残さないでたべろ。
example_sentences.english: Eat your food without leaving anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察が来た、にげろ！
example_sentences.english: The police are here, run away!

example_sentences.japanese: 妹にあやまれ！
example_sentences.english: Apologize to your sister!

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は宿題をもってこい。
example_sentences.english: Bring your homework when you come tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業中は携帯の電源をきれ。
example_sentences.english: Turn off your cellphone during class.

example_sentences.japanese: 危ないからはなれろ！
example_sentences.english: Because it is dangerous, move away.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度からはもっときをつけろ！
example_sentences.english: Be more careful next time!

example_sentences.japanese: テスト：「１・２・３・４から一つ選びなさい。」
example_sentences.english: Test: 'Choose one answer out of 1, 2, 3, and 4.'

example_sentences.japanese: 犬へ：「お座り。」
example_sentences.english: To a dog: 'Sit!'

general_translation: So that, In order to, In such a way that
formation: Verb［る］(1) + ように + PhraseVerb［できる］(2) + ように + Phrase(1) Verb［ない］(2) Verb［できる］［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + ように + PhraseVerb［できる］(2) + ように + Phrase(1) Verb［ない］(2) Verb［できる］［ない］
explanation: A structure implying that (A) is done in a manner which will enable success.

example_sentences.japanese: 例えば風邪をひかないように、暖かい服装をする。
example_sentences.english: For example, I wear warm clothes so that I won't catch a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんから離れないように手をつなぐ。
example_sentences.english: I hold my mothers hands so that I won't get separated from her.

example_sentences.japanese: 泥棒が入れないように家のカギを閉める。
example_sentences.english: I lock my house, so that burglars can't come in.

example_sentences.japanese: マイケルジャクソンみたいに踊れるように毎日ダンスの練習をする。
example_sentences.english: I practice dancing every day, so that I can dance like Michael Jackson.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語をペラペラに話せるように毎日近所の人と日本語で話をしている。
example_sentences.english: I speak Japanese with my neighbor every day, so that I can speak Japanese fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強ができるように机の上を掃除した。
example_sentences.english: I tidied up my desk so that I could study.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日にスキーが出来るように仕事を休んだ。
example_sentences.english: I took the day off of work, in order to be able to ski on a weekday.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が理解できるように説明しようと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I plan to explain it in such a way that he will be able to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 大事なことをわすれないようにいつもメモをしている。
example_sentences.english: I always take notes so that I won't forget important things.

example_sentences.japanese: まにあうように数分早く出るつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to leave a few minutes earlier so that I will be on time.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽に目がくらまないように、スキーヤーはゴーグルをかけています。
example_sentences.english: The skiiers wear goggles so that they won't be blinded (disoriented) by the sun.

example_sentences.japanese: ペラペラにはなせるように日本語を勉強します。
example_sentences.english: I learn Japanese so that I will be able to speak fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、兄は私がだまっているように、お金をよくくれた。
example_sentences.english: During my childhood, my brother often gave me money in order to keep my mouth shut.

example_sentences.japanese: 火事の場合に車がもえないように、消火器を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a fire extinguisher so that my car won't go up in flames in the case of a fire..

example_sentences.japanese: 子供がナイフなどにちかづかないようにキッチンキャビネットを閉める必要がある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to close the kitchen cabinets so that children won't get near knives and the like.

example_sentences.japanese: 独立してくらせるように働き始めた。
example_sentences.english: I started working in order to be able to live independently.

example_sentences.japanese: 目が悪いので、字幕がみえるように椅子をテレビに近づけた。
example_sentences.english: Because I have bad eyes, I moved the chair closer to the TV so that I can see the subtitles.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に合格できるように、毎日文法を学んだりＮＨＫニュースを読んだりしている。
example_sentences.english: Every day I am doing things like learning grammar and reading NHK news so that I can pass the JLPT.

example_sentences.japanese: 迷子にならないように、外に出る時はいつも子供と手をつないでいる。
example_sentences.english: I always hold hands with my child when we go outside so that he/she won't get lost.

formation: Phrase + かしら
casual_structure: Phrase + かしら
explanation: A semi-polite way to express uncertainty, that is primarily used only by women.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it will rain today.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこにいるのはタケル君かしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if that person over there is Takeru-kun.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は晴れるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it will clear up tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐ冷房をつけてくれないかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if they won't turn on the air conditioning for us soon.

example_sentences.japanese: ここで食べてもいいかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if it is ok to eat here.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆は変な匂いがするから、食べれるかしら。
example_sentences.english: Since natto has a strange smell, I wonder if I will be able to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: あまり理解出来ていないみたい。行けるかしら。
example_sentences.english: It appears that they don't really understand. I wonder if it will go well.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りまでに出せるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if I will be able to turn it in by the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆が言うように魚みたいに泳げるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if he can really swim like a fish, like everyone says.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは何時ごろ帰ってくるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what time dad will get home.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が犯人だったら、どうなるかしら。
example_sentences.english: If he is the criminal, I wonder what will happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は飛ぶのが怖いので、飛行機に乗れるかしら。
example_sentences.english: He is terrified of flying, I wonder if he can board the plane.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いよ。冷房を入れていいかしら。
example_sentences.english: It's hot. I wonder if it is okay to turn on the air conditioning.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はイケメンだし、頭がいいし、悪いところがあるかしら。
example_sentences.english: He is both handsome and smart, I wonder if he has any shortcomings.

example_sentences.japanese: 観光客がこれ以上くるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if any more sightseers will come.

general_translation: typical of, -ish・like, appropriate for, becoming of, befitting
formation: Noun + らしい。Noun + らしく + PhraseNoun + らしい + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + らしい。Noun + らしく + PhraseNoun + らしい + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + らしい + です。Noun + らしく + PhraseNoun + らしい + Noun
explanation: A word showing that (A) is expressing typical features that would usually be expected of itself, or typical of itself.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もっと大人らしくしなさいよ！」
example_sentences.english: 'Behave more like an adult!' (befitting of)

example_sentences.japanese: トムは本当に男らしいね。
example_sentences.english: Tom, you are really manly.

example_sentences.japanese: タケル君はもうお兄ちゃんなので、お兄ちゃんらしくしなさい！
example_sentences.english: Takeru, you are already an older brother, so you should act like an older brother!

example_sentences.japanese: やっと１０月らしい天気になったね。
example_sentences.english: It has finally become October-like weather, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: トムがこんなに勉強をしているのは見たことがない、トムらしくない。
example_sentences.english: I've never seen Tom study this much. It's very uncharacteristic of him.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は８月らしくないです。涼しいです。
example_sentences.english: Today is not typical of August. It's cool.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は女らしくない人だ。
example_sentences.english: She is an unladylike person.

example_sentences.japanese: 「やっと夏らしい日が来たよ！」
example_sentences.english: 'At last, a day befitting of summer has come!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「そんなことを言うのは、彼女らしい。」
example_sentences.english: 'Saying something like that, (it is) typical of her.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「カップルらしく映画を見に行こう！」
example_sentences.english: 'Let's go to the movies like couples do!' (typical of)

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたの笑顔の愛らしさに気づいたばかりだわ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I just noticed the loveliness of your smile.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「テーマパークらしいテーマパークの方が好きだよ。ブラックジャックと....」
example_sentences.english: 'I prefer theme park-like theme parks! With blackjack and…' (typical of)

example_sentences.japanese: スコット：「これは一番だいこんらしいだいこんだよ！」
example_sentences.english: Scott: 'This is the most radish radish among radishes!' (very radish-like/typical of)

example_sentences.japanese: トモちゃんは女の子だけど、女らしくない。
example_sentences.english: Tomo-chan is a girl, but she is unladylike. (lacks typical traits of a woman)

example_sentences.japanese: 「今年の５月は５月らしくない日が多いじゃないか。」
example_sentences.english: This May will have many days that are not May-typical, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 「いかにもめぐにんらしいね。最初に爆発して質問は後だよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Typical of Megunin. First explosions, then questions.'

example_sentences.japanese: 父親：「学校に行きたくなくなることは子供らしい。オレもそうだったよ。」
example_sentences.english: Father: 'Not wanting to go to school is typical of children. I was also like that.'

example_sentences.japanese: スーツの色で一番人気なのは黒だと思っている。一番サラリーマンらしいし、他の服にも合いやすいから。
example_sentences.english: I think that the most popular suit color is black. Because it is (the color) most typical of company employees and easily matches other clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の８月は夏らしい夏だね。
example_sentences.english: August this year is the prime example of summer. (Literally, 'the most summery summer')

general_translation: Kind of thing, Kind of vibe, Kind of feeling
formation: Phrase + って感（かん）じ
casual_structure: Phrase + って感（かん）じ
polite_structure: Phrase + って感（かん）じ + です
explanation: A casual phrase used to describe the vibe or nature of an object or situation without making a definitive statement.

example_sentences.japanese: あの雲、夏ってかんじ！
example_sentences.english: Those clouds have a summer kind of vibe!

example_sentences.japanese: ジェシーはアメリカ人ってかんじの人だ。
example_sentences.english: Jesse is a person with an American kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 今はお米が食べたいってかんじなの。
example_sentences.english: Right now, I have an 'I want to eat rice' kind of feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月も全然お金がないってかんじで大変。
example_sentences.english: It's tough because it's an 'I have absolutely no money this month either' kind of situation. (Feeling)

example_sentences.japanese: このカバンは軽くて持ちやすいってかんじで人気だよ！
example_sentences.english: This bag is popular for its 'light and easy to carry' kind of vibe!

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に帰って、早くお風呂に入りたいってかんじ。
example_sentences.english: It's an 'I want to go back to Japan and take a bath immediately' kind of feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: ゆうこ：「今日は天気が悪いね。」あやか：「うん。一日家にいたいってかんじ。」
example_sentences.english: Yuko: 'The weather is bad today.' Ayaka: 'Yeah. It's an "I want to stay home all day" kind of vibe.'

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がスーツを着ると、飼っている犬が寂しいってかんじの顔で僕を見てきます。
example_sentences.english: When I wear a suit, my pet dog looks at me with a 'lonely' kind of expression. (Feeling)

example_sentences.japanese: たいが：「彼氏と最近どうなの？」さくら：「うーん。まあまあってかんじかな。」
example_sentences.english: Taiga: 'How are things with your boyfriend recently?' Sakura: 'Hmm. It's a so-so kind of vibe.'

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しすぎて、１日２４時間じゃ足りないってかんじなんです。
example_sentences.english: Work is so busy, it's a '24 hours in a day isn't enough' kind of feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の姉は熱があっても、大雪で電車が止まっても必ず仕事に行くような、すごく真面目ってかんじの女性なんです。
example_sentences.english: My older sister is the kind of woman who will definitely go to work even if she has a fever or if the trains stop due to heavy snow; she gives off a very serious kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族で旅行に行く時、私たちの準備が遅いから、お父さんはいつも早くしろってかんじで玄関で一人で待っているの。
example_sentences.english: When we go on family trips, because we are slow to get ready, my dad is always waiting alone at the entrance with a 'hurry up' kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜、誰もいない公園の真ん中で座っている男がいて、とにかく変な人ってかんじでした。
example_sentences.english: Last night, there was a man sitting in the middle of an empty park, and he just gave off a totally weird guy kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもキャットフードしかあげていない私の猫に、ツナ缶をあげたら三日間何も食べてませんってかんじの速さで全部食べたよ。
example_sentences.english: When I gave canned tuna to my cat, who I usually only give cat food to, she ate it all with a speed that gave off an 'I haven't eaten anything for three days' kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 家で仕事をしながら洗濯や掃除をして、子供にお昼ご飯を作って夕方にまた夜ご飯を作って、すごく大変ってかんじの一日だった。
example_sentences.english: I worked from home while doing laundry and cleaning, made lunch for the kids, and then made dinner again in the evening; it was a 'really exhausting' kind of vibe of a day.

example_sentences.japanese: たくさん食べたいって感じだね。
example_sentences.english: It feels like you want to eat a lot, huh.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人って感じ。
example_sentences.english: They have a Japanese kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 可愛いって感じの子だよ。
example_sentences.english: She is a girl with a cute kind of vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 複雑って感じ。
example_sentences.english: It has a complicated vibe.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は朝から雨で、電車も遅れて、会社についたらもう会議が始まってて、資料も忘れて、もう最悪だったって感じ。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday it was like raining from the morning, the train was late, the meeting had already started by the time I got to the office, I forgot my documents, and it was just, like, the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長：「君はどう思う？」部下：「時間が足りなくて間に合わないって感じですね。」
example_sentences.english: President: 'What do you think?' Subordinate: 'It is, like, we don't have enough time and won't make it, kind of vibes.'

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん：「どのくらい頭が痛いの？」娘：「うーん。とにかく頭が痛すぎて、よく分かんないって感じ。」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'How badly does your head hurt?' Daughter: 'Hmm. My head just hurts way too much, and I don't really know, kind of thing.'

general_translation: To look, To seem, To appear
formation: Verb + よう(1) + に + みえる ［い］Adjective［い］+ そうに(2) + みえる ［な］Adjective + （そう） + に + みえる Noun + （の + よう(1)）+ に + みえる(1) みたい(2) く
casual_structure: Verb + よう(1) + に + みえる ［い］Adjective［い］+ そうに(2) + みえる ［な］Adjective + （そう） + に + みえる Noun + （の + よう(1)）+ に + みえる(1) みたい(2) く
polite_structure: Verb + よう(1) + に + みえます ［い］Adjective［い］+ そうに(2) + みえます ［な］Adjective + （そう） + に + みえます Noun + （の + よう(1)）+ に + みえます(1) みたい(2) く
explanation: An expression that strictly highlights the way something looks, or can be viewed.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は忙しそうにみえる。
example_sentences.english: He looks/appears busy.

example_sentences.japanese: あの雲はアイスクリームにみえる。
example_sentences.english: That cloud looks like ice cream.

example_sentences.japanese: サムの泳ぎ方は溺れているようにみえる。
example_sentences.english: Sam's way of swimming looks as if he is drowning.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒そうにみえるけど、大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: You look like you are cold, are you okay?

example_sentences.japanese: あの仕事は大変そうにみえる。
example_sentences.english: That job looks like it is tough.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で暗い所にいるとなんでも顔のようにみえる。
example_sentences.english: When I am in a dark place alone, everything looks like a face.

example_sentences.japanese: このコートを着ると太ったみたいにみえるから嫌いだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems to look like I got fat when I wear this coat, so I don't like it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は怒っているようにみえる。
example_sentences.english: The teacher looks/appears angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 水ぼうそうにみえるニキビ。
example_sentences.english: Pimples that look like/have the appearance of chicken pox.

example_sentences.japanese: このスーツケースはかるくみえる。
example_sentences.english: This suitcase looks light/appears light.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は幸せそうにみえる。
example_sentences.english: She seems/appears happy.

example_sentences.japanese: この写真を見ると私たちは家族にみえる。
example_sentences.english: Looking at this picture, we seem like a family. (look like・appear as)

example_sentences.japanese: 綺麗にみえるけど、近くで見たら汚れている。
example_sentences.english: It might appear/look clean, but if you look closely it is dirty.

example_sentences.japanese: 雲にみえるけど、実は煙だ。
example_sentences.english: It might look like/appear to be clouds, but it is actually smoke.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの商品が高いから、これはやすくみえる。
example_sentences.english: The surrounding products are expensive so this seems cheap/looks cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 歩くのが速いから、走っているようにみえる。
example_sentences.english: Because he walks quickly, it looks like/appears as if he is running.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランのスープは美味しそうにみえるけど、実は美味しくない。
example_sentences.english: This restaurant's soup might look/appear good, but it is actually not good.

example_sentences.japanese: 遠くから見ると背がたかくみえるけど、本当は背が低い。
example_sentences.english: From afar it looks like I am tall/I appear tall, but I am actually short.

general_translation: It seems that, It can be deduced, One can conclude that
formation: Verb + とみえる［い］Adjective + とみえる［な］Adjective + （だ） + とみえるNoun + （だ） + とみえる
casual_structure: Verb + とみえる［い］Adjective + とみえる［な］Adjective + （だ） + とみえるNoun + （だ） + とみえる
polite_structure: Verb + とみえます［い］Adjective + とみえます［な］Adjective + （だ） + とみえますNoun + （だ） + とみえます
explanation: An expression that makes a conclusion about the way that something appears.

example_sentences.japanese: あの親は優しいとみえる。
example_sentences.english: Those parents seem nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の窓が外から割られていた。泥棒に入られたとみえる。
example_sentences.english: The windows of the house have been broken from the outside, so I can deduce that a burglar came in.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は上着を脱いだ。彼は暑いとみえる。
example_sentences.english: He took off his jacket, so it seems that he is hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はサンドイッチを残した。彼はサンドイッチが嫌いだとみえる。
example_sentences.english: He left the sandwich, so I can conclude that he doesn't like sandwiches.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは今日は会社に来なかった。トムは昨日風邪を引いたから今日は休みだとみえる。
example_sentences.english: Tom didn't come to work today. He caught a cold yesterday, so I can conclude that he is resting today.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に行ったけど留守とみえた。
example_sentences.english: I went to their house, but it seemed that they weren't home.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はマラソンを走ったとみえてハアハア言っている。
example_sentences.english: It seems that he ran a marathon, he is breathing heavily.

example_sentences.japanese: テストに落ちたから、勉強してなかったとみえる。
example_sentences.english: Since he failed the test, one can conclude that he did not study.

example_sentences.japanese: 水とみえたが、ラムネでした。
example_sentences.english: It seemed that it was water, but it was lemon soda. (One can conclude that)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が今プールから出て来たとみえて、全部が濡れている。
example_sentences.english: He is completely soaked. It can be deduced that he just got out of a pool.

example_sentences.japanese: 教える必要がなかった。元々知っていたとみえる。
example_sentences.english: There was no need for me to teach it. It seems that they already knew it. (One can conclude that)

example_sentences.japanese: もう準備してあった。誰かから聞いていたとみえる。
example_sentences.english: They had already prepared. One can conclude that they heard about it from someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も理解出来ていないとみえて、皆は難しい顔をしていた。
example_sentences.english: One can conclude that no one understood from all of the confused faces.

example_sentences.japanese: この城が静かだとみえて、忍者も居ない。
example_sentences.english: This castle seems so quiet that there aren't even any ninjas. (One can conclude that)

example_sentences.japanese: 外に干した洗濯物はびしょ濡れです。雨が降ったとみえる。
example_sentences.english: The laundry that I hung outside is soaking wet. It can be deduced that it rained.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋の電気が点いている。彼はまだ忙しいとみえる。
example_sentences.english: The light is still on in his room. It seems that he is still busy. (One can conclude that)

example_sentences.japanese: 幽霊を見たとき、彼女が叫んだ。驚いたとみえる。
example_sentences.english: When she saw a ghost, she screamed. One could conclude that she was surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の宿題は難しかったとみえて、誰も終わらせてなかった。
example_sentences.english: One can conclude that today's homework was difficult, because no one completed it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が生徒に「廊下で走るな」と言った。
example_sentences.english: The teacher said 'don't run in the hallway' to the students.

example_sentences.japanese: 母とレストランに行った。
example_sentences.english: I went to the restaurant with my mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 昼寝をすると夜に寝れなくなる。
example_sentences.english: I can't fall asleep at night if I take a nap during the day.

formation: Noun + 風（ふう）Noun + 風（ふう） + （の） + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + 風（ふう）Noun + 風（ふう） + （の） + Noun
explanation: A suffix highlighting that something is in the style or air of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんはオランダふうのサラダが好きだよ。
example_sentences.english: My mother likes Dutch-style salad.

example_sentences.japanese: ９０年代ふうファッションがまた流行ってきています。
example_sentences.english: 90's style fashion is starting to gain popularity again.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカふう料理が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like American style food.

example_sentences.japanese: メキシコふうの料理を食べたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat Mexican food.

example_sentences.japanese: 広島ふうのお好み焼きが一番おいしい。
example_sentences.english: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is the most delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: パブは韓国ふうのほうがいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to pubs, I think I prefer the Korean style.

example_sentences.japanese: 中国ふうのドレスがほしいよ！
example_sentences.english: I want the Chinese-style dress!

example_sentences.japanese: このイラストは漫画ふうだね。
example_sentences.english: This illustration is in manga style, right?

example_sentences.japanese: それはアメリカふうの生活と言われている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that that is the American style of life.

example_sentences.japanese: 「なあんだ。ここには関西ふうのお好み焼きしかないのか。」
example_sentences.english: 'What?! They only have Kansai-style okonomiyaki here?'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では洋ふうの結婚式が人気です。
example_sentences.english: A western-style marriage ceremony is popular in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞を読むサラリーマンふうの中年男がひとりで座っていた。
example_sentences.english: The newspaper-reading, salaryman-style, middle-aged man sat by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このドレスは今ふうだと思ったら大間違いだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'If you thought that this dress is in a modern style, then you were greatly mistaken.'

example_sentences.japanese: １９世紀ふうの時計を買ってよかった。
example_sentences.english: I'm glad that I bought this 19-century-style clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生ふうの若い女性はタバコを吸いながら電話で話していた。
example_sentences.english: The young woman in university-style (appearance) was talking on the phone while smoking a cigarette.

example_sentences.japanese: ネットショップの広告：「ヴィンテージふう家具、ご覧ください！」
example_sentences.english: Online shop's advertisement: 'Vintage-style furniture, please have a look!'

general_translation: Can see, Can be seen, Can observe, Can be observed, Be evident, Chance to see something
formation: Noun + が(1) + 見（み）られる(1)も
casual_structure: Noun + が(1) + 見（み）られる(1)も
polite_structure: Noun + が(1) + 見（み）られます(1)も
explanation: A grammar point indicating that (A) can be observed, given the right opportunity or ability of the viewer.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏には、ここでクマがみられます。
example_sentences.english: In summer, bears can be seen here.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋からは富士山がみられる。
example_sentences.english: Mount Fuji can be seen from this room. (If you look closely, and it is a clear day)

example_sentences.japanese: 奈良に行くと、横断歩道を渡るシカがみられる。
example_sentences.english: If you go to Nara, you can observe deer crossing the crosswalk. (If you are lucky, and the timing is right)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はタッチパネルが付いている冷蔵庫がみられる。
example_sentences.english: Recently, refrigerators with touch panels can be seen.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はタッチパネルが付いている冷蔵庫がみれる。
example_sentences.english: Recently, you can see refrigerators with touch panels.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近ガラスでできているスマホがみられる。
example_sentences.english: Recently, smartphones that are made of glass can be seen.

example_sentences.japanese: いつか姫路城がみられるといいな。
example_sentences.english: I hope I can see Himeji Castle one day. (chance to be seen)

example_sentences.japanese: どこで紙芝居がみられますか？
example_sentences.english: Where can the picture story show be seen?

example_sentences.japanese: よく見てみると動物の足跡がみられる。
example_sentences.english: If you look closely, animal tracks can be observed.

example_sentences.japanese: 変化していくインターネットの時代なので、言語にも急速な変化がみられる。
example_sentences.english: Since we live in the fast-paced age of the internet, rapid changes in language can be observed.

example_sentences.japanese: カメレオンは、環境が変わったとき、色の変化がみられる。
example_sentences.english: You can observe a chameleon change color when the surrounding environment changes.

example_sentences.japanese: ら抜き言葉の使用は、若者によくみられる。
example_sentences.english: Usage of ら removed words can often be seen among young people.

example_sentences.japanese: インドネシアに行ったら多くの火山がみられる。
example_sentences.english: If you go to Indonesia, many volcanoes can be seen.

example_sentences.japanese: 写真には宇宙飛行士のような姿がみられる。
example_sentences.english: A figure looking like an astronaut is visible in the photograph.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の技術で地球にいながらブラックホールの写真がみられます。
example_sentences.english: With modern technology, we can observe photographs of black holes while being on earth.

example_sentences.japanese: キウイフルーツは皮をむいて食べるのが一般的ですが、皮をむかないで食べる人もみられます。
example_sentences.english: Kiwifruit is generally eaten after peeling the skin, but people who eat it without peeling the skin can also be observed.

formation: Verb + こと(1) + に気（き）がつくNoun + に気（き）がつく(1) の
casual_structure: Verb + こと(1) + に気（き）がつくNoun + に気（き）がつく(1) の
polite_structure: Verb + こと(1) + に気（き）がつきますNoun + に気（き）がつきます(1) の
explanation: A way to highlight that someone's attention has been drawn to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私の気持ちにきがついたのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if he noticed my feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせ場所に着いてから、携帯を忘れたことにきがついた。
example_sentences.english: I realized that I had forgotten my phone only after I arrived at the meeting place.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬に餌をあげていないのにきがついた。
example_sentences.english: I realized that I didn't feed my dog.

example_sentences.japanese: 猛スピードでこっちに来ている車にきがついた。
example_sentences.english: I noticed that there was a car heading this direction at a crazy speed.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、お金を忘れたことにきがついたばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: I just now noticed that I forgot my money.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分のミスにきがつきましたか。
example_sentences.english: Did you notice your mistake?

example_sentences.japanese: わぁ！きがついたの？嬉しい！
example_sentences.english: Woah! You noticed? I'm so happy!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は母の誕生日だ！ きがついていなかった。
example_sentences.english: Today is Mom's birthday! I didn't notice.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が話し終わった事にきがついていなかったです。
example_sentences.english: I didn't realize that the teacher was done talking.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が新しい車を買ったことにきがついた？
example_sentences.english: Did you notice that I bought a new car?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、私の新しい靴にきがついてくれた。
example_sentences.english: He noticed my new shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 長い間牛乳を飲んでいないから、腐ったことにきがついていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I hadn't had any milk in a while, so I didn't realize that it had gone bad. (Literally - Wasn't realizing)

example_sentences.japanese: 時計を見て、もう４時間が経ったことにきがついた。
example_sentences.english: I looked at the clock and realized that 4 hours had already passed.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰って来た時卵を買うことを忘れたことにきがついた。
example_sentences.english: When I got home I realized that I forgot to buy eggs.

example_sentences.japanese: これが最後の問題だと言うことにきがついていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn't realize this was the last question. (Literally - Wasn't realizing)

formation: ［い］Adjective［て］ + も + ［い］Adjective［て］ + も［な］Adjective +  でも + ［な］Adjective + でもNoun (A) + でも + Noun (B) + でも［い］Adjective［て］ + も + ［い］Adjective［て］ + も + Phrase［ない］［な］Adjective + でも + ［な］Adjective + でも + Phrase［ない］Noun (A) + でも + Noun (B) + でも + Phrase［ない］
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective［て］ + も + ［い］Adjective［て］ + も［な］Adjective +  でも + ［な］Adjective + でもNoun (A) + でも + Noun (B) + でも［い］Adjective［て］ + も + ［い］Adjective［て］ + も + Phrase［ない］［な］Adjective + でも + ［な］Adjective + でも + Phrase［ない］Noun (A) + でも + Noun (B) + でも + Phrase［ない］
explanation: A casual phrase which indicates that even if it is (A), or even if it is (B), the result is still the same.

example_sentences.japanese: これでも、それでも、何でもいいです！
example_sentences.english: Whether this, or that, whatever (is fine)!

example_sentences.japanese: サッカーでもバスケットボールでもいいからスポーツをやりたい。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether it is soccer or basketball, I want to play sports.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキでもクッキーでも苺が入っていたらどちらも食べない。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a cake or a cookie, I will not eat it if it has strawberries in it.

example_sentences.japanese: サッカーでも、卓球でも、彼ならスポーツは何でもできる。
example_sentences.english: Whether it's soccer or table tennis, he can play any sport.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車でも、バスでも行ける場所なので、便利です。
example_sentences.english: You can get there whether by train or bus, so it's convenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がＭａｃでもＷｉｎｄｏｗｓでも使えるって。
example_sentences.english: (He said) that whether it's Mac or Windows, he can use them.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃんけんでも、サイコロでも何でもいいから、早く決めてよ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is with rock, paper, scissors or with dice, or whatever, hurry up and decide.

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書でも、ネットでも日本語を学ぶことが出来るから習ってみたらどう？
example_sentences.english: Whether it is with a textbook or online, you can learn Japanese so why not give it a shot?

example_sentences.japanese: ６０点でも、１００点でも、合格したらいいんだよ。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter whether you get a 60 or a 100, as long as you pass.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車でも、バスでも、飛行機でも、タクシーでも使える。
example_sentences.english: You can use either a train or a bus or a plane or a taxi.

example_sentences.japanese: ジュースでもコーラでも何でもいいから、早く飲みましょう。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter whether it is juice or cola, let's hurry up and drink!

example_sentences.japanese: 喉が渇いたので、水でも、お茶でも飲みたいな。
example_sentences.english: I am thirsty, so whether it is water or tea I want to drink it.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語でも、日本語でも、中国語でも喋れる彼が凄いと思う。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is English or Japanese or even Chinese, he (who can speak those languages) is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 円でも、ドルでも商品を買えるからこのコンビニが便利だ！
example_sentences.english: Whether it is with yen or dollars, you can buy products at this convenience store so it is convenient!

formation: それに + (Additional Information) Phrase
casual_structure: それに + (Additional Information) Phrase
explanation: A phrase used for giving additional information, by stating on that which was said, or to that which was said.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動は楽しいです。それに体にいいです。
example_sentences.english: Exercise is fun. In addition, it's good for you.

example_sentences.japanese: それに彼は家事もしないんでしょう？
example_sentences.english: In addition, he doesn't do house chores either, right?

example_sentences.japanese: リサの会社には残業がない。それに給料もいい。
example_sentences.english: Lisa's company doesn't have overtime work. What's more, her salary is good too.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、道で五千円を拾って、それに車が抽選で当たった！
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, I picked up 5 thousand yen on the street, and in addition to that I won a car in the lottery. (Natural Japanese, as both events are positive)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は雨がいっぱい降るし、それに風も強いし、外に出れなくて寂しい。
example_sentences.english: Recently, it has been raining a lot, and in addition to that the wind has been strong. I'm sad that I can't go outside. (Natural Japanese, as both events are negative)

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝はマッサージに行って、それにスピード違反の切符も切られた。
example_sentences.english: I went to get a massage this morning, and moreover I also got a speeding ticket. (Unnatural Japanese, as one event is positive, while the other is negative)

example_sentences.japanese: 夜遅くまで働きます。それに朝も早いです。
example_sentences.english: I work late into the night. In addition, I am up early.

example_sentences.japanese: この旅館の料理が美味しい。それに周りの景色も美しい。
example_sentences.english: This Japanese-style hotel's food is delicious. Moreover, the surrounding scenery is beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は住みやすい。それに病院代が安い。
example_sentences.english: It is easy to live in Japan. Moreover medical expenses are reasonable.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上からの景色が綺麗。それに空気も綺麗。
example_sentences.english: The scenery from atop the mountain is beautiful. In addition the air is clear.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランのデザートはアップルパイ。それにアイスクリームが付いてる。
example_sentences.english: This restaurant's dessert is apple pie. In addition, ice cream is included.

example_sentences.japanese: タブレットを買っても、あまり使わないだろう？それにＹｏｕＴｕｂｅしか見ないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if you buy a tablet, you wouldn't really use it right? Besides you would do nothing but watch Youtube, right?

example_sentences.japanese: あの夫婦には子供が六人居て、それに犬を四匹も飼っています。
example_sentences.english: That couple has six children, in addition to also having four dogs.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫁さんが車が必要と言っているけど、置く場所がない。それに電車で通うから要らないと思う。
example_sentences.english: My wife keeps saying that we need a car, but we don't have anywhere to put it. Moreover we take the train, so I don't think we need one.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬を飼いたいが、庭がない。それに家が狭いから可哀想だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I want to get a dog, but I don't have a yard. In addition my house is small so I don't think that it would be fair to the dog.

example_sentences.japanese: 誕生日にギターをもらったけど弾き方が分からない。それに習いたいと思わない。
example_sentences.english: I got a guitar for my birthday, but I don't know how to play. Moreover I don't want to learn.

example_sentences.japanese: コーラを４杯頼んだら、一杯無料です。それにフライドポテトが付いています。
example_sentences.english: If you order four colas, you get one free. In addition you get some french fries.

general_translation: Because of that, So?, And then?, Therefore, With that
formation: Phrase (A)。 それで + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A)。 それで + Phrase (B)
explanation: A casual sentence starter used either to explain the result of what was said previously, or ask what happened with that.

example_sentences.japanese: 「それでプロジェクトどうなったのですか？」「期限通りに終わりました。」
example_sentences.english: 'And then, what happened to the project?''We finished it on time.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私は子供のころにお医者さんに命を救われた。それで医者になろうと思った。
example_sentences.english: A doctor saved my life when I was a child. Due to that, I became determined to be a doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は電車の中で痴漢をした。それで彼は警察に捕まった。
example_sentences.english: He groped someone on the train. As a result of that, he got arrested by the cops.

example_sentences.japanese: ＪＬＰＴに合格したいです。それで毎日しっかり勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I want to pass the JLPT. Therefore, I study hard every day.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りには多くの桜が植えられている。それで外国人が花見に来る人気の観光スポットになった。
example_sentences.english: In this area, numerous cherry trees are growing. Because of that, it has become a popular tourist attraction where many foreigners come to view cherry blossoms.

example_sentences.japanese: このヘビは有毒の一種です。それで非常に危険だと考えられています。
example_sentences.english: This snake is one of (many) venomous species. Because of that, it is considered extremely dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: いずくさんは子供の頃よくいじめられました。それで弱い者の味方になっています。
example_sentences.english: Izuku-san was often bullied as a child. Therefore, he is now an ally of the weak.

example_sentences.japanese: きょうこ：「昨日、私たちは初めてデートしたわ。」あけみ：「へえーそうなんだ。それでどうだった？」
example_sentences.english: Kyoko: 'Yesterday, we went on a date for the first time.'Akemi: 'Oh yeah? And then? What happened?'

example_sentences.japanese: きょうこ：「その後、映画を見に行ったわ。」あけみ：「それで何があったの？」
example_sentences.english: Kyoko: 'After that, we went to a movie. 'Akemi: 'And then? Did something happen?'

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋は真っ暗だった。それで彼は何も見えなかった。
example_sentences.english: The room was pitch black. Therefore, he couldn't see anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までにプロジェクトを終わらせなきゃ。それで今日は一緒に遊べないんだ。
example_sentences.english: I have to finish a project by tomorrow. So, I cannot hang out today.

example_sentences.japanese: うるさいあけみ：「それでどうなったの。」きょうこ：「ずっと同じ質問するのは止めて。イライラするわ。」
example_sentences.english: Annoying Akemi: 'And then? What happened after that?'Kyoko: 'Stop constantly asking the same question. It's getting on my nerves.'

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館の映画前の宣伝は長すぎる。それでいつも上映が始まった後２０分経ってから行くよ。
example_sentences.english: The advertisements before the movie are too long. Because of that, I always go 20 minutes after the screening starts.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品は手作業で作られています。それで値段がより高いのです。
example_sentences.english: This product is handcrafted. Therefore, the price is higher.

example_sentences.japanese: サリーは世界中のほとんどの国に行ったことがある。それで旅行会社で働くことにした。
example_sentences.english: Sally has been to most countries in the world. Because of that, she decided to work at a travel agency.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、会議を始めます。
example_sentences.english: Well then, I will start the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: それじゃミクは来ないの？
example_sentences.english: In that case, Miku, are you not coming?

formation: Question Word + か + わかる(1)(1) 覚（おぼ）える、決（き）める、知（し）っている and so on
casual_structure: Question Word + か + わかる(1)(1) 覚（おぼ）える、決（き）める、知（し）っている and so on
explanation: A particle used to highlight questions or statements of uncertainty within longer sentences.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がどこにいるかわかる？
example_sentences.english: Do you know where I am?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 忘年会に社長が来るか分かりますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know if the CEO is coming to the end of year party? (Literally, 'If the CEO is coming, do you know?')

example_sentences.japanese: これで足りるか分かる？
example_sentences.english: Do you know if this is enough? (Literally, 'If this is enough, do you know?')

example_sentences.japanese: 何でこのビルを壊すか知っていますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you know why they are destroying this building? (Literally, 'Why they are destroying it, do you know?')

example_sentences.japanese: お祭りは何時に終わるか知ってる？
example_sentences.english: Do you know what time the festival is going to end? (Literally, 'What time it will end, do you know?')

example_sentences.japanese: いつ美術館に行くか決めましたか？
example_sentences.english: Have you decided when you are going to the art museum?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の好みの味が何かわかる？
example_sentences.english: Do you know what kind of flavor(s) he likes?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が誰のことを好きかわかりません。
example_sentences.english: I do not know who he likes.(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 何を消したか知っている？
example_sentences.english: Do you know what was erased?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: ん？先生はどこに行ったかわかる？
example_sentences.english: Huh? Do you know where the teacher went?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がどんなセーターを着ていたか覚えていませんか？
example_sentences.english: Do you remember what kind of sweater she was wearing?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日どこで集まるかも決めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please decide where we will gather tomorrow as well.(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の嫌いなレストランがどこか確認してください。
example_sentences.english: Please confirm what restaurants she is not fond of.(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 誰が道具を持ってきたか彼に聞いてみてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Would you mind asking him who brought tools (and who didn't)?(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 誰が一番上手に漢字を書けるかわかるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if you know who is the best at writing kanji.(question within a larger sentence)

example_sentences.japanese: 誰が一番上手かわからないけど、誰が一番下手かわかるよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't know who is the best, but I know who is the worst.(question within a larger sentence)

general_translation: But still, And yet, Even so, Nevertheless
formation: Phrase (A) + それでも + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + それでも + Phrase (B)
explanation: An expression that highlights that despite the previous statement, something still occurs.

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーは甘いですが、それでも砂糖を加えます。
example_sentences.english: This coffee is sweet but nevertheless, I will add sugar.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降るよ、それでも釣りに行くの？
example_sentences.english: It's going to rain today, even with that, are you still going fishing?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は殴られたり、蹴られたりするのが嫌いです。それでも、空手が好きなので辞めれないです。
example_sentences.english: I don't like getting punched or kicked, even so, I like karate so it is hard to quit.

example_sentences.japanese: タバコは体に悪いと言われている。それでも、止めにくい。
example_sentences.english: It is said that smoking is bad for you and yet it is tough to quit.

example_sentences.japanese: 高いのに、それでも買うつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: It is expensive and yet you are still planning on buying it?

example_sentences.japanese: そのカップルがずっと喧嘩している。それでも、よく旅行に行く。
example_sentences.english: That couple is always fighting. Nevertheless they often go on trips together.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がインフルエンザにかかった。それでも、学校を休んでいない。
example_sentences.english: The teacher got the flu. Nevertheless he still came to school.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは毎日遅くまで働いているのに、それでも毎日ジムに行く。
example_sentences.english: My dad works late every day, but he still goes to the gym every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近太ってきたのに、それでも誰かがケーキを買ってくれたら食べる。
example_sentences.english: I have been gaining weight lately, and yet I will still eat cake if someone buys it for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪い天気だったのに、それでも子供が公園で遊んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The weather was bad, nevertheless the children played in the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒すぎてスキーウェアを着た。それでも、暖かくならなかった。
example_sentences.english: It was so cold that I wore my skiwear. But I could still not get warm.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は猫のアレルギーがある。それでも、彼女が猫を飼いたいって言っている。
example_sentences.english: I am allergic to cats. Nevertheless my girlfriend is talking about wanting to get a cat.

example_sentences.japanese: 虎を飼うことは出来ないといわれている。それでも飼おうとしている人が居ます。
example_sentences.english: It is said that you cannot keep a tiger as a pet. Nevertheless there are people who try.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近出た映画があまり面白くない。それでも有名な俳優が出ているから皆が見に行く。
example_sentences.english: A movie that was released recently isn't very interesting. Nevertheless everyone will go see it because it has a famous actor in it.

general_translation: Why don't you...?, What if you did...?
formation: Verb［たら］+ どう + だ？Verb［たら］+ どう + （か）？Verb［たら］ ？
casual_structure: Verb［たら］+ どう + だ？Verb［たら］+ どう + （か）？Verb［たら］ ？
polite_structure: Verb［たら］+ どう + です + か。
explanation: A casual, sometimes sarcastic way to suggest that someone do (A). When doing (A), how 'bout that?

example_sentences.japanese: 公園にあそびにいったらどうですか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you go to play in the park?

example_sentences.japanese: 苦いなら砂糖を入れたらどうか。
example_sentences.english: If it is bitter, why don't you add some sugar?

example_sentences.japanese: テレビがつかないの？叩いてみたらどう。
example_sentences.english: Your TV doesn't turn on? Why don't you try hitting it?

example_sentences.japanese: 暇なら外に行ったら？
example_sentences.english: If you are bored, why don't you go outside?

example_sentences.japanese: 警察に電話をしてみたらどうだ。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you try calling the police?

example_sentences.japanese: 食べる量を減らしたらどう？
example_sentences.english: Why don't you reduce the amount you eat?

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのゴミをひろったらどうですか。
example_sentences.english: Why don't you go pick up that garbage over there?

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットをしてみたらどう？
example_sentences.english: Why don't you try dieting?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに彼が好きだったら、つきあったらどう？
example_sentences.english: If you like him that much, why don't you go out with him?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に居て寂しいなら、アメリカにかえったらどう？
example_sentences.english: If you feel lonely in Japan, why don't you go back to America?

example_sentences.japanese: 用事がいっぱいあるから、今すぐしはじめたらどう？
example_sentences.english: Since you have so many things to do, why don't you start now?

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史が好きだったら、この大学にいったらどう？
example_sentences.english: If you like history, why don't you go to this university?

example_sentences.japanese: タイピングが遅いから、ちゃんとやり方をおぼえたらどう？
example_sentences.english: Since you are a slow typer, why don't you learn the proper way to do it?

example_sentences.japanese: 君と僕の友達が映画好きだから、一緒にみにいったらどう？
example_sentences.english: Your friends and my friends like movies, so why don't we go see a movie together.

example_sentences.japanese: 鍋の味がちょっと薄いから、お味噌をいれたらどう？
example_sentences.english: The nabe's flavor is a little weak. Why don't you add some miso? (nabe = kind of soup/stew cooked in a pot)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに暇だったら、アルバイトさがしたらどう？
example_sentences.english: If you are really that bored (have that much free time), why don't you look for a part-time job?

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと頭が痛いって言っているから、お医者さんにいったらどう？
example_sentences.english: You keep saying that your head hurts. Why don't you go to a doctor?

example_sentences.japanese: たまには頭を使ったらどう？
example_sentences.english: Why don't you use your head occasionally? (You should try thinking for once)

grammar_point: と考（かんが）えられている
general_translation: Is considered, Is thought of as
formation: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられているPhrase + と思（おも）われている
casual_structure: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられているPhrase + と思（おも）われている
polite_structure: Phrase + と考（かんが）えられていますPhrase + と思（おも）われています
explanation: A way of expressing that something is often thought of as (A), or considered as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: イルカはとても賢いとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Dolphins are considered to be very intelligent.

example_sentences.japanese: 「最初はグー」と最初に言ったのは、志村けんだとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Shimura Ken is considered to be the first person who said 'saisho wa gu'. (A phrase said before playing rock, paper, scissors, in Japan)

example_sentences.japanese: このトンネルは日本で一番呪われているトンネルだとおもわれている。
example_sentences.english: This tunnel is thought to be one of the most cursed tunnels in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: カバは世界で最も危ない動物だとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Everyone knows that hippos are the most dangerous animal in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: この街に海賊が住んでいたとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that pirates used to live in this town.

example_sentences.japanese: お金はどんな人にも悪い影響があるとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Money is considered to have a bad influence on anyone and everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: この建物は５００年頃建てられたとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: This building is thought to have been built around the year 500.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間でひらがなを覚えることができるとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: It is thought that you can memorize hiragana in one week.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵は人間が描いた絵の中で一番古いとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: This painting is considered to be the oldest ever painted by man.

example_sentences.japanese: 見つかった宝物は黒ひげが無くしたのだとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: The treasure that we discovered is thought to be the one that Black Beard lost.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で作られている車は環境にいいとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Cars made in Japan are considered to be good for the environment.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と一緒に居るだけで、幸せになるとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: Just being with a dog is considered enough to make you happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語はアメリカだけでなく、世界中で使われる言語だとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: English is considered a worldly language, not only used in America.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は最も難しい言語の一つとおもわれている。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is thought of as one of the most difficult languages.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は怖いと思わないが、サメが最も危ない動物だとかんがえられている。
example_sentences.english: I don't think (they) are scary, but sharks are considered to be extremely dangerous animals.

general_translation: To be considered, To be deemed, Be regarded as, Be accepted as, To be said, To be accredited with
formation: Verb + とされている［い］Adjective + とされている［な］Adjective + （だ） + とされているNoun + （だ） + とされている
casual_structure: Verb + とされている［い］Adjective + とされている［な］Adjective + （だ） + とされているNoun + （だ） + とされている
polite_structure: Verb + とされています［い］Adjective + とされています［な］Adjective + （だ） + とされていますNoun + （だ） + とされています
explanation: An expression highlighting that something is considered or accepted as (A). It presupposes that (A) is true.

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「ＷＰ４０は使用が多いとされている。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'WP 40 is (generally) considered to have many applications.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時代にはインターネットが必要だとされている。
example_sentences.english: In current times, the internet is widely considered to be necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: これはニコラテスラが発明したものだとされている。
example_sentences.english: This is considered to be something invented by Nikola Tesla.

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「ポーランド人には１３という数字は不吉な数字とされている。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'The number 13 is considered unlucky by the Polish.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「ジム・モリソンの正確な死因は不明とされているのである。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'The exact cause of Jim Morrison's death is (widely) regarded to be unknown.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「歴史的に平仮名は元は『女のもの』だとされていた。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'Historically, hiragana was originally (widely) considered 'a woman's thing.''

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「過度のアルコール飲料の摂取は多数の病気の原因になるとされている。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'It is (generally) accepted that excessive consumption of alcohol causes numerous diseases.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「外国人の間では、日本人は議論が苦手とされている。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'Foreigners (generally) consider Japanese as poor debaters.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「食糧不足が始まったのは、気候変動のためとされている。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'Climate change is (generally) considered as the cause of the beginning of the food shortage.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「この絵画はその技法の類似によりレンブラントの作とされている。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'This painting is (widely) considered to be work of Rembrandt due to the similarity in technique.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「皇帝ネロはローマに放火したとされているけれども、歴史的な証拠はない。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'It is (widely) accepted that emperor Nero set Rome on fire, however there is no historical evidence.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「甘味料はガンの原因にならないとされているが、更に研究が必要である。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'Sweeteners are deemed to not be the source of cancer, but more research is needed.'

example_sentences.japanese: 論説：「ジャズは以前は『悪魔の音楽』とされていたが、今は『アメリカのクラシック』と認識されている。」
example_sentences.english: Dissertation: 'In the past, jazz was considered to be "the music of the devil", but now it is recognized as "the classic music of America"'.

example_sentences.japanese: 語学学校のサイト：「外国語を学ぼうとする際に最も大切とされているのは毎日欠かさず学ぶこと、すなわち継続です。」
example_sentences.english: Language school website: 'When learning a foreign language the thing that is considered the most important is studying without missing a single day, that is - continuity.'

example_sentences.japanese: 水は氷となる。
example_sentences.english: Water becomes ice. (As a result of transformation, water will be ice)

example_sentences.japanese: 温度が０度になると、水は氷となる。
example_sentences.english: If the temperature is 0 degrees, it results in water becoming ice.

general_translation: It is said that, Is known as
formation: Phrase + といわれている
casual_structure: Phrase + といわれている
polite_structure: Phrase + といわれています
explanation: A grammar point that highlights a whole phrase as often being said, or as a common opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 危ないといわれているので、しないほうがいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Because it is said that it is dangerous, you shouldn't do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪のタコ焼きは日本一美味しいといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that Osaka's takoyaki is the most delicious in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: ティフアナは世界一危険な町といわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that Tijuana is the most dangerous city in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: ライオンがジャングルの王様だといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that the lion is the king of the jungle.

example_sentences.japanese: プロテインを食べると力がつくといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that if you eat protein, you will gain strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 見えないことは信じられないことだといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that seeing is believing. (Things that cannot be seen are unbelievable)

example_sentences.japanese: ひどいことをしたから、犯人といわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that he is a criminal because he did terrible things.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の家では幽霊が出るといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that ghosts appear in that person's house.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が力強いから、ゴリラマンといわれている。
example_sentences.english: He is known as Gorilla Man because he is strong.

example_sentences.japanese: スターウォーズは誰でも知っているといわれている映画だ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that Star Wars is a movie known by everyone. (By anyone)

example_sentences.japanese: この町はたくさん有名な食べ物があるといわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is said that this town has a lot of famous foods.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノを弾くのが上手といわれているけど、全然上手じゃない。
example_sentences.english: It is said that I am good at piano, but I am not good at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 鶏と野菜が健康にいいといわれているので、いっぱい食べてください。
example_sentences.english: It is said that chicken and vegetables are good for your health, so please eat plenty of them.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹は歌を上手に歌えるとよくいわれている。
example_sentences.english: It is often said that my little sister can sing songs well.

general_translation: Should have, I wish, It would have been better to
formation: Verb［ば］+ よかったExamples:食（た）べる ￫ 食（た）べれば + よかった飲（の）む ￫ 飲（の）めば + よかったする ￫ すれば + よかった
casual_structure: Verb［ば］+ よかったExamples:食（た）べる ￫ 食（た）べれば + よかった飲（の）む ￫ 飲（の）めば + よかったする ￫ すれば + よかった
polite_structure: Verb［ば］+ よかった + ですExamples:食（た）べる ￫ 食（た）べれば + よかった + です飲（の）む ￫ 飲（の）めば + よかった + ですする ￫ すれば + よかった + です
explanation: A grammar point that expresses a hypothetical outcome that would have been preferred.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の電車をまてばよかったです。
example_sentences.english: I should have waited for the next train.

example_sentences.japanese: サービスエリアが一つもないじゃないか。高速に乗る前にトイレに行けばよかった。
example_sentences.english: There aren't any service stops, are there? I wish I had gone to the bathroom before we got on the highway.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も残業？昨日は早く寝ればよかった。
example_sentences.english: I have to work overtime again today? I should have gone to sleep early last night.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームより勉強をすればよかったです。
example_sentences.english: It would have been better to study rather than play games.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報をみればよかったです。
example_sentences.english: I should have looked at the weather forecast.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーに行った時、牛乳をかえばよかった。
example_sentences.english: I should have bought milk while I was at the store.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝ないで、日本語を勉強すればよかった。
example_sentences.english: It would have been better to study Japanese rather than sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強することが大切ってもうちょっと早めにわかればよかった。
example_sentences.english: I wish that I understood how important studying was earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れてすみません。家をもっと早くでればよかったです。
example_sentences.english: I apologize for my tardiness. I should have left my home earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: またお金がなくなった。ＡＴＭにいけばよかった。
example_sentences.english: I'm out of money again. I should have gone to an ATM.

example_sentences.japanese: 杉本さんが持っている車みたいな車をかえばよかった。
example_sentences.english: I should have bought a car like the one that Sugimoto-san has.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫁さんがそんなカバンを欲しがるなら、かってあげればよかった。
example_sentences.english: If my wife wanted a bag like that, it would’ve been better if I had bought it for her.

example_sentences.japanese: この漢字の意味があまり分からないので、先生にきけばよかった。
example_sentences.english: I do not really understand the meaning of this kanji. I should have asked the teacher about it.

example_sentences.japanese: クリスマスにＮｉｎｔｅｎｄｏスイッチが欲しかったら、そういえばよかった。
example_sentences.english: If you wanted a Nintendo Switch for Christmas, you should have said so.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転をしたくなかったら、電車で行けばいい。
example_sentences.english: If you don't want to drive, it would be better if you went by train.
